# Changelog

All notable changes to VirtRigaud will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [2026-10-25 12:30] - Command-line tools fixed for v0.4.0 (GA)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Added
- `cmd/internal/cliclient/cliclient.go`: the client set-up the tools share: a scheme with the client-go types and the `infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1` types (built like `cmd/manager`'s), `--kubeconfig` resolution, and a controller-runtime client over that scheme.
- `cmd/internal/cliout/cliout.go`: writes the tools' command output (a failed write to the command's own output has nowhere to be reported).
- `cmd/internal/envtestutil/envtestutil.go`: starts a real kube-apiserver (envtest) with the CRDs from `config/crd/bases` for the tools' tests.
- `cmd/vrtg/main_test.go`, `cmd/vcts/main_test.go`, `cmd/virtrigaud-loadgen/main_test.go`, `cmd/vrtg-provider/main_test.go`, `internal/scaffold/scaffold_test.go`: tests that run the commands in-process against a real apiserver, `vcts validate`'s real exit status, and a `vrtg-provider init` project through `go build`, `go vet`, `go test` (resolved from the local module cache, no network), `generate`, `verify` and `publish` for every provider type.
- `docs/cli-tools.md`: reference for the four tools (commands, flags, the load-generator config format, what is not implemented), linked from `docs/README.md`.
- `vrtg`, `vcts`, `virtrigaud-loadgen`, `vrtg-provider`: `--version` reports the release set with `-ldflags "-X main.version=..."` (the release workflow already passed it; no tool had the variable).
- `vrtg-provider init --virtrigaud-path <checkout>`: the VirtRigaud checkout the generated `go.mod` resolves the SDK and proto modules from; detected when the project is created inside a checkout.

### Fixed
- `cmd/vrtg/main.go`, `cmd/vcts/main.go`, `cmd/virtrigaud-loadgen/main.go`: `vrtg` (every command except `vm events`), `vcts run` and `virtrigaud-loadgen` failed with `no kind is registered for the type v1beta1...` because the client was built with `client.Options{}` (empty scheme). They now use a scheme with the VirtRigaud types.
- `cmd/vrtg/main.go`: `--kubeconfig` is honoured (it was ignored, the flag set was never read); the `list` commands honour `-n` and show a `NAMESPACE` column (they listed every namespace and hid which); `-o json` and `-o yaml` print the resources with `apiVersion` and `kind` (they printed "not implemented"); a `VirtualMachine` without `spec.imageRef` no longer panics `vm list` and `vm describe`; `provider status` prints `status.healthy` instead of a fixed "Status: Available"; the subcommands with no implementation exit non-zero and name what to use instead of printing a notice and exiting 0; tables are aligned.
- `cmd/vcts/main.go`: `vcts validate` exits non-zero when a specification file is invalid (an invalid file was skipped, counted as neither valid nor invalid, and the command exited 0, so the CI step that validates `test/conformance/specs` could not fail); `--kubeconfig` is honoured.
- `cmd/virtrigaud-loadgen/main.go`: `--config` is honoured (it printed "not implemented"): a strict YAML file overrides the defaults and an unknown key or unusable value is an error; `delete` removes only VMs that run created (it deleted a random VM from the whole namespace); VM names carry a run id so a second run does not fail with `AlreadyExists`; an operation in flight when the duration ends is not reported as failed; the summary no longer divides by zero and its table header is complete; `--kubeconfig` is honoured.
- `cmd/vrtg-provider/generate.go`: `checkProviderProject` compared the whole `go.mod` to one string, so `generate`, `verify` and `publish` always failed with "not in a provider project directory"; it now checks that `go.mod` requires a `github.com/projectbeskar/virtrigaud` module. `generate` no longer fails on a project that has no proto sources, and `--clean` removes the `*.pb.go` files under `internal/rpc` (it only printed "Would remove").
- `internal/scaffold/scaffold.go`: the scaffold did not compile: it imported the repository's `internal/version` package (not importable from another module), an unused `fmt`, and required a `github.com/projectbeskar/virtrigaud` v0.1.0 that has no `sdk` or `proto` packages. The generated `go.mod` now requires the sdk and proto modules and resolves them from a checkout; the version is a `main.version` set with `-ldflags`; the server stops on SIGINT/SIGTERM; the Go files are `gofmt`-clean; the README no longer claims flags and features the scaffold does not have and renders its code fences.
- `cmd/vrtg-provider/verify.go`, `cmd/vrtg-provider/publish.go`: `verify` ran `vcts version` and `vcts run --profile`, which do not exist, and then printed "Conformance profile verified"; it now runs the build, checks and unit tests, falls back to `go build`/`go test` only when the Makefile has no such target (it also fell back when `make build` failed), and says that conformance was not run. `publish` wrote hard-coded passing conformance results to the catalog; it now builds and tests the project and records conformance as `skip` (not run) with a "not run" badge.

### Security
- `cmd/vrtg-provider/generate.go`: `generate --clean` walks and removes the generated `*.pb.go` files through an `os.Root` opened on `internal/rpc`, so a symbolic link in the tree cannot make it remove a file outside that directory.
- `cmd/vcts/main.go`, `cmd/virtrigaud-loadgen/main.go`: the report output directory is created with mode 0750 (was 0755).
- `cmd/virtrigaud-loadgen/main.go`: the non-cryptographic random choices (next operation, provider, which created VM to delete) are marked as such for gosec.
- `cmd/vrtg-provider/main_test.go`: a test that `generate --clean` removes only the generated bindings and does not follow a symbolic link out of `internal/rpc`.

### Why
The command-line tools shipped in v0.4.0 release candidates could not do what they document: they failed on every VirtRigaud resource, `vcts validate` could not fail CI, and `vrtg-provider` rejected and could not build its own scaffold. v0.4.0 GA must ship the operator code that v0.4.0-rc9 validated, so this changes only `cmd/vrtg`, `cmd/vcts`, `cmd/virtrigaud-loadgen`, `cmd/vrtg-provider`, `cmd/internal` and `internal/scaffold`. `go list -deps` shows that no operator binary (`cmd/manager`, `cmd/provider-*`) depends on a changed package, so the manager and provider images are unchanged.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-25 12:00] - v0.4.0 GA: examples, docs and scripts aligned with the code
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Changed
- `examples/**`: Provider image pins moved to `v0.4.0`; every Provider example now sets `spec.runtime.service.tls` (a Provider without it is not deployed); libvirt examples use `qemu+ssh://` endpoints and Secrets with `known_hosts`; Proxmox, vSphere and libvirt credential examples list only keys the providers read; migration, reconfigure, snapshot, console, hostpool and graceful-shutdown comments corrected; the clustered-migration examples no longer say vSphere and Proxmox sources were not run; `examples/README.md` and `examples/advanced/README.md` rewritten for v0.4.0.
- `examples/security/*`: NetworkPolicies use the real provider pod labels and ports.
- `docs/*.md`, `docs/adr/*`: "this/next release" wording replaced by explicit versions; clustered capability, placement, installed-CRD-check, restore and seed-directory statements corrected; `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md` no longer says a bound VM is re-placed when its host is cordoned or `NotReady` (the scheduler runs only for a VM's first create), gives the Spread and BinPack tie-break order the scheduler uses, says that only `HostPool.spec.strategy` and `spec.overcommit` reach it and that `VMPlacementPolicy` `priority`, `weight` and status are not used, and lists the clustered-migration sources that were run; `docs/vm-snapshot-revert.md` points to the lab validation; `Host.spec.endpoint` is written `qemu+ssh://` throughout; docs and ADR indexes updated.
- `docs/release-notes/next.md`: links are relative to `docs/release-notes/`, so they resolve in GitHub's file view.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `ca-certs/README.md`, `internal/storage/README.md`: removed nonexistent make targets and paths; the storage README describes the pvc and s3 backends.
- `Makefile`: `providers-version` lists the Proxmox and mock providers.
- `hack/dev-watch.sh`, `hack/test-lint-locally.sh`, `hack/test-ci-locally.sh`, `hack/test-workflows-locally.sh`: use `make lint` and the Go and golangci-lint versions CI uses.
- `charts/virtrigaud-provider-runtime/`: image pins moved to `v0.4.0`.
- `charts/virtrigaud/templates/manager-rbac.yaml`: the comment above the CRD `get` rule says five CRDs (it listed five under "Four"); the rendered manifests are unchanged apart from that comment.

### Removed
- `examples/security/proxmox-rbac.yaml`: the provider pods run under a controller-created ServiceAccount and need no RBAC; the file also carried a PodSecurityPolicy.
- `spec.lifecycle` blocks from examples: no controller reads `preStop`, `postStart` or `gracefulShutdownTimeout`.

### Why
The examples and docs described behaviour of v0.3.x or earlier (missing TLS block, plaintext and env-var provider setup, hooks that never run, a scheduler that moves bound VMs), which made the shipped examples fail or mislead. The code is the reference.

### Impact

- [ ] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [x] Documentation only

## [2026-10-25 08:00] - Release documentation for v0.4.0 (GA)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Changed
- `docs/release-notes/next.md`: retitled for v0.4.0 (GA), which ships the code of v0.4.0-rc9. The release-candidate material is folded in: every "Changes since v0.4.0-rcN" section and "About this release candidate" are gone; their user-visible content now lives in "Breaking changes" (one list of actions and one of behaviour changes, no "New since rcN" groups), "Highlights" (new subsections "Snapshots and revert", "Proxmox" and "Addresses, phase and conditions"; the clustered section gains the migration-into-a-clustered-Provider requirements, the host-loss answers and `HostPool.status`; "Security" gains the seed directory and the `VMClone` identity and read-access notes), "Fixes" (one flat list), "Known limitations" and "Upgrade". A new "Validation" section consolidates the lab runs of all nine candidates and lists what was not validated, including the rc9 run (a disk-only snapshot, then a memory snapshot, then the refused and the accepted delete order). "Upgrade" gets one subsection, "Upgrading from a v0.4.0 release candidate", with what each candidate still needs (the per-rc "Upgrade order" sections are gone). The header comment says the file is over GitHub's 125,000-character limit and the published body drops "Fixes".
- `docs/upgrading.md`: opens for v0.3.11 to v0.4.0 and loses the rc wording in the breaking-change and behaviour-change rows (rc1 and rc2 now read v0.3.11 or "this release"); the three per-rc roll-order bullets are one bullet; new section "Upgrading from a v0.4.0 release candidate" with the per-candidate table; "Rollback caveats" gains the manager and libvirt-provider caveats of the candidates (rc5 to rc9) that lived only in the old per-rc upgrade sections.
- `README.md`, `charts/virtrigaud/README.md`: version references go to v0.4.0 (header, `helm install` and `helm upgrade --version`, provider image tags, the Argo CD and Flux examples of the chart README, "Since v0.3.11" no longer says "not yet released"); the `virtrigaud_queue_depth` deprecation no longer says it is removed in v0.4.0, because it is still exposed.
- `docs/libvirt-clones.md`, `docs/vm-snapshot-revert.md`: wording correction for the memory-snapshot delete (see Why).

### Added
- `docs/release-notes/next.md` (Known limitations): V12. On libvirt, a new disk-only snapshot whose name matches an earlier snapshot's leftover overlay file (`<pool>/<domain>-disk.<name>`) fails in libvirt with "external snapshot file for disk vda already exists"; a clustered provider answers it with a generic error, so the `VMSnapshot` never gets a phase and the create is re-sent about once a minute. Workaround: a new snapshot name, or remove the leftover file after verifying that nothing references it. A definite refusal is planned for a later release.

### Fixed
- Documentation correction for V11 (the old entries above are history and are not rewritten): on libvirt 10.0, deleting an external snapshot block-commits its overlay into the base but does not delete the overlay file. On v0.3.11 and v0.4.0-rc8 or earlier a memory snapshot stored in that overlay was therefore orphaned (its data stayed in the leftover file, unusable) rather than destroyed, and VirtRigaud's overlay cleanup kept the file because the memory snapshot's metadata still referenced it; when nothing references the merged overlay the cleanup removes it. The wording in the release notes, `docs/libvirt-clones.md` (the section "A memory snapshot that was already orphaned" replaces "...whose data was already lost"), `docs/vm-snapshot-revert.md` and `docs/upgrading.md` now says orphaned and unusable. The provider's refusal text still says "would be lost"; no code changed.

### Why
v0.4.0 GA ships the code of v0.4.0-rc9, so this is the documentation the release needs: notes that read cold for someone coming from v0.3.11 instead of as a candidate-by-candidate history, one place for the actions a release-candidate user still has to take, version references that point at the release, and the lab's V11 correction and V12 finding.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [x] Documentation only

## [2026-10-24 23:30] - libvirt: deleting a disk-only snapshot no longer destroys a memory snapshot stored in its overlay (V11)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/snapshot_delete_guard.go`, `server.go`: libvirt (>= 9.0, checked against v10.0.0 `qemu_snapshot.c`) deletes an external snapshot by block-committing the file it merges away (the first child's recorded disk source, or the domain's current one) into its backing file with `VIR_DOMAIN_BLOCK_COMMIT_DELETE`; it refuses an internal *parent* but not an internal snapshot stored *in* that file, and updates only external snapshots' recorded sources. A memory snapshot taken on a disk-only snapshot's overlay was therefore destroyed by the disk-only snapshot's delete, success was reported, and the memory snapshot's metadata could never be deleted while the VM ran (V11, v0.4.0-rc8 lab). `SnapshotDelete` (single-host and routed/owner-checked, gRPC server and `contracts.Provider` paths, one core `snapshotDeleteOn`) now reads the snapshot strictly and, for an external snapshot, refuses (`snapshotDeleteLosesSnapshotsError`: `FailedPrecondition`, plus `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` when routed; nothing sent) while any other snapshot is stored in a file the delete may merge away or remove — the snapshot's `<disks>`/`<revertDisks>` overlays, its children's recorded sources and its own recorded source — by libvirt's metadata (another snapshot's internal disk recorded on such a file) or by the file's header (`qemu-img info -U -f qcow2 --output=json`, the existing `VR_DISK_READ` root read; a missing file holds nothing). The message names the blocking snapshots only (up to three, guidance first within the 256-byte status budget). A check that cannot be completed (snapshot, list or header unreadable, an external overlay that is not a file) refuses retryably (`diskCheckFailedError`, `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED`, new `check` wording; host unreachable stays a host failure).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/snapshot_delete_guard.go`: when libvirt refuses to delete an internal snapshot with "is not the same as disk image currently used by VM" (validated before anything changes), the provider deletes only its metadata (`virsh snapshot-delete <domain> <snapshot> --metadata`) if it proves the data is gone — every file the snapshot recorded for its internal disks no longer exists, and no image of the domain's current disk chains lists the name — and otherwise answers a definite `snapshotDeleteStaleInternalError` ("power the VM off and delete it again"), or a retryable check failure.
- `internal/controller/vmsnapshot_controller.go`: a `SnapshotDelete` answered with `FailedPrecondition` other than `VM_DISK_IN_USE` (the V11 refusal; also a vSphere image-artifact or an owner-stamp refusal) keeps the finalizer with `Ready=False`/`Deleting=False` reason `DeleteBlocked` and the provider's sanitized, capped answer in the status (`retainForRefusedSnapshotDelete`), a `SnapshotDeleteFailed` Warning when it changes, and re-checks with the failed-delete backoff (15 s up to 5 min). Before, it was `ProviderError` with a constant message and the answer only in the event.

### Changed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`, `snapshot_overlay_cleanup.go`: a snapshot whose definition cannot be read is no longer deleted without its overlay cleanup; the delete is refused retryably. `snapshotOverlaysOf` is replaced by `snapshotOverlaysIn` (parses the XML read once).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/imagepath.go`: `qemuImgInfo` decodes the image's internal `snapshots`; a walked chain level records them.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routing.go`: routed answers for the two new refusals (`FailedPrecondition` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`).
- `docs/libvirt-clones.md`: new "Deleting memory and disk-only snapshots of the same VM" (the refusal, the delete order, what is checked, fail-closed answers, force-delete) and "A memory snapshot whose data was already lost" (the provable metadata-only delete and the manual cleanup: `snapshot-dumpxml`, `qemu-img snapshot -l -U` of each recorded file, `qemu-img info -U --backing-chain` of the current disks, then `virsh snapshot-delete --metadata`). `docs/vm-snapshot-revert.md`: pointer in the libvirt section. `docs/upgrading.md`: behaviour-change row and provider-order bullet for rc9. `docs/release-notes/next.md`: "Changes since v0.4.0-rc8".

### Added
- `internal/providers/libvirt/snapshot_delete_guard_test.go` (and the opt-in V11 model in `snapshot_readonly_disks_test.go`'s in-memory host: image files, backing files, internal snapshots stored in files, the snapshot tree, libvirt 10's external delete commit and its stale-internal refusal): the model reproduces the lab; the lab sequence (refused, then memory snapshot first, then disk-only); only external descendants (allowed) and a memory snapshot in a later overlay (blocks only the snapshot whose overlay holds it); a header-only internal snapshot; fail-closed checks; the orphaned memory snapshot (metadata-only when proven; definite refusal when its file exists or the current chain lists it; retryable when the proof cannot run); single-host, `contracts.Provider` and routed wire forms; the 256-byte message budget. `internal/controller/vmsnapshot_delete_refused_test.go`: a refused delete keeps the finalizer, shows the answer, backs off, writes nothing new on a re-check, and is released by success or force-delete.
- Test fixtures: the createHost fake's default external snapshot records its overlay file; the seam fake answers `qemu-img info`; the snapshot fake can refuse `snapshot-delete` with a scripted stderr. The single-host command-sequence golden is unchanged (a snapshot with no external disk sends the same commands).

### Why
Validating v0.4.0-rc8 on libvirt 10.0: deleting a disk-only snapshot silently destroyed a memory snapshot of the same VM and left a `VMSnapshot` that could never be deleted. Maintainer decision: fail closed, small, for rc9.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-24 18:00] - libvirt snapshot overlays no longer block other VMs' disk checks; a routed snapshot create that was not performed is retried with a backoff, not held (V7, V8)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/imagepath.go`: the disk in-use scan (`domainRefsOnHostBounded`) walked every `<source>` nested in a shut-off domain's `<backingStore>` again with no format, so it was probed as the SSH user only (`qemu-img info -U --output=json -- <file>`, no sudo, by design: a probed header may be a guest's forgery). libvirt keeps such nested backing stores after an offline external snapshot or a revert, and the overlays it creates are `0600`: the read failed with "Permission denied" and every guarded operation (snapshot create/revert/delete, delete; clustered create/clone) of every OTHER VM on the host was answered "not performed ... (transient host error)" for ever (V7, v0.4.0-rc7 lab). Top-level disks are now walked first; a nested source a walk already read as a level of its chain is not walked again (its sub-chain is taken from that walk); one no walk reached is still probed as the SSH user and fails closed. No read runs as root that did not before.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/imagepath.go`, `disk_dependents.go`, `cluster_disk_guard.go`: a chain read that `qemu-img` answers "Permission denied" is an `unreadableImageError`; the single-host guard (`diskCheckFailedError`) and the cluster-wide guard (`clusterGuardIncompleteError`) then answer "... not performed: permission denied reading a disk image on its host / on a host of this Provider (see docs/libvirt-clones.md#unreadable-disk-images; the provider log names it) ...; retried" instead of the generic transient host error, and log the file and the fix. The answer names no image, host or other domain, and stays `Unavailable` + `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED` (fail-closed, retried, out of the circuit breaker).
- `internal/controller/vmsnapshot_controller.go`, `vmsnapshot_request_marker.go`: a routed `SnapshotCreate` answered with a definite "not performed" (`contracts.IsNothingDone` and not `IsOutcomeUnknownRetry`: `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED`, `HOST_UNAVAILABLE`, `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` not performed, request not sent) kept its `SnapshotRequested` marker, so each retry counted as a re-send of an unknown outcome and after ten the `VMSnapshot` was held `Ready=False/SnapshotOutcomeUnknown` for an operator annotation (V8). It now closes the attempt (`routedCreateNotPerformed`: the marker is removed), sets `Ready=False/ProviderError` with `snapshotCreateNotPerformedMessage`, and is sent again as a new attempt with the same request token after an exponential backoff per VMSnapshot UID (`notPerformedBackoff`, reusing `unschedulableBackoff`: 1 minute doubling up to `snapshotNotPerformedRetryMax`, 10 minutes; a reconcile before the wait has passed sends nothing; any other answer resets it; in memory). Unknown outcomes keep the marker, the re-send cap and the hold.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_snapshot_revert.go`: a revert the provider answers with `FailedPrecondition` (other than `VM_DISK_IN_USE`) no longer ends its `RevertFailed` message with "remove spec.snapshot.revertToRef and set it again to retry" (`snapshotRevertFailureHint`): the same revert is refused every time, and the provider's message says what to do (libvirt: take a new snapshot with the VM powered off).

### Removed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/overlay_perms.go` and the normalisation of a VM's own snapshot overlays after a snapshot or revert (`sudo -n chown -h` / `sudo -n chmod g+r`), with its `VR_OVERLAY_MODE` sudo rule, before release (revert of 414c5ef0, security review of #437): the rule's `[^/ ]+` also matches `.`, `..` and symbolic links and a root `chmod` follows links; the stat-then-chown/chmod sequence races in sticky directories; the on-by-default sudo attempts add policy-violation noise to auth.log; and it widened kvm-group read of live guest data. The single-host snapshot command-sequence golden is back to its rc7 sequences.

### Changed
- `docs/libvirt-clones.md`: new "Unreadable disk images" troubleshooting section (symptom, cause: libvirt's `0600` snapshot and revert overlays; fix: grant the existing `VR_DISK_READ` rule over the pool directory; an NFS pool export that does not squash root must be dedicated to the Provider's hosts; the manual `chown -h` / `chmod 0640` repair as an alternative); nested backing stores in "How the dependency is found"; snapshot overlays under "Clone files on the host". `docs/vm-snapshot-revert.md`: overlay permissions; the retry hint is not appended to a `FailedPrecondition` refusal. `docs/provider-call-outcomes.md`: a routed `VMSnapshot` create answered "not performed" closes its attempt and backs off. `docs/release-notes/next.md`: "Changes since v0.4.0-rc7".

### Added
- `internal/providers/libvirt/overlay_perms_test.go`: the lab's nested-chain scan no longer probes the root-only overlay (fails on the previous code), an uncovered nested source is still probed and fails closed, the single-host, routed and cluster-wide guard answers for an unreadable image (wire-safe, retryable, `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED`).
- `internal/controller/vmsnapshot_request_marker_test.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/client_definite_outcome_test.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_snapshot_revert_test.go`: a routed create answered not performed is retried as a new attempt past the re-send cap and never held; its backoff grows 1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 10 minutes, paces reconciles in between and is reset by any other answer; unknown outcomes keep the marker and the hold; the transport's mapping of the routed answers; the revert hint only where a retry can help.

### Why
Validating v0.4.0-rc7 on real libvirt 10.0 hosts (AppArmor, a shared NFS pool used by a single-host and a clustered Provider): with rc7's advice to snapshot powered-off VMs, every offline snapshot and every revert left a `0600` overlay that made every other VM's snapshot, revert and delete on the host fail for good, and the resulting "not performed" answers exhausted a `VMSnapshot` into an operator hold.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change

- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-24 17:30] - A NAT guest without the guest agent shows its DHCP lease in status.ips (V10)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/virsh.go`: `getDomainIPAddresses` kept only the rows of `virsh domifaddr` whose interface name started with `e`. That fits the agent source (guest interface names) but the `lease` and `arp` sources name rows after the NIC's host-side device (`vnetN`), so every lease and ARP row was dropped and a guest on libvirt's NAT `default` network without the QEMU guest agent had an empty `status.ips` while libvirt held its lease. The parsing is now `parseDomifaddr`: every row counts, the prefix length (`/24`, `/0` for `arp`) is removed, and `contracts.RoutableIPs` decides by address (V9 rules) instead of the interface name. The order of the sources (agent, lease, arp) and first-source-wins are unchanged. Also fixed: the second address of a NIC, printed by virsh on a row whose name is `-`, was skipped, so a multi-address NIC lost addresses.

### Changed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/virsh.go`: the interface-name filter is gone for the agent source too (`br0`, `docker0` in the guest are no longer dropped by name); the address rules apply. Behaviour change: the `arp` source now yields addresses, so a guest on a host bridge without the agent shows one if the host has an ARP entry for its MAC (before, such rows were dropped).
- `docs/vm-status-ips.md`, `docs/upgrading.md`, `docs/release-notes/next.md` ("V10"): NAT shows the lease without the agent, a host bridge has no lease so the agent is needed, the ARP last resort.

### Tests
- `internal/providers/libvirt/virsh_domifaddr_test.go`: `parseDomifaddr` on the real libvirt 10.0 output shapes (empty agent output, a `vnetN` lease row with `/24`, an `arp` row with `/0`, an agent answer with `lo` and `eth0`, two NICs with a continuation row, N/A and repeated rows), and `getDomainIPAddresses` against a stub `virsh` on `PATH`: NAT guest without the agent, a failing agent, agent first-wins, loopback-only agent falling through, multi-NIC lease, arp last resort, and the order of the sources asked.

### Why
V10, pre-existing: found while checking V9 in the lab, a NAT guest without the guest agent never showed an address although `virsh domifaddr --source lease` listed it.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

Roll the libvirt provider.

## [2026-10-24 16:30] - `status.ips` lists only addresses a user can reach the VM on (V9)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Changed
- `internal/providers/contracts/routable_ips.go`: new `RoutableIPs`, the one normaliser for VM addresses. Entries are parsed with `net/netip`; loopback, unspecified, IPv4 and IPv6 link-local and multicast addresses and entries that do not parse (including `addr/prefix`) are dropped; an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address becomes the IPv4 address, an IPv6 zone is removed, duplicates (also differently spelled IPv6) are dropped, the provider's order is kept. Private, IPv6 unique-local and global addresses stay. The result is `nil` when nothing is left.

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`: `describeOn` appended every address the guest agent reported for every guest interface, loopback and IPv6 link-local included, so `status.ips` read `["127.0.0.1","::1","192.0.2.31","fe80::..."]` and `primary_ip` in `status.provider` could be `127.0.0.1`. The agent's addresses go through `contracts.RoutableIPs` first; an agent that reports only unreachable addresses falls back to the `virsh domifaddr` list.

### Tests
- `internal/providers/contracts/routable_ips_test.go`: table test of every rule (IPv4 and IPv6 loopback, unspecified, link-local with and without a zone, multicast, boundary addresses just outside each range, private, ULA, global), de-duplication and IPv6 spellings, IPv4-mapped addresses, order, whitespace, garbage, and that the input is not modified.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_status_ips_test.go`: `reconcileVM` writes `status.ips` normalised for a provider answer with loopback and link-local addresses, rewrites a status that already holds them, and leaves it empty when nothing is reachable; a VM with only unreachable addresses is still "waiting for an IP" in `getRequeueInterval`.

### Why
Rc7 lab validation (V9): `status.ips` of a libvirt VM with the guest agent listed loopback and link-local addresses. The field is for reaching the VM, and every provider should answer the same way, so the filter is applied once in the manager rather than per provider.

## [2026-10-24 12:00] - A clustered call waiting for another call's SSH dial is answered in time (V3c follow-up)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/host_answer.go`, `sshclient.go`, `virsh.go`: on a clustered libvirt provider, a call that arrived while another call was dialing an unreachable host waited for that dial without regard to its own deadline, and was answered `codes.Unknown` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` ("failed to describe VM on host ...", 1m28s with a 30 s deadline; a held delete took 1m55s) in the rc6 lab. Cause: `ensureSSHClient` held `sshMu` across the whole `dialSSH`, and a waiter's `sshMu.Lock()` honoured no context, so a `Describe` queued behind a call with a longer deadline (a `Delete`, a detached cleanup) or none. On a clustered host connection (`boundHostWaits`) the dial is now a single flight (`ensureClusteredSSHClient`, `sshDial`): `sshMu` only guards the cached client and the flight and is never held across network I/O; a waiter waits for the flight's end or its own `hostWaitContext` bound and a wait that ends on the bound is a `hostNotAnsweringError` (HOST_UNAVAILABLE for a read, by how far the call got otherwise), never the call's context error. A dial that failed for its own reason is the answer of the calls that waited for it; a dial that ended on its caller's time makes the waiters dial again. No goroutine is added.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/sshclient.go`: the TCP connect of a clustered dial is capped at `sshHandshakeTimeout` (a call without a deadline waited for the TCP stack, minutes), and a call cancelled during the SSH handshake expires the socket's deadline (`context.AfterFunc`) instead of waiting for it. The single-host provider is unchanged (it still dials under `sshMu`).
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_clustered.go`: `deleteBlockedEscape` starts with "To release ..." — every `DeleteBlocked` message appended it after a period, so the sentence began in lower case ("... completes once the host answers. to release ..."). Only the capitalisation changed.

### Added
- `internal/providers/libvirt/host_answer_dial_test.go`: callers arriving while a long-deadline call dials a host that never completes the handshake, and staggered concurrent callers to such a host, are all answered `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` before their 3 s deadline (the first fails on the previous code with 15 s); callers share one successful dial; a refused dial is the answer of the calls that waited for it; the single-host dial is unchanged.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_delete_host_hold_test.go`: the escape-hatch sentence of every `DeleteBlocked` message starts a new sentence.

### Changed
- `docs/provider-call-outcomes.md`, `docs/release-notes/next.md`: describe what rc6 left unbounded and what is bounded now ("Changes since v0.4.0-rc6").

### Why
The rc6 lab validation showed that bounding the waits a call runs itself (#432) was not enough: a wait for a lock another call held across a dial still lasted as long as that call's deadline, and ended as a failure of the operation.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-24 10:05] - libvirt: snapshot revert no longer breaks the cloud-init CD-ROM (V6)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/snapshot_media.go`, `server.go`, `provider_virsh.go`, `domain_disks.go`: libvirt (>= 9.9) reverts an external snapshot by rebuilding the domain's disks from the definition the snapshot stored and making a new qcow2 overlay, `<file without extension>.<epoch>`, of every disk there that has media — the read-only cloud-init seed CD-ROM included, whatever its snapshot mode (libvirt records it `snapshot='no'` by itself; `--diskspec` does not help). The CD-ROM became a root-owned overlay in the VM's private seed directory that AppArmor's `virt-aa-helper` profile does not let QEMU open: the revert answered success and the VM no longer started, on single-host and clustered Providers (V6, found validating v0.4.0-rc6 on libvirt 10 hosts). A disk-only `SnapshotCreate` of a shut-off domain (gRPC and `contracts.Provider`, which now share the core) records its file-backed CD-ROMs/floppies in the domain's metadata (namespace `https://virtrigaud.io/xmlns/libvirt/media/v1`), ejects them (`change-media <d> <t> --eject --config`), takes the snapshot, inserts each file again (`change-media <d> <t> <file> --insert --config`, also after a failed snapshot), checks each is back with its driver type, and removes the record. A running domain is never ejected; read-only disks or drives that keep a source (running, memory, non-file media, read-only data disks) are excluded with `--diskspec <target>,snapshot=no`. Failures: a definite eject failure puts back what was ejected (not performed); an eject or re-insert whose outcome is unknown, or a failed create with the media still out, is never answered "not performed"; a snapshot made whose media could not be re-inserted is answered as made, with the record kept.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/snapshot_media.go`, `server.go`, `provider_virsh.go`: an interrupted ejection is repaired by the next `SnapshotCreate` (routed: before an earlier attempt's snapshot is adopted), `SnapshotRevert`, and power on/reboot of the domain (`restoreEjectedMedia`): a recorded file is inserted again into its still-empty drive only when it is provably the domain's own cloud-init seed (`isOwnSeedISO`: `cloud-init.iso` in `<seed root>/virtrigaud-cloudinit-<domain>.<random>` or an earlier release's `<seed root>/virtrigaud-cloudinit/<domain>`); anything else is logged and left with its record. A start whose seed cannot be re-inserted is not attempted.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/snapshot_readonly_disks.go`, `routing.go`: `SnapshotRevert` refuses, before the revert changes anything (only the ejection repair may run first), an external snapshot whose stored definition has a CD-ROM, floppy or read-only disk with a source, and a snapshot whose disk lists record one as external (`snapshotRevertGate`, `snapshotRevertUnsafeError`: `FailedPrecondition`; routed, + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`) — every rc6-and-earlier snapshot of a VM with cloud-init (as created, and after libvirt rewrote its metadata on a revert) and every disk-only snapshot of such a VM taken while it ran; the manager ends the request `SnapshotReverted=False/RevertFailed`, terminal. Internal (memory) snapshots are not refused for their media. An unreadable snapshot or domain definition, or an external snapshot without a stored definition, means no revert. After a revert the media the domain had before it are inserted again into the drives the revert left empty (recorded first; `--live` too when the VM runs); a medium that cannot be (`snapshotRevertMediaError`) or a read-only disk on a new file (`snapshotRevertBrokeDisksError`) is answered `FailedPrecondition` instead of success. Messages name only the snapshot and disk targets and put the guidance first, so the manager's 256-byte status detail keeps it even for a long snapshot name.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/snapshot_overlay_cleanup.go`: the `SnapshotDelete` overlay cleanup also recognises the overlay a revert made, `<domain>-disk.<epoch>`, which libvirt records as the snapshot's (and reads `<revertDisks>`), under the existing checks (out of the domain's chains, no other snapshot references it, a regular file in the pool, no other domain on any host uses it).

### Changed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/testdata/single_host_snapshot_clone_disk.golden.json`, `single_host_power_reconfigure.golden.json`: regenerated: single-host `SnapshotCreate` of a shut-off VM gains the media read, record, eject, re-insert, check and record removal around `snapshot-create-as`; `SnapshotRevert` gains the domain and snapshot reads before and a domain read after the revert; power on and reboot gain a `dumpxml` before the start.
- `docs/vm-snapshot-revert.md`: libvirt section (how libvirt reverts, the ejection, running VMs, the refusal, the re-insert, the repair of an interrupted ejection) and a runbook to repair a VM broken by a v0.4.0-rc6 revert; upgrade note. `docs/libvirt-clones.md`: the `<domain>-disk.<epoch>` overlay. `docs/release-notes/next.md`: "Changes since v0.4.0-rc6" (V6).

### Added
- `internal/providers/libvirt/snapshot_readonly_disks_test.go`: an in-memory libvirt host modelling `change-media`, the media record, stored definitions and libvirt's external revert: eject/insert order around the snapshot; running and memory snapshots never eject; definite and unknown eject failures; a failed create still re-inserts; a re-insert failure repaired by the next call; the repair inserts only the domain's own seed; the revert gate on the real shapes (rc6 as created, rc6 after a revert, this release's, internal memory, no stored definition); a new-style revert puts the seed back (and `--live` for a running revert); re-insert failure after a revert; repair before a revert; single-host and clustered wire forms; power-on re-inserts an ejected seed before the start, and does not start when it cannot; message budget; `<domain>-disk.<epoch>` cleanup and VM delete of a reverted chain. Test fakes answer `snapshot-dumpxml`, `metadata`, `change-media` and `start`.

### Why
Every revert of a disk-only snapshot of a libvirt VM with cloud-init, on libvirt 9.9 or later with AppArmor, left the VM unable to start while the revert reported success; lab probes showed that only a snapshot whose stored definition has an empty CD-ROM reverts cleanly. Maintainer decision: fix for rc7.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-24 00:55] - Honest VirtualMachine status: unreachable hosts, restore holds, unattached spec.disks (V3, V4)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/host_answer.go`, `sshclient.go`, `virsh.go`, `routing.go`, `cluster_dialer.go`: on a clustered libvirt provider a call to a host that stopped answering could end `codes.Unknown` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` ("failed to describe VM on host ...") after 30 s instead of `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` (V3c). The SSH session open waited on the dead connection without regard to the call's context (`withSession`, `client.NewSession`), the calls stuck there held the host's command slots, and later calls waited for a slot until their own deadline; the context error was not a host failure (`isHostTransportFailure`), so `hostOpRPCErrorFor` answered it as a failure of the operation. On a clustered provider's host connections (`VirshProvider.boundHostWaits`) the command-slot wait, the SSH dial and handshake (the handshake was unbounded: `ssh.ClientConfig.Timeout` covers only `ssh.Dial`) and the session open now end 5 s before the call's deadline (at most a quarter of the time left) with `hostNotAnsweringError`, a host failure that ran nothing, classified by R25 as before (`Describe`: always `HOST_UNAVAILABLE`), and answered before the manager gives up; it is not retried as a transient SSH error. The single-host provider is unchanged.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routing.go`, `internal/providers/contracts/host_unavailable.go`: a `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` about the host the call was routed to (its lease failed, or it stopped answering) carries the host id in its `ErrorInfo` metadata under `host` (`contracts.HostUnavailableHostKey`, read with `contracts.UnreachableHost`). The cluster-wide disk guard's answer, which may concern another host, carries none.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_delete_host_hold.go`, `virtualmachine_clustered.go`, `virtualmachine_controller.go`, `internal/k8s/conditions.go`: a clustered delete held because the VM's own host does not answer (V3a) now says so: `DeleteBlocked=True/HostUnreachable` (and `Ready=False/DeleteBlocked`) names the VM's `Host` (`status.placement.host`, or the pending host), says whether anything may have been deleted and that the delete completes once the host answers. It applies to a `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` naming the VM's host and, new, to `HOST_CONNECTION_LOST` (R25), which before set no condition. A `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` that does not name the VM's host keeps the constant message naming no host. No endpoint, URI or address is ever named. The finalizer is kept exactly as before.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_phase.go`: a VM held by a clustered restore guard (R1/R4: `RestorePending`, `OwnDomainOnAnotherHost`, `UniquenessCheckFailed`, `ProviderLacksListOwnerFilter` on `Placed`/`Provisioning`, and `Ready=False/RestorePending` of a restored binding) is phase `Pending`, not `Failed` (V3b): it is held and proceeds once the cause is gone. `ImportedDiskPinned` and the other operator holds stay `Failed`.

### Added
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/provider_disks.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_disks_applied.go`, `virtualmachine_create_marker.go`, `internal/k8s/conditions.go`: `spec.disks` on a `libvirt` or `proxmox` Provider, which attach none of them (V4), is reported: condition `DisksApplied=False/NotSupportedByProvider` (set at create and after later changes, removed when `spec.disks` is emptied, never `True`, `Ready` untouched) and one `Warning` event `NotSupportedByProvider` per generation. Which types do not attach them is a manager-side table (`ProviderIgnoresAdditionalDisks`); a provider capability bit is the long-term fix. The create marker write carries the condition.
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/disk_attach_warning.go`, `disk_size_webhook.go`: the `VirtualMachine` validating webhook returns an admission warning (never a refusal) for the same case when it can read the VM's Provider in the VM's namespace; no warning when the Provider is missing, unreadable or in another namespace.
- Tests: `internal/providers/libvirt/host_answer_test.go` (the wait bounds, a session that is never confirmed, a handshake that never starts, a clustered `Describe` with every command slot held answered `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` naming the host before its deadline, and the unbounded case reproducing the old `Unknown`, the `host` metadata only for the routed host); `internal/controller/virtualmachine_delete_host_hold_test.go`; `virtualmachine_phase_test.go` (restore holds `Pending`, `ImportedDiskPinned` `Failed`); `virtualmachine_disks_applied_test.go` (condition at create and on a running VM, event once per generation, cleared); `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/disk_attach_warning_test.go` (warning for libvirt and Proxmox, none for vSphere, a missing Provider, another namespace, no reader).

### Changed
- `docs/provider-call-outcomes.md` (a host that does not answer in time; which host; new section "A delete held for an unreachable host"), `docs/clustered-restore.md` and `docs/vm-status-phase.md` (restore holds are `Pending`), `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md`, `docs/reconfigure-results.md` (`spec.disks` on libvirt and Proxmox), `docs/release-notes/next.md`.

### Why
rc5 lab validation findings V3 and V4: a delete held for an unreachable host showed only a stale `ProviderError`; a VM held by the restore guard showed `Failed`; a clustered `Describe` to an unreachable host answered two different codes; and `spec.disks` on a libvirt VM was ignored while `Reconfiguring` said "VM reconfigured successfully".

## [2026-10-23 23:35] - spec.snapshot.revertToRef reverts the VM: once per request, only while it is powered off (V2)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_snapshot_revert.go` (new), `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`: `VirtualMachine.spec.snapshot.revertToRef` was accepted by the CRD and documented by `examples/advanced/snapshot-lifecycle.yaml`, but no controller ever sent the provider's `SnapshotRevert` (present since 2025-08; found by the v0.4.0-rc5 lab validation, V2): the VM stayed `Ready` with no condition and no event. The `VirtualMachine` controller now acts on it after each successful `Describe` of a bound VM. The revert is sent only while the provider reports the VM `Off` and `spec.powerState` is `Off` or `OffGraceful`; the controller never powers a VM off for it and does not power it on afterwards (otherwise `SnapshotReverted=False/WaitingForPowerOff`). The `VMSnapshot` is resolved fail-closed: it must exist in the VM's namespace, name this VM in `spec.vmRef`, be bound to this VM's UID (`status.vmUID`, or a legacy snapshot proven by its timestamps) and, when it records one, Provider (`status.boundProvider`), be `Ready`, not be deleting, and carry `status.snapshotID` (`SnapshotNotFound`, `SnapshotNotReady`, `SnapshotForAnotherVM`); a Provider reporting `supportsSnapshots: false` gets `Unsupported`. It is sent at most once per request: `status.snapshotRevert` records the `VMSnapshot`'s name and UID and the outcome, and while it records `Succeeded` or `Failed` for the `VMSnapshot` the field names nothing is sent again (a GitOps re-apply or another spec change never reverts again); removing the field clears the record, and a ref to another `VMSnapshot` (another UID) is a new request. The attempt (`phase: Reverting`, `attempts`, `attemptTime`) is written with the optimistic lock of the read `resourceVersion` before the call, and nothing is sent if that write fails or if the installed CRD prunes the field. The answer is written the same way; when that write loses a `resourceVersion` race (the spec changed during the call), the VM is re-read live and the record and condition are written over the stored status while it still holds the same attempt (`persistSnapshotRevert`). A provider task (Proxmox, mock) is recorded in `taskRef` and polled every 10 s, for at most 2 hours after the attempt; while it runs nothing else is done to the VM. A task the provider reports in-band that it does not know ends `Failed` (fail-closed); a `NotFound` from the task-status call makes the outcome unknown. A call whose outcome is unknown (a retryable or transport failure, a clustered `HOST_CONNECTION_LOST`, a lost answer) stays `Reverting` and is sent again only after a fresh `Describe` shows the VM still off with `spec.powerState` still off, to the same `VMSnapshot` (same UID), while the Provider still reports snapshot support, 6 minutes after the last attempt doubling to 30, at most 5 calls. A VM seen in any other power state (or whose spec asks it to run) after such an attempt may have run since, so the request then ends `Failed` and is never re-sent; so does a deleted `VMSnapshot`, a withdrawn capability, or the fifth unknown outcome. A definite provider failure (a refusal, an untyped error, `Unimplemented` → `Unsupported`) is terminal (`RevertFailed`, the provider's message sanitised by `providerFailureDetail`) and is not retried until the field is removed and set again. Events `SnapshotRevertStarted`, `SnapshotRevertSucceeded` (Normal) and `SnapshotRevertFailed` (Warning). `Ready` is never `True` while `SnapshotReverted` is `False` (`setVMReady` at the three Ready=True sites, and `applySnapshotRevertReadiness` on every status write); `status.phase` is unchanged (it follows the power state). `status.snapshotRevert.message` is cut to the CRD's 1024-byte bound before every write, so a long message never makes the status write fail.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_reconfigure_result.go`: Ready=True goes through `setVMReady`.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`: RBAC marker for `vmsnapshots` `get;list;watch` on the `VirtualMachine` controller (already granted to the manager role; no generated RBAC change).

### Added
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/virtualmachine_types.go`: additive `VirtualMachineStatus.SnapshotRevert` (`SnapshotRevertStatus`: `snapshotName`, `snapshotUID`, `phase` `Pending|Reverting|Succeeded|Failed`, `taskRef`, `attempts`, `requestedAt`, `attemptTime`, `completionTime`, `message`), the `SnapshotReverted` condition type and its reasons (`WaitingForPowerOff`, `SnapshotNotFound`, `SnapshotNotReady`, `SnapshotForAnotherVM`, `Unsupported`, `Reverting`, `Reverted`, `RevertFailed`); `revertToRef`'s GoDoc states the rules. Regenerated `zz_generated.deepcopy.go`, `config/crd/bases/infra.virtrigaud.io_virtualmachines.yaml` and `infra.virtrigaud.io_vmsets.yaml` (`make generate gen-crds`).
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_snapshot_revert_test.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_snapshot_revert_envtest_test.go`: the happy path (one RPC, no second one on later reconciles or after an unrelated spec change), VM on or spec `On` (`WaitingForPowerOff`, no RPC, never powered off for it), every refused `VMSnapshot` (missing, not Ready, no id, deleting, another VM by name, UID or Provider, unbound legacy), unsupported (capabilities and `Unimplemented`), an async task polled to completion with power held while it runs, a failed task, a task unknown to the provider, a terminal failure with a credential-bearing message sanitised, removal clearing the record, remove-and-re-add and another snapshot reverting again, a `VMSnapshot` re-created under the same name, a manager restart mid-call (re-sent once after the wait; `Failed` and never re-sent when the VM was seen on, its spec set to On, its capability withdrawn or the snapshot deleted), unknown outcomes bounded at 5 calls, `HOST_CONNECTION_LOST` read as unknown, a task reported unknown in-band failing, an overdue task released after 2 hours, the field removed while a task runs, the answer kept across a spec change during the call (success, task and failure), Ready kept False through a synchronous Reconfigure, a stale cached read sending nothing, a CRD that prunes the field sending nothing, the message bound, the clustered call carrying host and owner; and an envtest run of the whole flow against a real API server. The unit tests drive a scripted provider fake, not the gRPC transport.

### Changed
- `examples/advanced/snapshot-lifecycle.yaml`: the revert section describes the real flow (power off, set `revertToRef`, watch `status.snapshotRevert` and the condition, power on; remove then re-add to repeat) instead of a controller that powers the VM off, reverts, powers it on and clears the field.
- `docs/vm-snapshot-revert.md` (new): how to revert, the rules, `status.snapshotRevert`, the condition and its reasons, events, GitOps, per-provider behaviour as implemented, limitations and upgrade notes. `docs/README.md` indexes it; `docs/provider-call-outcomes.md` (the marker table, the unknown-outcome table, and the routed `SnapshotRevert` row, which said the controllers did not call it), `docs/vm-status-phase.md` and `docs/upgrading.md` (behaviour-change row with a command that lists VMs carrying the field) updated.
- `docs/release-notes/next.md`: new section "Changes since v0.4.0-rc5" for this fix, marked as never validated on a real hypervisor.

### Why
A field that is accepted and silently ignored let a user believe a VM was reverted when it was not. The revert discards the VM's disk state, so it must never be sent twice by accident (GitOps re-applies, stale caches, restarts) and never to a running VM VirtRigaud was not asked to power off.

## [2026-10-23 23:30] - HostPool.status is written from its member Hosts (V1)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/controller/hostpool_controller.go`, `cmd/manager/main.go`: `HostPool.status` was never written by any controller (every pool showed `status: null`). A new `HostPoolReconciler` counts the pool's member Hosts (in the pool's namespace, `spec.poolRef.name` naming the pool) into `totalHosts`, `readyHosts` (`status.health` Ready) and `schedulableHosts` (Ready, `spec.schedulable` true, not being deleted, and `spec.providerRef` equal to the pool's: the per-host test placement applies), stamps `observedGeneration`, and sets a `Ready` condition with `observedGeneration`: `True`/`HostsAvailable` when `schedulableHosts` > 0, `False`/`NoMemberHosts` for an empty pool, `False`/`NoSchedulableHosts` when no member is schedulable. The message states counts only. Host events are mapped to the pool their `spec.poolRef` names (an update maps both the old and the new object, so a Host moving pools recounts both; a delete recounts its pool); a Host update is passed only when its poolRef, providerRef, schedulable flag, health or deletion state changes, so heartbeats do not recount. An unchanged status is not written; a changed one is sent whole as a merge patch on the status subresource (single writer, no conflict). No periodic requeue.

### Changed
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/hostpool_types.go`, `config/crd/bases/infra.virtrigaud.io_hostpools.yaml`: printer columns `Total`, `Ready`, `Schedulable`; the three counts are written even when 0 (no `omitempty`, still optional in the schema); field descriptions say exactly what is counted. The schema is otherwise unchanged.
- `config/rbac/role.yaml` (regenerated), `charts/virtrigaud/templates/manager-rbac.yaml` (ClusterRole and namespaced Role): the manager may `get`/`patch`/`update` `hostpools/status`. `hostpools` and `hosts` reads were already granted.
- `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md`: new "`HostPool.status`" section (members, counts, condition and reasons, when it is written, example `kubectl get hostpools`); the First VM checklist points at it. `docs/release-notes/next.md`: "Changes since v0.4.0-rc5".

### Added
- `internal/controller/hostpool_controller_test.go`: counts (Ready / NotReady / Unknown / unschedulable / deleting / other Provider / other pool / other namespace), condition reasons, observedGeneration, no write when unchanged or on a heartbeat, the Host mapping and update predicate, and the chart and generated RBAC.
- `internal/controller/hostpool_status_envtest_test.go`: the controller in a manager against a real apiserver: counts, a foreign-namespace Host not counted, an empty pool, a Host moving from one pool to another updating both, a health change, a deleted Host, no pool write on Host heartbeats, observedGeneration after a spec change, and the printer columns (0 shown for an empty pool).

### Why
rc5 lab validation finding V1: a pool with two Ready, schedulable Hosts showed `status: null`, while the documentation said the status aggregated member-host counts and readiness. Operators had no pool-level view of whether a clustered Provider could place a VM.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-23 18:00] - Proxmox VMs get the bridge, VLAN, model and static IP their networks name (R36, ADR-0014 Slice 0a)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/proxmox/networks.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`: the provider read `networks_json` into a `map[string]interface{}` with lower-case keys (`name`, `vlan`, `mac`, a nested `static_ip`), but the manager sends `json.Marshal([]contracts.NetworkAttachment)`, whose keys are the Go field names (`Bridge`, `VLAN`, `Model`, `StaticIP`, ...). No field of a Proxmox network was applied: every NIC was `virtio` on `vmbr0` with no static IP. `networks_json` is now decoded into `[]contracts.NetworkAttachment` (no JSON tags added to the contract, so other providers' wire keys are unchanged) and each attachment's bridge, model, VLAN tag, MAC (when one arrives) and flat `StaticIP`/`Prefix`/`Gateway`/`DNS` are applied. A static IP becomes `ipconfigN` (`ip=<addr>/<prefix>[,gw=<gateway>]`, `ip6=`/`gw6=` for IPv6) and the DNS servers the VM's `nameserver`. An invalid bridge, model, VLAN, MAC, static IP, prefix, gateway or DNS server, more than 32 attachments, or malformed `networks_json` is refused as `InvalidSpec` (the message names the entry, never the value) before any VM is made.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`: the dead name-to-bridge heuristic (`dmz` to `vmbr1`, `mgmt` to `vmbr2`) is removed; an attachment's name is a label.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/networks.go`: `configureClonedVM` overwrote every `netN` of a clone that had user-data or SSH keys with `virtio,bridge=vmbr0` (the template's bridge and VLAN lost, a new MAC). It now writes only the NICs the spec names (a bridge, model, VLAN or MAC), merged into the clone's own NIC: the clone's PVE-assigned MAC and other options are kept, a named bridge replaces the template's placement (VLAN included), and a NIC the spec does not name is untouched. It runs for clones without user-data too. The provider's `,mac=` writer (not a PVE key) is gone; the merge writes PVE's `<model>=<MAC>` form.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/pveapi/client.go`: an `ipconfigN` carried `nameserver=`, which PVE rejects; DNS is now the VM's own `nameserver` key (`IPConfigString`, `NameserverValue`).
- `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`: `ListVMs` reads a NIC's MAC from PVE's `<model>=<MAC>` (and `macaddr=`) form and reports NICs in index order (it read `mac=`, so it never reported a MAC, and listed NICs in map order).
- `internal/controller/network_attachment_blocks.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`: the manager filled a network's VLAN from a `VMNetworkAttachment`'s vSphere block and its bridge and model from the libvirt block whatever the target Provider's type, so an attachment with several blocks put a vSphere VLAN on a Proxmox NIC and a libvirt-only attachment gave a Proxmox VM `bridge=br0`. Only the block of the target Provider's type (`vsphere`, `libvirt`, `proxmox`) is read now; a Proxmox VM whose attachment has no `proxmox` block sends no bridge, model or VLAN. A Provider type with no block of its own (`qemu`, `firecracker`) or no Provider reads all blocks, as before.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/networks.go`: the DNS servers of a DHCP entry are applied (PVE's `nameserver` is VM-wide) and validated; a model change away from `virtio` drops the virtio-only NIC options (`mtu`, `queues`, `host-tunnel`); the bridge refusal says the CRD currently allows `vmbrN` only.

### Changed
- `internal/providers/proxmox/pvefake/netconfig.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/pvefake/server.go`: the fake validates `netN`, `ipconfigN` and `nameserver` on create and config updates the way PVE does (unknown keys such as `mac=`, multicast MACs, a bad bridge ID and a gateway without its address are refused; `host-tunnel` is a known option), keeps them in the VM's config, and gives each NIC of a clone a new MAC (`pvefake.CloneMAC`).
- `examples/proxmox-complete-example.yaml`: the static IP is on the `VirtualMachine`'s entry (the attachment's `ipAllocation` was never forwarded); a comment says `macAddress` is not forwarded to the Proxmox provider yet.
- `test/proxmox-grpc-test/main.go`: its networks use the manager's key spelling.

### Added
- `internal/providers/proxmox/networks_test.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/pvefake/netconfig_test.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/pveapi/ipconfig_test.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/client_create_proxmox_networks_test.go`: tests that marshal the real `contracts.NetworkAttachment` (the last one through `convertCreateRequest` into the real provider on the fake), cover new-VM and clone NICs, MAC preservation, IP settings, refusals and reporting; `TestProxmoxProvider_MultiNIC` no longer sends hand-written lower-case JSON.
- `docs/proxmox-networks.md` (listed in `docs/README.md`): how networks reach PVE; `docs/upgrading.md`: the behavior change and the rollback caveat.

### Why
rc4 validation finding R36 (ADR-0014 Slice 0a): the Proxmox provider ignored the bridge, VLAN, model and static IP of every VM, migrated or not, so VMs landed on the wrong network. This is the standalone first slice; MAC forwarding and its tenant policy are Slice 0b. It needs a Proxmox provider rollout and a manager rollout (the manager now sends only the target Provider type's network block), and a PVE token that holds `VM.Config.Network`, `VM.Config.Cloudinit` and `SDN.Use` on its bridges (documented in `docs/proxmox-networks.md`). Refused now that were silently ignored: an `ipAddress` without `prefix`, and a `dns` entry that is not an IP. VMs that relied on the accidental `vmbr0` default change on their next create or clone, and existing VMs are not modified.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-23 17:00] - Proxmox cloud-init drive: never collide with the clone's own drive; power-task fixes (R33/R34 review)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/cloudinit_storage.go`: a full clone of a template that already has a cloud-init drive owns a `vm-<id>-cloudinit` volume, and PVE cannot allocate it a second time on the same storage (confirmed on PVE 9.2: `Logical Volume ... already exists`, the drive left unchanged). With the storage chosen by #425 (usually the drive's own), every Create of such a template failed and was retried. The provider now sets no drive when the clone's is already on the chosen storage, replaces it in its own slot when it is on another one, and handles a template whose cloud-init drive is not `ide2` (the boot order follows the slot). A re-sent Create changes nothing the second time.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`: the clone's config is read once, and if it cannot be read the Create fails and is retried; #425 fell back to `local`, which recreates R33 silently. `local` is only used when the config reads fine and shows no storage-backed disk (and no default storage is set).
- `internal/providers/proxmox/cloudinit_storage.go`: the order is now the request's or image's storage, then the storage the clone's primary disk lives on, then `PROVIDER_DEFAULT_STORAGE` / `PVE_DEFAULT_STORAGE`, then `local` (#425 had the default before the disk). The drive goes where the VM's disk is; the default stays the target for imports, VMs without a template and clones whose disk is not storage-backed.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/cloudinit_storage.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`: a storage named for the VM (request, image) and the provider's default storage must be a valid PVE storage ID; otherwise the Create is refused as an invalid spec before anything is created, with a message that does not repeat the value, so it cannot add parameters to the `<storage>:cloudinit` config value.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`: `TaskStatus` answered "done, with an error" when its own query of PVE failed (an API blip, a timeout), which made the manager forget a task that was still running. A transient failure (a transport error, a timeout, a 5xx, 401/403, 429) now answers Unavailable, so the manager keeps the task and asks again; a query PVE rejects as a request (a malformed or unknown UPID: any other 4xx, or a 5xx saying there is no such task) ends the task with an error, so no manager polls it for ever; "done with an error" is also what a task that ended with a non-OK exit status gets. A `VMMigration` whose snapshot task cannot be polled now fails the snapshot at the task's wait limit instead of polling for ever.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`, `internal/k8s/conditions.go`: a failed power task was settled as `Reconfiguring=False/ProviderError`, which the manager reads as a failed Reconfigure and answers with a Reconfigure (and which blocked lowering a clustered VM's memory ceiling). The failure is now on `Ready=False/ProviderError` only, and the marker is settled as `Reconfiguring=False/PowerTaskFailed` (new reason).
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`: a power task that keeps failing no longer re-sends the power operation about every 10 seconds (thousands of PVE start tasks per VM per day): it goes on a per-VM backoff, 5 s doubling to 5 min, reset when a power operation completes or the spec changes.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`: the "Adjusting power state" marker is only set over an absent or settled `Reconfiguring` condition. #425 overwrote the condition of a real reconfigure (a reconfigure in flight, `RestartRequired`, `ResizePendingPowerOff`, a failed Reconfigure to be sent again); it is now kept, and a power task that fails is still recognised (the manager remembers the task its last power operation returned).
- `internal/providers/proxmox/pvefake/server.go`: the fake models what a clone owns (disks, cloud-init drive, efidisk and tpmstate are renamed `vm-<newid>-*` and, for a full clone with a target storage, moved to it), refuses to allocate a cloud-init volume that already exists on the storage, and records the drives a create or config update sets; directory/file storages (`SetDirStorages`) name the cloud-init file `<id>/vm-<id>-cloudinit.raw` after a full clone and `.qcow2` after a config update (as seen on PVE 9.2); a clone without `full` is linked when its source is a template, as in PVE; `handlePowerOp` has its doc comment back.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/pveapi/client.go`: `PrimaryDiskFromConfig`, `CloudInitDrive` (matches PVE's volume name `vm-<id>-cloudinit`, with the `<id>/` directory and a `.raw`, `.qcow2` or `.vmdk` extension on file storages; an ISO named `cloudinit...` is not a drive), `ValidStorageID` and `IsTerminalTaskQueryError` (pure helpers); `GetTaskStatus` returns the PVE answer as an `APIError`; `DetectPrimaryDisk` is removed (unused).
- `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`: the default storage (`PROVIDER_DEFAULT_STORAGE` / `PVE_DEFAULT_STORAGE`) is also checked as a storage ID when the provider starts (an error is logged, without the value) and by `Validate`, which fails with a message naming the variables.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`: a VM's power task record and its power and Reconfigure backoffs are dropped when it is deleted; `Reconfiguring=False/PowerTaskFailed` is settled to `ReconcileSuccess` once the VM is observed in the power state its spec asks for.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_snapshot_task.go`: a snapshot task whose polls keep failing fails the snapshot once the task's wait limit has passed, as a task that answers but does not finish does.

### Added
- `internal/providers/proxmox/cloudinit_storage_test.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/pveapi/cloudinit_drive_test.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_power_task_marker_test.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_power_task_retry_test.go`, `internal/controller/vmmigration_snapshot_task_test.go`: tests for the fixes.

### Changed
- `docs/proxmox-cloud-init-storage.md`: the order, the clone's own cloud-init drive, the storage-ID check, what "primary disk" means (the first non-cdrom drive in the order virtio, scsi, sata, ide, which can be a data disk).
- `docs/vm-status-phase.md`: "A power change that returns a task" (the kept conditions, `PowerTaskFailed`, the backoff, tasks the provider cannot report on).
- `docs/README.md`: the row of the Proxmox cloud-init storage page.

**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

- `docs/adr/0014-migrated-guest-network.md`: accepted with the maintainer's decisions on its twelve open questions (keep the MAC as identity; `guestIdentity: Preserve|Fresh`, default `Preserve`; wait for the source to be off; never copy user-data; no datasource when the instance-id is unknown; a VM-owned Proxmox seed volume; no synthesized target networks; Slice 0 split into 0a (Proxmox network plumbing, now) and 0b (MAC forwarding with a default-deny tenant MAC policy); Windows out of scope; `DataSourceNone` guests documented with a warning).
- `docs/adr/0014-migrated-guest-network.md`: design for R36 (maintainer decision "option 1"). Researches cloud-init 24.4/25.1 semantics (instance-id comparison, datasource change between boots, update events, `manual_cache_clean`) and PVE's instance-id derivation, with source citations. Finds that a same-instance-id seed with a network-config does not re-render the network on the first target boot. Recommends carrying the source NIC MACs to the target and presenting the same instance-id (or no datasource when it is unknown), captured once by a new `DescribeGuestIdentity` RPC. Proposes `spec.options.guestIdentity: Preserve|Fresh`, eight slices and twelve open questions. Also records two latent bugs. First, `spec.networks[].macAddress` is dropped before every provider; forwarding it comes with a default-deny tenant MAC policy, because an arbitrary MAC on a shared bridge allows ARP and DHCP hijacking. Second, the Proxmox provider parses `networks_json` with keys the manager never sends, so bridge, VLAN, MAC and static IP are ignored and cloned NICs are reset to `vmbr0`.
- `docs/adr/README.md`: index row for ADR-0014.

### Why
v0.4.0-rc4 lab runs showed migrated Ubuntu guests without network on vSphere and Proxmox targets, and with a new cloud-init identity (hostname, SSH host keys) on libvirt targets.

## [2026-10-23 16:00] - Proxmox cloud-init drive storage (R33) and the stuck "Adjusting power state" phase (R34)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/cloudinit_storage.go`: the cloud-init drive (`ide2`) of a VM with user-data was `local:cloudinit` for every VM cloned from a template, because the clone path carried no storage, and PVE's stock `local` has no `images` content type, so every such VM failed to start. The storage is now the request's or image's (`storage` key, or `source.proxmox.storage` of a `VMImageSpec`, read even when the template is named), else `PROVIDER_DEFAULT_STORAGE` / `PVE_DEFAULT_STORAGE`, else the storage the cloned VM's boot disk lives on (read from its config), and `local` only when none of those exist (a warning is logged). A VM created without a template uses the first two, then `local`.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/pveapi/client.go`: `DetectPrimaryDiskVolume` (the boot disk's key and config value from one config read; `DetectPrimaryDisk` uses it) and `DiskStorage` (the storage ID of a disk value, validated against PVE's storage-ID syntax).
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`: a power operation that returns a task (Proxmox) set `Reconfiguring=True` "Adjusting power state" and `status.lastTaskRef`; when the task ended only `lastTaskRef` was cleared, so every Proxmox VM stayed in phase `Reconfiguring` with `Ready=True`. The condition is now set to `False` (`ReconcileSuccess`, "Power state adjusted") when the task ends, and also on the first reconcile of a VM an earlier manager left with the marker and no task. A real reconfigure's condition (another reason or message, or a recorded `reconfigureTaskRef`) is never touched. A power task that ends in failure is forgotten (it was polled for ever before) and shown on `Ready` and `Reconfiguring` as `ProviderError` "Power state change failed: ...".
- `internal/providers/proxmox/pvefake/server.go`: the fake records `ide2` on create and config updates, and a clone copies its source's raw config (disks moved to the clone request's `storage`).

### Added
- `internal/providers/proxmox/cloudinit_storage_test.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_power_task_marker_test.go`: tests for both fixes.
- `docs/proxmox-cloud-init-storage.md`: how the drive's storage is chosen; `docs/README.md` lists it.
- `docs/vm-status-phase.md`: "A power change that returns a task".
- `charts/virtrigaud-provider-runtime/examples/values-proxmox.yaml`: a commented `PVE_DEFAULT_STORAGE` example.

### Why
rc4 validation on a real PVE 9.2 node (R33, R34): every Proxmox VM with user-data failed to start on `local`, and every Proxmox VM showed phase `Reconfiguring` after a power change although it was Ready.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout

- [ ] Documentation only
