## [2026-10-23 12:00] - Clustered libvirt: a host that stops answering is not always "nothing done" (R25)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routing.go` (`hostOpRPCErrorFor`, `routedRPCErrorFor`, `routedReadRPCError`, `routedIdempotentRPCError`): a routed call on a clustered provider whose host stopped answering (a command that ended with no exit status of its own, or a virsh that could not reach libvirtd) was always answered `Unavailable` + `HOST_UNAVAILABLE`, which the manager reads as definite ("nothing was done"). It is now answered by how far the call got: `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` only while the host answered no command and none that may change it was sent; "not performed" (`Unavailable` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`) while only reads ran; an unknown outcome (`Unknown` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`) once a command that may change the host was sent. `SnapshotCreate` and `Clone` answer the retryable form of the unknown outcome (`Unavailable` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`, "its outcome is unknown ... retry"), because the manager retries them on the same host (request token; stamped target and `flock`) and an `Unknown` would fail the `VMClone`. `Describe`, `GetDiskInfo` and `TaskStatus` only read and stay `HOST_UNAVAILABLE`. The routed `ExportDisk` is the case that mattered: a session that dropped while `qemu-img` flattened or converted was reported as nothing done, so the migration cleared its `ExportRequested` marker, failed the attempt, and its retry policy could send the export again while the first one still ran (the export's `flock` then answers "still running").
- `internal/providers/libvirt/host_progress.go` (new), `routing.go` (`withHostConn`, `withOwnedDomain`, `hostOpError`), `virsh.go`, `hoststdin.go`, `sshclient.go`, `provider_virsh.go` (`createClustered`): each routed call carries a `hostProgress` in its context (`withHostConn` and the clustered create make it, and pass the context to the call's closure); `runVirshCommand`, `runHostStdin`, `runSSHStdin` and `runSSHStdout` record into it when it is present, and do nothing otherwise (single-host calls are unchanged). A command is recorded when it is **sent**. Only a fixed list of reads (read-only `virsh` subcommands, `qemu-img info`, `test`/`stat`, the provider's path and disk probes) does not count as a write.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_migration_cleanup.go`: the routed `DeleteLandedDisk` was `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` for a dropped session even after its `rm` was sent. It is now `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` only before the host answered a command, `Unavailable` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` ("could not be checked or removed") after reads, and `Unavailable` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` ("not known whether it was removed; will retry") after the `rm` was sent. The manager retries any error, and a retry that finds the disk gone is `NOT_FOUND`. The routed `DeleteStagedDisk` (`nfs`) already answered a failed `qemu-img` as a plain `Unavailable` and is unchanged.
- The disk-dependency guard's "host unreachable" answer (`guardHostUnreachableError`, nothing changed by construction) stays `HOST_UNAVAILABLE`, as do the cluster-wide guard's answers.

- Review round (#422): `internal/providers/contracts/errors.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/client.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/routing.go`, `routed_migration_cleanup.go`, `server.go`, `routed_snapshot_token.go`, `internal/controller/provider_request_marker.go`: the "outcome unknown, safe to retry" answer (a `Clone` or `SnapshotCreate` whose write was sent, the `SnapshotCreate` time-budget answer, "the request's snapshot is still being taken", a `DeleteLandedDisk` whose `rm` was sent) has its own `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` reason, `VM_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN_RETRY` (`contracts.OutcomeUnknownRetryReason`), sent with `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`. The transport client maps it to a retryable error that is **not** "nothing done" (`IsNothingDone` false, `contracts.IsOutcomeUnknownRetry`), checked before `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`; `providerCallOutcomeKnown` never reads it as definite; it stays out of the circuit breaker. A manager that predates the reason maps the answer as before (retryable, read as not performed by `IsNothingDone`, out of the breaker) and its controllers check "retryable" first, so it still retries and never fails on it. The answers "another operation is still running" and "the same copy is still running" stay "not performed".
- `internal/providers/libvirt/host_progress.go`, `sshclient.go`, `virsh.go`: a write is recorded as sent only once its SSH session is open (or its local process starts): a dial or session-open failure ran nothing, so it stays `HOST_UNAVAILABLE`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/host_progress.go`: `snapshot-current` (it can set the current snapshot) is no longer on the read list, and `dommemstat` is a read only without `--period`, `--config`, `--live` or `--current`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`: a `SnapshotCreate` gets the retry form only when it names its snapshot and carries a request token; any other (a direct caller) gets `Unknown`, its time-budget answer included, because its retry could take a second snapshot.
- `internal/providers/contracts/errors.go` (`HostConnectionLostReason`), `routing.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_clustered.go`: the host-loss answers (not performed, unknown, retry form) also carry `HOST_CONNECTION_LOST`, and a routed `Power` or `Reconfigure` answered with it is re-checked every 30 s (`boundHostUnavailableRetryInterval`), as for an unavailable host, instead of every 5 s; other provider errors keep 5 s.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`: a clustered `Delete` stops, and is retried, when the host stops answering during the `destroy` instead of going on to `undefine` a domain that may still be running (which would leave it running as a transient domain whose disks are then removed). A `destroy` that fails with an exit status is still ignored, and the single-host delete is unchanged.

### Added
- `internal/providers/libvirt/host_progress_test.go`, `host_progress_ssh_test.go`, `routed_host_outcomes_retry_test.go`, `routed_host_outcomes_guard_test.go`, `internal/controller/provider_outcome_unknown_retry_test.go`, `virtualmachine_clustered_hostloss_test.go`: the dial failure over a real SSH client, the allowlist changes, the retry answers of `Clone`, `SnapshotCreate` (with and without a token, and its time budget) and `DeleteLandedDisk` through a real gRPC hop and the transport client, a `Create` whose guard cannot reach another host after setup writes (stays `HOST_UNAVAILABLE`), a `Delete` whose `destroy` drops, and the 30 s pacing of `Power` and `Reconfigure`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/host_progress_test.go`, `routed_host_outcomes_test.go`, `routed_host_outcomes_transport_test.go`: tables per routed RPC (Power, Reconfigure, Delete, Describe, SnapshotCreate, SnapshotDelete, SnapshotRevert, Clone, ExportDisk `nfs` and `s3`, TransferOwner, Create, DeleteLandedDisk, GetDiskInfo) for a host that never answers (also a dial failure), one that drops after answering reads, and one whose write is sent and whose session drops, is killed (137) or is stopped by `timeout(1)` (124); the answer matrix by RPC kind and stage; the classification of commands as reads or writes; and a routed `ExportDisk` through a real gRPC hop and the transport client's `mapGRPCError` (`IsNothingDone`, `IsHostUnavailable`, circuit breaker closed). The shell-shim fakes learned `dead` / `dead-<command>` (a call that dies without an exit status) and `exit-qemu-img-<subcommand>`.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_routed_export_answers_test.go`: the three answers of a routed `ExportDisk` through the transport client, and whether the migration controller reads them as a definite outcome (`providerCallOutcomeKnownFor`).

### Changed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_review415_test.go`: "the rm's session drops" is now the removal-unknown answer, not `HOST_UNAVAILABLE`. The existing tests that built a `hostOpError` by hand carry a `hostProgress`; one built without it assumes a write was sent.
- `docs/provider-call-outcomes.md` (new section "Clustered libvirt: a host that stops answering"), `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md`, `docs/reconfigure-results.md`, `docs/adr/0007-clustered-orchestrator-provider.md`: the answers by RPC, how the manager reads each, and what stays as it was. The ADR's "hostOpRPCError gap" is closed.

### Why
The manager treats `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` as proof that nothing was done, and acts on it (clears the `ExportRequested` marker, re-places, retries). A dropped SSH session after a mutating command started proves nothing, so answering it that way could start a second export, or a second copy, while the first still ran on the host. The routed `ImportDisk` already used the model (#415); this extends it to every routed call.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout (libvirt provider)
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-23 11:00] - ADR-0013 (Proposed): disk resize as its own, honest flow (R19)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Added
- `docs/adr/0013-disk-resize-flow.md`: Proposed design for R19 (from the #401 review). It records with file:line citations that a disk size change alone never reaches a provider (`needsReconfigure` compares CPU and memory only), what each provider does with disk sizes today, the missing stable disk identity and observed per-disk sizes, the capabilities that overstate disk support, and the missing disk dimension in clustered capacity. It proposes additive per-disk observation in `Describe` (`disks`, `disks_reported`) recorded in a new `status.disks`, a typed grow-only `ResizeDisks` RPC with per-disk outcomes behind a `supports_disk_resize` capability, a `DiskSizeApplied` condition, stable identities per provider (vSphere backing UUID and boot-order root, libvirt target dev, Proxmox bus key), clustered storage admission against `allocatableStorageBytes`, the upgrade and rollback matrix, security constraints, a test and lab plan, seven slices, and eight open questions.

A user's disk resize (`spec.disks[].sizeGiB`, VMClass `diskDefaults.size`) is silently ignored unless a CPU or memory change carries it, Proxmox never applies the class disk size, and the manager cannot see which disk sizes are applied. The design must be reviewed before implementation.

## [2026-10-22 17:00] - libvirt Host allocatable storage measured fresh (R31)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/hostinfo.go`: a libvirt host's allocatable storage (`Host.status.allocatableStorageBytes`) is the free space available to non-root users in its active `default` pool's directory — statvfs `f_bavail × f_frsize`, what `df` shows as *Available*, which excludes root-reserved blocks, so a host may report less than before — measured on every inventory sync with `timeout --kill-after=1s 10s stat -f -c "%a %S"` after reading the pool's type and target from `virsh pool-dumpxml default`. libvirt's `pool-info` *Available* is no longer used: libvirt caches it until a `pool-refresh` and counts root-reserved blocks. On two lab hosts sharing one NFS export it differed between the hosts (220.8 GiB and 558.5 GiB earlier in the day; 596,642,889,728 and 596,772,913,152 bytes, about 555.7 and 555.8 GiB, at review time), while `stat -f` gave 507261 × 1048576 = 531,901,710,336 bytes (about 495.4 GiB, `df`'s *Available*) on both. No `pool-refresh` is run.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/hostinfo.go`, `storage.go`: the pool directory is accepted exactly as creates and imports accept it (`isRequiredPoolDirOn`, now shared with `EnsureDefaultStoragePool`: `/var/lib/libvirt/images` lexically after cleaning, else once resolved on the host with `realpath`), and that directory is what is measured. The host reports 0 (fail closed for the disk-space filter; the provider log says why, at Warn when a problem starts for a host and at Debug while it lasts) when the `default` pool is not of type `dir`, `fs` or `netfs`, or is not at `/var/lib/libvirt/images`; also when it is inactive, its definition or directory cannot be read or resolved, `stat` fails or prints something unexpected (quoted host output is clipped to 200 bytes), the probe runs out of its budget (15 s, or half of the caller's remaining deadline when that is less), or a previous probe of the same host has not returned.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/nfs.go`: the import-time free-space check (`hostFreeBytes`) shares the same format and a strict parser (exactly two non-negative integers, a positive block size, no overflow).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_import.go`: the file comment says the routed landing lock is keyed on the landing name alone, provider-wide (`routedLandingKey`), not on (host, landing name).
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/host_types.go`, `proto/provider/v1/provider.proto` (regenerated CRD and Go bindings: comments only), `docs/adr/0007-clustered-orchestrator-provider.md`: the description of the storage figure.

### Added
- `internal/providers/libvirt/hostinfo_test.go`, `hosts_test.go`: statvfs output parsing (odd outputs, overflow, clipping), pool types, unclean, symbolic-link, misplaced and unresolvable pool directories, the budget (15 s, half of a short caller deadline, real expiry, a cancelled caller), the per-host in-flight guard and Warn-once logging, the command sequence (no `pool-refresh`, no `pool-info`), `hostFreeBytes` strictness, and two hosts sharing one pool filesystem reporting the same value and following it when it changes.
- `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md`, `docs/upgrading.md`: the `allocatable_storage` source, its fail-closed cases and limitations (an unmounted filesystem behind an active pool; a `stat` in uninterruptible sleep on a dead hard mount cannot be killed), and the visible change.

### Why
The B7.4 disk-space placement filter (migration targets, `VMPlacementPolicy` `minDiskSpacePerHost`) compared requests against stale per-host values, so it could place a disk on a host without room or refuse one with room.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout (libvirt provider)
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-22 10:53] - Migration into a clustered provider: #416 review fixes (R11 slice B.3)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_clustered_target.go` (H1, L1): a retry after a routed import deletes the landed disk on its recorded host and, once the provider confirms it deleted, forgets the import completely (`status.importID`, the landed path/format/checksum, `Importing`, the `ImportRequested` marker and its in-memory guard, `importTarget.host`, `TargetPlaced`; the export too when the staged object is gone), so the retry imports again instead of handing a deleted path to its fresh target. A kept landed disk (`cleanupPolicy: Never`, in use, left behind) keeps `importTarget.host`: the fresh target is placed on that host only and the disk is reused there. A retry whose target is still bound to exactly the imported disk reuses it.
- `internal/scheduler`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_import_wait.go` (L3): `Request.RequiredHost`; a migration target whose migration recorded an import host is scheduled onto that host only (an administrator clearing its pending host, a retry keeping its disk).
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_clustered_target.go` (M1, L2): the B1.2 release persists the VMMigration first (marker removed, `TargetPlaced=False/TargetHostReleased`, `importTarget.host` and `LandedDiskCleanup` cleared — nothing landed), then releases the VM with in-place conflict retries; a failure between the two heals on the next import. A full `excludedHosts` list makes the next attempt wait `vmCreateConflictRetryInterval`.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`, `vmmigration_clustered_target_guard.go` (M2): a routed migration completes only on a target whose `spec.importedDisk` names it with `diskID == status.importID` and `path == status.diskInfo.targetPath` (checked in Creating and, live, in Validating-Target); otherwise `Ready=False/TargetDiskMismatch` and one Warning — never Ready, never `deleteAfterMigration`.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_clustered_target.go` (M3): consecutive "not performed" answers to a routed import fail the attempt into `retryPolicy` after 5 minutes (about five answers on the backoff), instead of re-downloading the disk forever.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/hostinfo.go` (M3): a libvirt host's allocatable storage is its `default` pool's free space only, not the sum of every active pool. - `internal/controller/vmmigration_staging_cleanup.go` (L4): an nfs staged object whose import was never routed and whose target VM is gone is emptied through any Ready host of the clustered Provider; held (not left behind) while none is Ready.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_clustered_target.go` (L5, L7): force-delete of a migration whose unbound target could not be deleted records an `UnboundTargetVMLeft` Warning; the B1.4 target reads run only for a migration with a target-first VM (`TargetPlaced`, now written with the claim), so single-host terminal and retry paths read nothing new.

## [2026-10-22 09:47] - VMMigration into a clustered provider: target-first flow (ADR-0007 Addendum B slice 3, R11)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Added
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/vmmigration_types.go`: `MigrationImportTarget.host` (status): the clustered host the import was routed to; re-sends and the landed / nfs staged-disk deletes go there only.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_clustered_target.go`: the migration's half of a clustered target. Validating gates on the runtime `supportsRoutedImport` (constant `ClusteredTargetUnsupported` refusal; also for a target in another namespace and for `pvc`), reads the source disk size, creates the target VM first (claim, empty `diskID`, `sizeGiB`) and waits with the new `TargetPlaced` condition until it has a pending host — before the source is powered off or exported. Importing re-reads the target live (`TargetNotPending` otherwise), records `importTarget.host` before the `ImportRequested` marker and sends `ImportDisk` with `target_host_id` and the VM's UID; a re-send goes only to the recorded host. Creating writes the landed disk into the target's `spec.importedDisk` (resourceVersion precondition) instead of creating a VM. A plain `AlreadyExists` or `HOST_STORAGE_MISCONFIGURED` from the landing host releases the target's pending host (checked status write: `pendingHost` cleared, host added to `excludedHosts`); a previous incarnation, `VM_DISK_IN_USE`, any other pre-write `FailedPrecondition`, `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` / `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED` and not-performed answers hold on a paced backoff. A migration that fails for good, is retried or is deleted deletes its unbound target VM first (UID precondition) and cleans up the landed disk only once it is gone; a retry also cleans up the previous attempt's landed disk.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_import_wait.go`: the VirtualMachine controller places a migration target and holds it (`Provisioning=False/WaitingForImport`) without a `Create` while its `diskID` is empty; a `migrationRef` naming a migration that is gone or did not create the VM is held unplaced (`MigrationNotFound`). After the import the host is pinned: a `Create` name conflict holds `Placed=False/ImportedDiskPinned` (no slice-2 exclusion, no A6.2 move).
- `internal/scheduler`: `Request.RequiredStorageBytes` filters hosts whose `allocatableStorageBytes` cannot hold a migration target's disk (or report none).
- `internal/k8s/conditions.go`: reasons `WaitingForImport`, `MigrationNotFound`, `ImportedDiskPinned`.
- `examples/vmmigration-into-clustered.yaml`; envtest (`vmmigration_clustered_target_envtest_test.go`) and unit tests.

### Changed
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/virtualmachine_types.go`: `ImportedDiskRef.diskID` may be empty while `migrationRef` is set (CEL rule replacing `MinLength=1`; an additive relaxation). CRDs regenerated.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_landed_disk_cleanup.go`, `vmmigration_staging_cleanup.go`: routed `DeleteLandedDisk` / nfs `DeleteStagedDisk` carry `target_host_id`; a clustered import target without a recorded host is left behind, never sent.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`: the clustered-target refusal at Validating is replaced by the gate above; the VMMigration controller watches its target VMs' placement; RBAC markers for `virtualmachines` delete and `virtualmachines/status`.
- `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md`, `docs/upgrading.md`, `docs/provider-call-outcomes.md`, `docs/cross-namespace-targets.md`, `examples/README.md`.

### Why
ADR-0007 Addendum B (accepted 2026-10-22, decisions B7): a clustered Provider becomes a migration target without a second scheduler — the target is placed (and its capacity reserved) before the source is touched, and the disk lands on the host the VM will run on. Single-host, vSphere and Proxmox targets keep import-then-create, unchanged.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout (CRDs: `VirtualMachine`, `VMSet`, `VMMigration`)
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-22 08:52] - Clustered libvirt provider routes ImportDisk and its cleanup (ADR-0007 Addendum B slices 1-2, R11)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Added
- `proto/provider/v1/provider.proto`: additive fields `ImportDiskRequest.target_host_id` (13), `DeleteLandedDiskRequest.target_host_id` (4), `DeleteStagedDiskRequest.target_host_id` (8) and `GetCapabilitiesResponse.supports_routed_import` (30); `ImportDiskRequest.target_vm` carries the target VirtualMachine's uid for a clustered provider. Regenerated bindings.
- `internal/providers/contracts/{types,landed_disk,staged_disk,capabilities}.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/client.go`: `TargetHostID` on the import, landed-disk and staged-disk delete requests and `Capabilities.SupportsRoutedImport`, threaded to and from the wire.
- `sdk/provider/capabilities/capabilities.go`: `CapabilityRoutedImport` and `Builder.RoutedImport`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_import.go`: the clustered `ImportDisk` (`s3` and `nfs`; `pvc` and the empty legacy backend are a constant `InvalidArgument` before any host is leased). It lands `<default pool>/<ns>.<vm>-migrated.qcow2` on `target_host_id` for the target VM named with its uid, after the landing host's name check (`VM_PREVIOUS_INCARNATION`, its `own` kind, or a plain `AlreadyExists`), the A6.1 cross-host guard on the landing file (fails closed; a file used on another host is `FailedPrecondition` + `VM_DISK_IN_USE`, a symlink at the landing name a host-guard refusal), the in-process landing lock on the landing name (provider-wide, whatever the host: a shared pool makes it one file; the wait bounded to 2 minutes) and a host `flock -n` on `<staging>/virtrigaud-locks/import-<domain>.lock`. The write half is the single-host one; every one of its host commands runs under the host guard, `flock` and `timeout --kill-after=10s` within the routed budget, so a re-send is safe; it is not started with less than a minute of budget left. The import's own removals run under `timeout(1)` only (never under the import's flock), and private write directories older than 65 minutes are reaped at import start. A landing host whose default pool is misplaced is `FailedPrecondition` + `HOST_STORAGE_MISCONFIGURED` (scoped to the host); a staged format outside `qcow2`/`raw`/`vmdk` (`nfs`: `qcow2`) is `InvalidArgument`. Staged locations are redacted from its log lines. Failures are classified R21-style: not performed for commands that ended with an exit status of their own, unknown for a command stopped by `timeout(1)`, killed or whose session dropped once the write phase began, and `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` only when the host never answered a command of the call (the `hostOpRPCError` gap the addendum records, closed for this path).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_migration_cleanup.go`: the clustered `DeleteLandedDisk` on `target_host_id`, with the in-use scan of EVERY host of the Provider (fails closed), the provider-wide landing lock and the removal under the import's host lock; the clustered `DeleteStagedDisk` (`s3` from the pod, `nfs` through `target_host_id`'s qemu-img under `timeout(1)`).
- `internal/providers/contracts/errors.go`: new ErrorInfo reason `HOST_STORAGE_MISCONFIGURED` (`HostStorageMisconfiguredReason`, `IsHostStorageMisconfigured`): an operation refused because the storage of the one host it was routed to is misconfigured.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_review415_test.go` and additions to the routed tests: the #415 security review fixes (cross-host landing lock against delete and create, cleanup without the flock and the reaper, removal outcomes of the routed delete, symlink refusal, format allow-list, minimum budget, cancelled call mid-convert, no staged location at WARN).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_import_test.go`, `routed_migration_cleanup_test.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/client_routed_import_test.go`, `sdk/provider/capabilities/routed_import_test.go`: a recording landing host proving every write-phase command is guarded and under `timeout(1)` within the budget, nfs and s3 golden sequences, refusals, the name check, a typed-outcome table, the landing lock and re-send; shared-pool tests for the cross-host guard, the real guarded write phase, the routed delete (in use elsewhere, unreachable host, host lock busy) and the clustered `Create`'s landing lock; wire and capability round trips.

### Changed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`: a clustered provider reports `supports_routed_import`, `supports_disk_import` (backends `s3`, `nfs`; the single-host source formats), `supports_import_size_limit`, `resend_safe_import_backends: [s3, nfs]`, `supports_landed_disk_delete` and staged-disk delete backends `s3`, `nfs`. Single-host capabilities are unchanged.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/{s3import,nfs}.go`: the s3/nfs import's write half is split into `landS3Import` / `landNFSImport` over an `importLanding`, shared by both paths (no single-host behaviour change).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`: a clustered `Create` that attaches an imported disk in place takes the landing lock of its landing name (provider-wide), serialised with the routed import and delete through any host.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/{staging,cluster_disk_guard,disk_mode}.go`: a symlink refusal of `checkWriteTarget` is a typed error that still reads and unwraps as the Conflict it was (Create, Clone and the single-host import answer unchanged); the cluster-wide guard answers `VM_DISK_IN_USE` for the import only; a private write directory can run its removals on a separate runner (the routed import's cleanup connection).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/staged_disk.go`: the DEBUG line of a failed staged-disk delete (single-host and clustered) no longer prints the staged object's nfs URL or s3 key.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/capabilities.go`, `internal/providers/mock/provider.go`: document that they ignore the new host fields and never report `supports_routed_import`.
- `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md` (Migration into a clustered provider, host prerequisites, routing table), `docs/provider-call-outcomes.md` (the routed import's outcomes, clustered `resend_safe_import_backends`), `docs/upgrading.md`.

### Security
- #415 review: on a shared pool, the landing lock keyed on (host, landing name) let a `DeleteLandedDisk` through one host remove a disk an import or create through another host was landing or attaching; it is now keyed on the landing name alone. The private write directory of a cancelled import could be leaked (its removal ran under the flock the still-running command held); removals no longer take the flock, and stale directories are reaped. Staged locations are no longer logged on these paths. Residual (documented): two Providers whose hosts share one pool are not serialised with each other.

### Why
ADR-0007 Addendum B (accepted 2026-10-22) makes a clustered Provider a migration target by routing the import to the target VM's pending host. These are its provider-side slices; the capability is what the manager will gate on. **The manager still refuses a clustered migration target at `Validating` until slice 3 (target-first flow) ships.**

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-22 10:47] - libvirt cloud-init seeds are private, in a dedicated seed directory (R27)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Security
- `internal/providers/libvirt/seed_dir.go` (new), `cloudinit.go`, `clone_clustered.go`, `staging.go`: a VM's cloud-init seed (its user-data, which may carry passwords, keys and tokens) was built in a per-create directory under the world-listable `/tmp`, so its random name was discoverable, with the ISO at the SSH user's umask (typically `0644`, and `0644` explicitly for a clustered clone's copy) and `user-data`/`meta-data` left next to it: any local user of a shared hypervisor host could read it. Seeds are now built in a dedicated seed directory, `VIRTRIGAUD_LIBVIRT_SEED_DIR` (default `/var/lib/libvirt/virtrigaud-seeds`, validated at startup: absolute, a safe character set, never under `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`, `/run`, `/dev`, `/proc`, `/sys`). Before it writes anything, the provider checks the directory on the target host (`ensureSeedRoot`): it creates a missing one with mode `0711` when the SSH user may, and refuses (fails closed, retryable, constant message `refusing to stage cloud-init data`, details in the provider log) one that is missing, not a directory, not owned by the SSH user, or readable or writable by its group or others. Inside a per-seed `mktemp -d` directory the ISO is created under umask `0077` and set to `0600` explicitly, the SSH user keeps a private copy (`cloud-init.private.iso`, `0600`) that a clone's copy reads (libvirt's `dynamic_ownership` gives the domain's ISO to the qemu user at start), `user-data` and `meta-data` are removed as soon as the ISO is built, and only then is the directory opened to `0711` (`sealSeedDir`, shared by Create and the clustered clone's `cloneSeedISO`). A create checks the seed directory before it writes the VM's disk, and a create without `spec.userData` now fails on an unusable seed directory instead of silently creating the VM without its seed. The meta-data content is no longer logged.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/domain_disks.go`, `seed_reclaim.go`, `provider_virsh.go`: a domain's seed directory is recognised, removed by `Delete` and swept by the R24 reclaim in every seed root (`Provider.seedRoots`: the seed directory and the staging directory earlier releases built seeds in), single-host and clustered; seeds of existing VMs are never moved.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/imagepath.go`: the seed directory and the private seed copy's name are refused as image directory / base image.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/seed_dir.go` (#414 review, L2): the seed-directory check now also walks every directory above it, along the configured path and its canonical path (`realpath -e`): each must be owned by root or the SSH user and not writable by group or others unless sticky, so no other account can rename the seed directory (or a directory on its path) away and plant its own between the check and the write. Refused with the same constant message.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/seed_dir.go` (#414 review, M1): `seedCopySource` also picks the private copy in an earlier release's per-name seed directory `<root>/virtrigaud-cloudinit/<name>/` (`isLegacySeedDirIn`), where the documented remediation now creates one.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go` (#414 review, L3): a successful create removes older (more than five minutes), unreferenced seed directories of the same domain name — plaintext user-data left by an earlier attempt — through the R24 reclaim, bounded and best-effort (never fails the create).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_seed.go`, `clone.go`, `clone_clustered.go`, `seed_dir.go` (integration with R26 clone seeds): `planCloneSeed` (now a `Provider` method) checks the host's seed directory before the source's seed is read or anything is copied (an unusable one refuses the clone, retryably, with the constant message), and `readSeedISO` reads the source's seed (the `isoinfo` listing and every file) from `seedCopySource`'s file — the SSH user's private copy once the source has started and libvirt has given its `cloud-init.iso` to the qemu user — keeping R26's rule that nothing read appears in an error or log. The clone's own seed (`writeCloneSeed`, `PrepareCloudInit`) is built in the seed directory and sealed like a create's, on single-host and clustered providers; `sealSeedDir` removes every NoCloud input (`user-data`, `meta-data`, `network-config`, `vendor-data`). The duplicate seed file-name constants are merged into R26's `seedFile*`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/seed_dir.go` (#414 review, I6): a single-host provider logs a startup `WARN` when the seed directory lacks `o+x` (a qemu running as another user cannot reach the seed ISOs); not refused.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider.go`: the constructors load `VIRTRIGAUD_LIBVIRT_SEED_DIR` (a malformed value fails start-up); a single-host provider checks the seed directory at startup and logs a `WARN` naming the problem.

### Removed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/cloudinit.go`: the unused `AttachCloudInitISO`/`copyISOToRemote` (copied seeds `0644` into `/var/lib/libvirt/images/cloud-init`).

### Added
- `internal/providers/libvirt/seed_dir_test.go` (new), `routed_clone_test.go`, `domain_disks_test.go`, and the fixtures in `main_test.go`, `domain_naming_create_test.go`, `snapshot_clone_disk_singlehost_test.go`, `routed_snapshot_test.go`, `cluster_disk_guard_test.go`, `seed_reclaim_test.go`: a create builds a `0600` ISO plus private copy in the seed directory with no `user-data`/`meta-data` left and nothing in the staging directory; a listable, group-readable, other-writable, non-directory or uncreatable seed directory is refused with nothing written and no domain defined (with and without user-data); a missing creatable one is created `0711`; seeds left in the staging directory by an earlier release are found and removed by `Delete` and by the leftover sweep; the clustered create builds its seed in the seed directory and the owner-checked Delete removes new and legacy seeds; the clustered clone runs the seed-root check, builds its copy private in order, reads the source's private copy, and is refused (copied disk removed, nothing defined) on an unusable seed directory; the clustered create is refused on an unusable seed directory; a seed directory of another uid is refused end to end; the ancestor rule with a group-writable, sticky, and symlinked parent (real shell); a failure at each sealing step (ISO chmod, private copy, its chmod, input removal, final chmod) and a create cancelled while the ISO is built leave no per-seed directory; a create removes the domain's old unreferenced seed and keeps a fresh one, its own and another domain's; `seedCopySource` with a legacy per-name directory, outside the seed roots and when the existence check fails; test seed directories live below a scratch base whose ancestors pass the rule (`safeTempDir`); with R26: a single-host and a clustered clone of a started source read its seed through the private copy (never the qemu user's ISO), the single-host clone's sealed seed is in the seed directory and each VM's Delete removes its own seed, a clone is refused on an unusable seed directory before the source's seed is read or its disk copied, and a clone seed carrying network-config and vendor-data is sealed without any input file while its ISO keeps them; R26's tests read the seed files from the fake ISO (the sealed directory keeps none), and the single-host golden call sequence (`testdata/single_host_snapshot_clone_disk.golden.json`) is regenerated for the seed-root checks and sealing steps; a seed built with the real `genisoimage` is still readable by the SSH user with `isoinfo` (the clone path's read) through `seedCopySource` after the domain's ISO is made unreadable (libvirt's hand-over to the qemu user, simulated), while the ISO itself no longer is; lexical validation, env loading and the check's output parsing.

### Changed
- `docs/libvirt-domain-ownership.md` (new section "Cloud-init seed directory": location, ownership and mode, the fail-closed check, `dynamic_ownership`, clones, AppArmor, SELinux, host preparation), `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md` (host prerequisite; the stale `/var/lib/libvirt/images/cloud-init` seed path removed), `docs/upgrading.md` (breaking-change row; leftovers: make `/tmp` seeds of existing VMs private — both layouts, the SSH user's private copy first — and move one into the seed directory with the exact name, ownership and modes Delete and clones need; the boot-time `/tmp` cleaning). After the #414 review the docs also state the ancestor rule, that the seed directory must be host-local (not NFS) and one per SSH user on a shared host (`VIRTRIGAUD_LIBVIRT_SEED_DIR` per Provider), that migration target hosts need it, and that it holds secret material (exclude it from backups or encrypt them; prefer short-lived bootstrap credentials), `docs/libvirt-clones.md` (with R26: the source's seed is read through the private copy, the seed directory is checked first, the clone's seed is sealed), `docs/image-preparation.md`, `examples/libvirt-complete-example.yaml`, `charts/virtrigaud-provider-runtime/examples/values-libvirt.yaml`.

### Why
Security review of #408: cloud-init seeds were readable by any unprivileged local user of the (shared) libvirt host. Also, `/tmp` is emptied at boot and cleaned of old files, after which a VM whose seed lived there no longer starts.

### Impact
- [x] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-22 08:40] - Clones get their own cloud-init seed and a new cloud-init identity (rc2 R26)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Security
- `internal/providers/cloneidentity/cloneidentity.go` (new): a clone booted with its source's cloud-init `instance-id` (its copied disk already records it), so cloud-init skipped every per-instance module: the clone kept the source's SSH host keys and hostname, and two VMs had one host identity. The shared helpers derive the clone's identity from its TARGET VirtualMachine: `InstanceID` (`virtrigaud-<uid>`, deterministic, so a re-sent Clone renders the same seed; the provider's clone name without a uid), `Hostname`/`LocalHostname` (`spec.customization.hostname`/`domain`, else the target's name), `ParseCustomization`. `RewriteMetaData` sets `instance-id`/`local-hostname` (and an existing `hostname`) in YAML or JSON meta-data, keeping every other key and the comments, and refuses a document that is not a mapping. `RewriteUserDataHostname` rewrites only the top-level block-style one-line `hostname:`/`fqdn:` keys of a `#cloud-config` document, and leaves any other format byte for byte.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_seed.go` (new), `internal/providers/libvirt/clone.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_clustered.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/cloudinit.go`: single-host and clustered `Clone` share one implementation. `planCloneSeed` reads the source's NoCloud seed with `isoinfo` (Rock Ridge, then Joliet; each file bounded to 1 MiB by a fixed `sh -c` script with positional arguments; contents never logged) BEFORE anything is copied. A read failure is retryable and an ISO without NoCloud files or with an oversized file is `InvalidSpec`, with nothing written. `writeCloneSeed` makes the clone's own seed through `PrepareCloudInit`, the same staging helper `Create` uses (a `mktemp` directory named after the CLONE's domain, so its Delete and the R24 reclaim remove it), and re-points the clone's CD-ROM at it. The seed holds the new identity, the user-data (`spec.customization.userData.cloudInit.inline` when set, else the source's with its hostname keys rewritten), and the source's `network-config`/`vendor-data` (new optional `CloudInitConfig` fields). A single-host clone no longer references its source's seed ISO; a clustered clone no longer gets a byte copy of it (`cloneSeedISO` removed). A failed single-host define removes the clone's seed unless the domain may exist. The #153 warning that `CustomizeJSON` was ignored is replaced by a warning naming the customization fields that are not applied.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/clone_identity.go` (new), `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go`, `internal/providers/vsphere/image_artifact.go`: `CloneVM_Task` copied the source's `guestinfo.metadata` (`instance-id: "<source name>"`) and `guestinfo.userdata`. The clone's ConfigSpec now rewrites them (keys matched without regard to case; decoding none, base64 and gzip+base64; each written back under the source's key spelling, in the source's encoding, with the source's encoding key restated). Metadata that cannot be decoded or parsed refuses the clone with `InvalidArgument` before anything is cloned. A source without `guestinfo.metadata` is unchanged: the instance-id then comes from the BIOS UUID, which vCenter regenerates. The source's ExtraConfig is read once (`sourceExtraConfig`) for this and for the image-stamp clearing.
- Security review of #413:
  - `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_seed.go` (M1): a seed read that failed after it started printing could leak part of the user-data. This happens when the SSH session drops or the context is cancelled mid `isoinfo | head -c`; the `VirshError` keeps the output in `Stdout`, which its `Error()` prints, and the Clone error mappers log the cause. `seedReadFailure` now reports only the exit code and stderr (context errors are kept; anything else becomes a constant), so no error or log line carries what was read.
  - `internal/providers/cloneidentity/cloneidentity.go`:
    - L2: `RewriteMetaData` refuses an `instance-id`/hostname value that carries a YAML anchor, and re-parses what it rendered.
    - L3: `RewriteUserDataHostname` only rewrites a line the YAML parser confirms is the top-level `hostname:`/`fqdn:` key with its whole value on the line. It never rewrites a look-alike line inside a multi-line quoted scalar or flow collection, and never a document that does not parse. A rewrite whose result would not parse is reverted and the keys are reported.
    - L4: new `IdentityOverrides` names the user-data keys that undo the new identity (`ssh_keys`, `ssh_deletekeys: false`, `preserve_hostname: true`, `manual_cache_clean: true`); libvirt and vSphere log them by name.
  - `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_seed.go`:
    - L1: a source seed without meta-data gets the provider's template filled through the YAML encoder, never `Sprintf`; an unvalidated customization domain can no longer inject keys.
    - L9: inline user-data over 1 MiB is `InvalidSpec`.
  - `internal/providers/vsphere/clone_identity.go`:
    - L5: guestinfo keys are matched without regard to case and written back under the source's spelling.
    - L6: each value keeps the source's encoding (gzip+base64 stays gzip), and the source's encoding key is restated.
  - `internal/providers/libvirt/clone.go` (L7): a single-host clone whose own seed cannot be made is retryable (`Unavailable`), not an unknown outcome, since nothing was defined. The define-failure seed cleanup is detached and bounded (documented).
  - `internal/providers/libvirt/cloudinit.go` (L8): meta-data is logged by length only.

### Changed
- `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go` (review L10): the `Clone` comment names the `configdrive2`-with-the-same-name exception.
- `docs/libvirt-clones.md`, `docs/vm-ownership.md`, `docs/cross-namespace-targets.md`, `docs/upgrading.md`, `README.md` (review M2, L4): **`create` on `VMClone` is read access to the source VM's data.** The clone's disk is a full copy of the source's, and on libvirt the `VMClone`'s inline user-data runs as root on its first boot. The upgrade row asks to review who can create `VMClone`s. These docs also cover the identity-pinning user-data keys, and the cross-namespace seed section is updated for R26.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/seed_reclaim.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/disk_dependents.go`: comments. The kept-because-a-clone-references-it seed path now matters only for single-host clones made before R26, and is kept for them.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`: `Clone` documents why no change is needed. PVE names the clone `target_name`, gives every `netN` a new MAC and regenerates the cloud-init drive. Its NoCloud `instance-id` is the SHA-1 of the generated user-data (with `hostname:`) and network data (with MACs). The documented exceptions are an out-of-band `cicustom` meta snippet, and `configdrive2` with an unchanged name.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/testdata/single_host_snapshot_clone_disk.golden.json`: regenerated. A single-host Clone now runs `isoinfo` before the copy and `mktemp`/`genisoimage`/`chmod` for the clone's seed, and defines the clone with its own seed; scenario `clone-customize-json-not-applied` renamed `clone-customize-hostname`.
- `docs/libvirt-clones.md`, `docs/vm-ownership.md`, `docs/upgrading.md`, `examples/advanced/vm-reconfigure-and-snapshot.yaml`: clones' cloud-init identity per provider. Covers what the seed holds, what re-runs on first boot, what does not change (`/etc/machine-id`, static network config), the customization fields applied, and the `isoinfo` requirement. Adds a behaviour-change row; the R24 row now concerns clones made before R26.

### Added
- `internal/providers/cloneidentity/cloneidentity_test.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_seed_test.go`, `internal/providers/vsphere/clone_identity_test.go`, and updates to `routed_clone_test.go`, `routed_cleanup_test.go`, `seed_reclaim_test.go`, `clone_target_test.go`, `clone_disk_format_test.go`, `snapshot_clone_disk_singlehost_test.go`, `domain_naming_create_test.go`, `main_test.go`:
  - Unit tests: instance-id derivation, meta-data and user-data rewrites, and customization parsing.
  - Single-host fake host (the fake ISO is now a tar a fake `isoinfo` reads back): the clone has its own seed with the new `instance-id` and target hostname; customization; a re-sent Clone renders an identical seed; deleting the source leaves the clone's seed; an unreadable source seed copies and defines nothing (Unavailable); a failed define removes the clone's seed.
  - Clustered: the clone's own seed and identity, read before the copy; identical seeds; an unreadable seed is retried before the copy.
  - A round trip with the REAL `genisoimage` and `isoinfo`, and `isoinfo` refusals.
  - vcsim: a clone of a cloud-init VM gets the new `guestinfo` identity; a source without cloud-init is unchanged. Unit tests for encodings and refusals.
  - The R24 tests now build a pre-R26 clone that shares its source's seed.
  - Review fixes:
    - M1: a seed read that fails after printing user-data (a fake `head`) leaves it in no error and no log line.
    - L1: an injected domain stays one meta-data value.
    - L2: anchored meta-data is refused.
    - L3: look-alike lines in multi-line values are never rewritten.
    - L4: identity-pinning keys are named, never their values.
    - L5 and L6: guestinfo keys in another case, and every encoding, round-trip.
    - L7: a seed failure is `Unavailable` with nothing defined, then the retry succeeds.
    - L9: inline user-data over 1 MiB is `InvalidArgument`.

### Why
Security review of #408 (R24): a single-host clone shared its source's seed ISO, which coupled the two VMs' lifecycles (R24's leak). Every libvirt and vSphere clone also booted with its source's cloud-init identity, so clone and source shared SSH host keys. That defeats SSH host-key authentication, a concern for regulated deployments.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-18 12:06] - vSphere import removes the history log; a Ready migration closes LandedDiskCleanup (rc2 R23)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/vsphere/s3import.go`: after an S3/NFS `ImportDisk`, the transient import VM's stub cleanup (#403) left vCenter's history log `<landing name>-<hex>.hlog` (about 300 bytes) in the landing folder: its suffix is random and it is in neither the derived stub names nor the VM's layout. `removeImportVMStubs` now lists the landing folder after the unregister and also removes a name that matches exactly `^<QuoteMeta(id)>-[0-9a-f]+\.hlog$` (`isImportVMHistoryLog`, `importVMHistoryLogNames`): only in that folder, never a `.vmdk` or a look-alike (`<id>.hlog.bak`, `<other>-abc.hlog`, `<id>-zz.hlog`), and only when the transient VM was verified as the import's (no stubs: nothing removed). Fail-soft as before: a folder that cannot be listed keeps the log, logged at `WARN`.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_landed_disk_cleanup.go`, `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`: a migration that reached `Ready` kept `LandedDiskCleanup=Unknown`/`LandedDiskMayExist` although its landed disk is the target VM's disk and is never deleted. The status write that marks the migration `Ready` now also records `LandedDiskCleanup=True` with the new reason `LandedDiskInUseByTarget` and a constant message, at the migration's generation (`markLandedDiskInUseByTarget`; no extra write). A migration that reached `Ready` under rc2 with the condition still `Unknown` is closed once by `handleReadyPhase` (`closeLandedDiskAtReady`), and the deletion path of a `Ready` migration that an older status still marks open records the same reason. Deleting a `Ready` migration sends no `DeleteLandedDisk` and holds nothing, with any `cleanupPolicy`.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/landed_disk_test.go`, `internal/controller/vmmigration_landed_disk_cleanup_test.go`, `internal/controller/vmmigration_landed_disk_cleanup_envtest_test.go`: vcsim test planting a `<id>-<hex>.hlog` next to look-alikes (removed vs kept, landed `.vmdk` kept), a matcher test against the anchored regular expression, a no-stubs test; controller unit tests for the Ready write, the rc2 close-once and the deletion of a `Ready` migration; an envtest spec in which a migration completes (`Ready` stored with `LandedDiskInUseByTarget`) and its deletion sends no `DeleteLandedDisk` and keeps the target VM.

- `docs/upgrading.md`: the landed-disk row names `LandedDiskInUseByTarget` and the history log; the leftovers bullet says rc2 imports still leave the `<landing name>-<hex>.hlog`.

## [2026-10-18 12:10] - Single-host libvirt Delete removes the VM's own cloud-init seed directory (rc2 R24)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/seed_reclaim.go` (new), `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`: a single-host `Delete` left the VM's seed directory `<staging>/virtrigaud-cloudinit-<domain>.<random>` (cloud-init.iso, user-data, meta-data) on the host when the VM and a clone of it were deleted at the same time. A single-host clone's CD-ROM references its source's seed, so the delete plan keeps a seed another domain still references; both deletes planned while the other domain was still defined, both kept it, and nothing removed it. After the undefine, `deleteExistingDomainChecked` (single-host only) now calls `reclaimSeedDirs`: the seed the definition referenced that the plan kept, and every seed directory named after exactly the deleted domain (`virtrigaud-cloudinit-<domain>.` plus the ten mktemp characters; `t2s3` never matches `t2s3c`), are removed once no defined domain references a file in them. A delete for a domain that is already absent (a retry) does the same via `cleanupOrphanedResources`. A seed found only by its name must be at least five minutes old (`orphanSeedMinAge`), on both paths; the seed the definition itself referenced is removed whatever its age. When a clone is the last domain to reference its source's seed, deleting the clone removes the SOURCE's seed (intended). Only real directories directly inside the staging directory are considered (`find -type d`, a symlink is never followed or removed), the name is matched in Go (no glob), references are read from each domain's persistent definition (`virsh dumpxml --inactive`) and compared with the candidate as canonical `realpath` paths, anything that cannot be checked (`find`, the domain list, a definition) keeps everything, and every failure is logged at `WARN` without failing the delete. The plan-time check of a seed another domain references now compares canonical paths too.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`: single-host `Create` and `Delete` now take the per-domain lock (`lockDomain`) that clustered Create/Delete/Clone and single-host Clone already take, so a re-sent `Create` of a name cannot interleave with the `Delete` of that name (it could bind the domain the delete is about to undefine, or lose the seed it just made to the delete's cleanup of leftovers). This also closes the same-name disk race between them. A call that waits for its whole budget is answered `domain busy` (retryable), nothing changed. Lock order: one domain lock per operation, then the landing-disk lock inside `Create`; nothing takes them in the opposite order.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/seed_reclaim_test.go` (new), `internal/providers/libvirt/domain_naming_create_test.go`: tests on the fake host: source and clone deleted together in both orders (fail before the fix), a seed the definition no longer names, the `t2s3` / `t2s3c` prefix pair, a symlink and a malformed-name decoy, the absent-domain sweep (age guard, still-referenced seed kept), fail-closed cases (`find` fails, the domain list or a definition cannot be read, a kept seed that is a symlink or outside the staging directory), a symlinked staging directory with references in another path form, glob and regexp characters in `TestIsOwnSeedDirName`, and the recreate race (a `Create` of a name waits for the `Delete` of it, then makes a complete VM). The fake virsh can now park an `undefine` to interleave two operations and fail `list --uuid`.

### Why
Found cleaning up the lab: deleting a migration-target VM and its clone together left the seed directory (which holds the VM's user-data) on the hypervisor.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-18 12:10] - ADR-0007 Addendum B (Proposed): migration into a clustered provider (R11, design only)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Added
- `docs/adr/0007-clustered-orchestrator-provider.md`: Addendum B (Status: Proposed), the P3 cold-path design for a `VMMigration` whose target Provider has `topology: cluster`, for the maintainer's sign-off. It covers:
  - B1: for clustered targets only, the migration creates its target VirtualMachine (with the #394 claim) at `Validating`, before any side effect on the source. The ordinary VirtualMachine scheduling path (R1, R4, admission under the assume lock, the checked `pendingHost` write) places it, and it is held `WaitingForImport` until the import is recorded. The import's host is pinned once an import was sent. A definite name conflict releases the host (the slice 2 rule). An unbound target is deleted on failure or retry.
  - B2: `ImportDiskRequest.target_host_id` (13) and the target VM UID, `withRoutedBudget` + `withHostConn`, the landing host's name check, A6.1's cross-host guard on the landed file, and the landing lock + `flock`. Landing on a shared pool is not required: host-local is the default.
  - B3: `s3` and `nfs` only. `pvc` is refused, with reasons. The host-side staged-image checks are reused. With `timeout(1)` on every host command, clustered can declare `resend_safe_import_backends: [s3, nfs]`.
  - B4: R6 markers and re-sends to the recorded host; R21-style typed outcomes on the routed path (`HOST_UNAVAILABLE` only before the first host command); a routed `DeleteLandedDisk` through a new optional `MigrationImportTarget.host` and `DeleteLandedDiskRequest.target_host_id` (4) with the cross-host in-use scan; a clustered `DeleteStagedDisk` (`target_host_id` 8 for nfs).
  - B5: the `supports_routed_import` (30) capability, the version matrix and the rollback behaviour. The Validating refusal stays for providers without the capability.
  - B6: four PR-sized slices with tests and a two-host shared-NFS lab plan.
  - B7: eight open questions.

  Single-host, vSphere and Proxmox targets keep today's order and requests, so the ADR-0008 soak window is unaffected. The Status block and A1 point at the addendum.
- `docs/adr/README.md`: the ADR-0007 index row links Addendum B (Proposed).

### Why
Rc2 roadmap item R11: a migration into a clustered libvirt Provider is refused at `Validating` because `ImportDisk` cannot reach a host. The design must compose with the scheduler (A2, A5), restore holds (A6), the target binding (#394), durable request markers (#402), typed outcomes (#405) and landed-disk cleanup (#403) before any code is written.

## [2026-10-17 13:28] - Single-host libvirt answers the failures of SnapshotCreate, ExportDisk and ImportDisk that its code can prove as definite (rc2 R21)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/call_outcome.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`: after #404 (R17), a pvc ImportDisk whose staged disk cannot be opened (a failure other than R17's typed refusals) is answered "not performed" instead of `Internal`, so the manager fails the attempt rather than holding it as an unknown outcome (`stagedSourceOpenOutcome`).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/call_outcome.go` (new), `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/s3export.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/nfs.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/s3import.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/conn.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/privileged_copy.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`: the manager's durable request markers (rc2 R6) hold a `VMMigration` or `VMSnapshot` for an operator on any failure that does not prove what the call did, and a single-host libvirt provider answered almost every failure as an untyped `codes.Unknown`, so ordinary failures (a `qemu-img` error, a missing source domain, a name already taken, a refusal before any side effect) were held. The single-host handlers now answer the failures their code proves, with a constant status text (host paths, commands, stderr and URLs go to the provider log only):
  - **Not performed** (`Unavailable` with `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`, the existing answer the manager reads as `contracts.IsNothingDone` and keeps out of the circuit breaker): a failing step that only reads or validates, or writes into a private directory that the call removes, before the call's one publishing step; and a host command that rewrites a whole disk (the s3 flatten, the import `qemu-img convert` / `dd`, the nfs export convert) only when it **ended with an exit status of its own** (1-127, request alive, a real process exit - not a dropped session, a signal or a stdout overflow), because a command whose session dropped may still run and a retry would start a second one. `SnapshotCreate`: the domain state, the disk-dependency check, the snapshot names or the disk sources cannot be read; `virsh snapshot-create-as --atomic` ended with an exit status of its own with one of libvirt's refusals before it executes anything (`cannot acquire state change lock`, `Requested operation is not valid`, `unsupported configuration`, `already exists`) and the snapshot names and `domblklist --details` sources, read again, are as before (only the first `error:` line of virsh's stderr is read) (libvirt can fail after the snapshot took effect, when it saves the domain's metadata last, so any other error text is unknown). `ExportDisk` s3: a check before the flatten, a flatten that ended on its own, any upload error before the flattened disk was read to its end (a credentials or bucket refusal, a 5xx, an unreachable service, a broken host stream; the S3 client sends an upload's completing call only after it has read its source to the end, which `errTrackingReader` records), while any upload error after that is unknown whatever the code (the client retries a completing call whose answer is lost, and the retry of an applied upload is answered `NoSuchUpload` or even `AccessDenied`); nfs: any check before the convert, and a convert that ended on its own; pvc: every failure (the export runs in the provider's own process). `ImportDisk` s3 and nfs: any read, check, download or stage before the convert, a convert / `dd` that ended on its own, and a rename that ended on its own; pvc: any failure up to and including the copy to the pool directory.
  - **Typed refusals**: an unusable storage configuration or request (`InvalidArgument`), a source domain that does not exist (`NotFound`), a snapshot name that is already taken (`AlreadyExists`; the single-host create now reads the snapshot names before it creates anything, so a snapshot found after a failed create is its own), a staged disk that is missing (`NotFound`), a local transport (`FailedPrecondition`). A contracts error from a step (`NotFound`, `InvalidSpec`, `Conflict`, `NotSupported`) is mapped to its status instead of crossing as `Unknown`.
  - **Still unknown** (the untyped answer, so the manager still holds): a host command that lost its connection or was killed (exit status 128 or above, or none) while it may still change something (a `virsh` that reports it lost libvirtd or timed out its keepalive included), a request whose deadline passed, an upload error once the source was read to its end, a rename whose result was lost, a snapshot create that failed with any other error text or left the snapshot or changed the disk sources, a failure after the pvc import's disk landed.
  - **A typed refusal keeps its own text** (never the wrapped errors' host paths or stderr).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/privileged_copy.go`: an export of a domain that is not on the host is `NotFound` instead of a retryable failure. `exportSourceOn` is shared, so a routed (clustered) export reaches it too; there `routedRPCError` already maps a `NotFound` to `codes.NotFound`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/virsh.go`: `snapshotExists` no longer reads a failed `snapshot-list` ("no domain snapshot") as the snapshot's absence; a list failure is an error.
- `internal/controller/provider_request_marker.go`, `vmsnapshot_controller.go`, `vmmigration_controller.go`, `vmmigration_request_marker.go`: a failure answering the manager's own automatic re-send (the marker was already on the object, no operator confirmed it) is never a definite outcome (`providerCallOutcomeKnownFor`; the rule of a VM Create's re-send): the marker is kept and the object held or settled. Without it a re-sent `SnapshotCreate` answered `AlreadyExists` (the first call's snapshot) failed the `VMSnapshot` and leaked the snapshot. A send on the operator's confirmation is a first send, as a confirmed VM Create is, so a definite failure fails the attempt; only an answer that contradicts the confirmation (a plain `Conflict`: a snapshot of that name exists, the landing name is in use) holds it again. A routed (clustered) `SnapshotCreate` is exempt from both: its provider adopts the earlier snapshot by request token, so its definite answers to a re-send stay definite (a routed re-send answered with a definite refusal fails the snapshot, as before).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`: the pvc export's unsupported format and bad destination are `InvalidSpec` (`InvalidArgument` on the wire).

### Changed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`: the single-host `SnapshotCreate` runs two more read-only commands before `snapshot-create-as` (`virsh snapshot-list --name`, `virsh domblklist --details`) and the same two after a failed create. The clustered create's command sequence is unchanged.
- The error texts of these three calls are now constant (the single-host golden `internal/providers/libvirt/testdata/single_host_snapshot_clone_disk.golden.json` is regenerated: only error texts and the extra `snapshot-list` changed).
- A host that cannot be reached during one of these three calls on a single-host libvirt provider is now "not performed": the attempt fails (as in rc1; the retry policy decides, it is not held) and the failure no longer counts toward the Provider's circuit breaker (other calls to the provider still do).
- The s3 and nfs imports may start the `default` storage pool before the private directory is made (idempotent, no disk): a failure after it is still "nothing landed".

### Added
- Tests:
  - `internal/providers/libvirt/call_outcome_test.go`, `call_outcome_transfer_test.go`, `call_outcome_helpers_test.go`: the helpers; every failure point of `SnapshotCreate`, `ExportDisk` (s3, nfs, pvc) and `ImportDisk` (s3, nfs, pvc) on a fake host, checked for its class (definite, typed refusal, unknown) and for a constant status text; the clustered create's command sequence.
  - `internal/transport/grpc/client_definite_outcome_test.go`: how the manager maps these answers (`IsNothingDone`, out of the breaker).
  - `internal/controller/provider_call_definite_outcome_test.go`: a typed definite libvirt failure fails the `VMMigration` (snapshot, export, import) or `VMSnapshot` attempt and clears the marker; an untyped one is held.
  - `internal/storage/s3fake/s3fake.go`: multipart uploads, `LoseNextComplete` (the completing call takes effect and its answer is lost), `AnswerRetriedCompleteWith`, `FailCompleteWith`, `CompleteRequests` (the tests count the completing calls, which relies on minio-go sending one only after the source was read to the end), S3 error codes by status.
  - `internal/controller/provider_call_definite_outcome_test.go`: an automatic re-send keeps the marker whatever it is answered; an operator-confirmed `SnapshotCreate`, `ExportDisk` or `ImportDisk` fails the attempt on a definite answer and holds on a plain `Conflict`; a routed re-send keeps its definite answers.
- `docs/provider-call-outcomes.md`, `docs/upgrading.md`: the classification table; the Limitations and the rc2 R6 upgrade row updated.

### Why
rc2 R6 made every failure without a definite outcome hold the object for an operator. On a single-host libvirt provider that turned ordinary, definite failures into holds because the provider never classified them. The failures whose outcome the code proves are now classified, and the rest stay held.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout (the libvirt provider image; until it is rolled, every libvirt failure of these calls stays held)
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-17 08:40] - pvc staging: staged files are opened beneath the PVC mount with no symbolic link followed (rc2 R17)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Security
- `internal/storage/stagedfile` (new package): `OpenRead`, `Create` and `Remove` resolve a path strictly beneath a trusted root with no symbolic link in any component: `openat2` with `RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS | RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS` (EAGAIN from a racing rename/mount is retried a bounded number of times, then the open fails closed), falling back (ENOSYS, or EPERM from a seccomp profile) to a per-component `openat(O_NOFOLLOW | O_DIRECTORY)` walk. `OpenRead` opens the final component `O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK | O_NOCTTY`, then `fstat`s the descriptor and accepts only a regular file with exactly one link (FIFOs, devices, sockets, directories and hard-linked files are refused). `Create` makes missing parents with `mkdirat` under the same walk, refuses a link or special file (or a directory, also when swapped in during the replace) at the name, replaces an earlier regular file by unlinking its name, and creates the new file with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW`. Errors are `*stagedfile.Error`: constant, path-free text (matching `ErrUnsafe` for a refusal, `fs.ErrNotExist` when missing) and a log-only `Detail()` (which says when the staging mount itself is missing). Non-Linux builds fail closed (`ErrUnsupported`).
- `internal/storage/pvc.go`: `PVCStorage.Upload`, `Download`, `Delete` and `GetMetadata` use `stagedfile` beneath the mount (they used `os.MkdirAll` / `os.Create` / `os.Open` / `os.Stat` / `os.Remove` on a joined path, so a link the tenant planted in the PVC — as the staged file or any parent directory — made the vSphere and libvirt `ImportDisk` read the provider pod's credentials, TLS key or ServiceAccount token into the tenant's target disk, and made `ExportDisk` write wherever the pod can write). Failures are `StorageError`s with constant messages (new `ErrorTypeUnsafePath` for a refusal); paths and system errors go to the provider log. New `storage.SplitPVCURL` (validated `pvc://<dns-1123-name>/<relative path>`) and `storage.PVCMountRoot`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/staged_source.go` (new), `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/conn.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/import_size_limit.go`: the pod-side (pvc) `ImportDisk` opens the staged disk once with `stagedfile` beneath `/mnt/migration-storage/<pvc>` and both the SSH copy to the host (`copyDiskToRemote` now takes the open reader) and the local private copy (`privateLocalImportCopy` now takes the open file) read that descriptor. Before, the SSH branch used `os.Open` (all links followed) and the local branch `O_NOFOLLOW` on the last component only, so a linked parent directory still worked. A refusal is `FailedPrecondition` with the constant `refused the staged disk: …` message; a missing disk is `NotFound`; a bad URL is `InvalidArgument` (constant messages, no paths). Only `pvc://` sources are accepted: the `file://` scheme (never sent by the manager) is removed, as it could import any regular file of the pod (e.g. `/proc/<pid>/environ`).

### Added
- Tests: `internal/storage/stagedfile/stagedfile_linux_test.go` (openat2 and the fallback walk: symlinked final component, symlinked parent at each depth, link to an `/etc` file, link inside the root, same-filesystem hard link, FIFO without blocking, `/dev/null`, directory, `..`/absolute paths, missing file; create through a planted link, a dangling link and a linked parent; remove through a linked parent), `internal/storage/stagedfile/stagedfile_race_linux_test.go` (ENOSYS/EPERM injected into openat2 take the fallback; EAGAIN is retried, then fails closed; a missing mount is named in the detail; a tenant goroutine swapping the migration directory and the staged file for links to the credentials while `OpenRead` / `Create` run, under both resolvers: no secret is read or written), `internal/storage/pvc_staged_file_test.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/staged_source_test.go` (an SSH `ImportDisk` that copies nothing to the host, and a local-connection `ImportDisk` that lands nothing in the pool, for a planted link; `file://` refused).

### Changed
- `examples/migration/README.md`: "Staged-file hardening (pvc backend)". `docs/upgrading.md`: a visible-but-not-breaking bullet (a link in the PVC's `vmmigrations/` tree, or a PVC filesystem reporting a link count other than 1, now fails a pvc migration; libvirt no longer accepts `file://` import sources).

### Why
The pvc staging backend mounts a tenant-writable PVC into the credentialed provider pods (read-only on the target after #399, which does not help: a link resolves in the pod's filesystem). A planted symbolic link let the tenant exfiltrate provider credentials through the imported disk, or redirect the export's write. NFS (libnfs resolves links inside the NFS namespace) and S3 (object keys) open no local tenant-writable path and are unchanged; the Proxmox provider rejects the pvc backend before any file access.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only
