## [2026-10-17 08:19] - A provider call whose result was lost, or whose outcome is unknown, is never re-sent blindly: durable requested-call markers (rc2 R6)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_request_marker.go` (new), `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`, `internal/controller/vmmigration_snapshot_task.go`, `internal/controller/provider_request_marker.go` (new): before a `VMMigration`'s `SnapshotCreate`, `ExportDisk` or `ImportDisk`, the migration records `SnapshotRequested` / `ExportRequested` / `ImportRequested=True`. The marker is written with the read `resourceVersion` as precondition, and nothing is sent if that write fails. The call's result, or a definite failure (`providerCallOutcomeKnown`: nothing done — request not sent, host unavailable, operation not performed — or a refusal: invalid spec, not found, conflict, owner or disk-size refusal), removes it in the same status write. A failure without a definite outcome — a deadline, `Unavailable` after the request was written, an unclassified error, and a routed `SnapshotCreate`'s "retry" — keeps the marker and never fails the migration (`afterUnknownMigrationCall`; rc1 failed the attempt and the retry policy re-sent the call while the first could still be writing). A phase that finds the marker without a result first re-reads the object live, so a stale cache is not taken for an unknown outcome. It then sends the call again only where that cannot duplicate anything:
  - a routed (clustered) `SnapshotCreate` for the same migration attempt (the provider adopts the snapshot by request token), at most once a minute and at most 10 times;
  - an `ExportDisk` / `ImportDisk` on a staging backend the provider reports re-send safe, once 35 minutes have passed since the marker (past the manager's 30-minute call deadline), at most 3 times.

  Automatic re-sends are counted in the marker's message; each send writes a strictly later attempt id. When it cannot be told yet whether a call may be re-sent (source VM, Provider or capabilities unreadable), the migration is re-checked every minute with no hold and no event.

  Otherwise the migration is held in its phase with `Ready=False` and reason `SnapshotOutcomeUnknown`, `ExportOutcomeUnknown` or `ImportOutcomeUnknown`. The hold has a constant message, one `Warning` event naming the attempt (and the snapshot name), and is written only on change. The operator's `virtrigaud.io/operation-outcome=not-performed@<attempt id>` sends the call again (and restarts the re-send count); it is audited with an `OperationOutcomeConfirmed` event, its field managers are logged, and it is removed before the call. A disk-size refusal of an import also persists the marker's removal. Metrics reason `provider-outcome-unknown`.
- `internal/controller/vmsnapshot_request_marker.go` (new), `internal/controller/vmsnapshot_controller.go`: a `VMSnapshot` records `SnapshotRequested` the same way, together with its binding, before its `SnapshotCreate`; the create's outcome replaces it. A `VMSnapshot` found in the initial phase with the marker:
  - routed: the create is re-sent (the provider adopts the snapshot made for its uid), paced;
  - single-host: held `Ready=False/SnapshotOutcomeUnknown` until the operator's confirmation — also when the create fails without a definite outcome (it is no longer failed).

  The confirmation annotation re-drives the snapshot through its update predicate.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_staging_cleanup.go`: a deleting migration whose `ExportDisk` outcome is unknown does not delete its nfs / s3 staged object until 35 minutes after the marker (a host-side copy outlives the cancelled call and could re-create it, unowned); force-delete still releases it.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_snapshot_token.go`: a clustered `SnapshotCreate` adopts the snapshot recorded with its request token only when `virsh domjobinfo` reports no job on the domain (libvirt lists a snapshot when its job starts and removes it if the job fails); while a job runs it answers retryable `Unavailable` (VM_OPERATION_FAILED); an unreadable job state is an error.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/import_stage.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/s3import.go`: the s3 stage is published (`mv -T`) only when exactly the object's reported size arrived (`importStageWriteExactly`): a cancelled call closed the node's stdin, `cat` saw end of input and a truncated stage was published (pre-existing). `cleanupNodeFile` is bounded (2 min). The stage script's comment no longer claims a hang-up stops it.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_status_write.go`: `forgetMigrationLongOps` logs every unrecorded result it evicts at `Error`, with the provider's ids (review L1 of #388). `pendingMigrationResult` keeps them.

### Added
- `proto/provider/v1/provider.proto` (bindings regenerated), `internal/providers/contracts/capabilities.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/client.go`, `sdk/provider/capabilities/capabilities.go` (`Manager.SetResendSafeExportBackends` / `SetResendSafeImportBackends`, `Builder.ResendSafeExportBackends` / `ResendSafeImportBackends`): `GetCapabilitiesResponse.resend_safe_export_backends` (27) and `resend_safe_import_backends` (28). These are the staging backends on which a re-sent `ExportDisk` / `ImportDisk`, after the earlier call's deadline, replaces what the earlier call wrote and never makes a second artifact. They are declared only where proven (per-provider audit):
  - `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go`: s3 and nfs both ways;
  - `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`: single-host export s3, import pvc+s3+nfs; clustered export s3+nfs;
  - `internal/providers/proxmox/capabilities.go`: s3 both ways (the nfs import's node script copies to completion and publishes the stage after a cancelled call: not re-send safe);
  - mock: none.
- Tests:
  - `internal/controller/vmmigration_request_marker_test.go`, `internal/controller/vmsnapshot_request_marker_test.go`: a failed or conflicting marker write sends nothing; restart after the call (new reconciler: in-memory state dropped) holds, or re-sends with the same token or after the settle time; operator confirmation; earlier-attempt marker; stale cache; a failure clears the marker; L1 eviction log.
  - `internal/controller/vmmigration_request_marker_review_test.go`: deadline / dropped connection / unclassified failures keep the marker and hold (or settle), nothing-done and refusals fail; a routed "retry" keeps the marker; strictly increasing attempt ids and the re-send count through `markMigrationRequested`; the caps; the quiet undecidable path; the staged-object delete waiting for an unknown export; the confirmation's field managers; the outcome classification. `internal/controller/vmsnapshot_clustered_test.go`, `vmsnapshot_request_marker_test.go`: a single-host create without a definite outcome is held, a nothing-done one fails; routed re-send cap; quiet undecidable path.
  - `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_snapshot_token_test.go` (fake virsh `domjobinfo`): adopted only with no job; retryable while one runs; error when unreadable. `internal/providers/proxmox/import_stage_script_test.go` (real shell): a short s3 copy is never published and an earlier stage is kept.
  - `internal/controller/provider_request_marker_envtest_test.go` (envtest): held export plus confirmation; settled re-send; a real `Conflict` sends nothing; held single-host `VMSnapshot` plus confirmation.
  - Per-provider capability tests in `internal/providers/{vsphere,libvirt,proxmox,mock}/resend_safe_capabilities_test.go`, the SDK builder and the transport client.

### Changed
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_pending_result_test.go`, `internal/controller/vmmigration_update_status_test.go`: the failing-write fakes let the marker write through, so the call is still sent and its result write fails.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/s3import.go`: comment — the landing name is `<ns>_<vm>-migrated`.
- `docs/provider-call-outcomes.md` (new), `docs/README.md`, `docs/upgrading.md` (behaviour row), `examples/migration/README.md`.

### Why
This was a known limitation in rc1. Between a `SnapshotCreate`, `ExportDisk` or `ImportDisk` and the write of its result, a manager restart or leader change lost the result, and the new leader sent the call again. On vSphere and the mock that took a second snapshot of the live source VM. A call that timed out failed the attempt and was re-sent by the retry policy while a host-side copy could still be writing. #388 made the result durable within one process only. This applies the `CreateRequested` / `CloneRequested` pattern (#395) to these calls, re-sending only where a per-provider audit shows the re-send replaces rather than duplicates (review and audit of #402 included).

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-17 08:16] - Reconfigure never resizes the root disk for spec.disks; vSphere waits for a power-off instead of retrying a change the VM cannot take (rc2 R5)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/vsphere/reconfigure.go` (new), `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go`: `Reconfigure` grew the FIRST disk (the root disk) to `spec.disks[0].sizeGiB`. It now never touches the root disk (the VMClass `spec.diskDefaults.size` is not applied by `Reconfigure`, as before) and grows a `spec.disks` entry's own additional disk only — the one disk recorded with the entry's name. Left alone: an entry with no disk recorded under its name (added after creation, adopted VMs, and every disk rc1 or earlier recorded without a name — never matched by position; logged at INFO), and — logged at WARN, since the call still succeeds — a name used by two entries or recorded on two disks, a recorded disk missing from the VM, a delta disk (snapshots, linked clone) and a physical-mode RDM. A smaller `spec.disks` size is refused with `InvalidArgument` before anything changes; a size of 0 (withheld by the disk-size limit) leaves the disk. CPU, memory and disk edits go in one `ReconfigVM_Task`.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/reconfigure.go`: before changing a VM that is not powered off, `Reconfigure` reads `config.cpuHotAddEnabled` / `cpuHotRemoveEnabled` / `memoryHotAddEnabled` / `hotPlugMemoryLimit` and the disk's controller and sharing, and when vCenter cannot apply the change now (no CPU/memory hot-add, fewer vCPUs without hot-remove, less memory, above the hot-plug limit, a shared-bus or multi-writer disk grow, any change of a suspended VM) refuses the whole request before changing anything with `FailedPrecondition` + `RECONFIGURE_NEEDS_POWER_OFF` instead of sending a task vCenter fails (rc1 lab finding V1: retried indefinitely). A CPU count that is not a multiple of the cores per socket is refused with `InvalidArgument`. A `ReconfigVM_Task` vCenter refuses to start (a SOAP or vim fault such as `TaskInProgress`, `InvalidState`, `InvalidPowerState`) or fails is answered `Unknown` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` with a constant message (the fault is logged), so it never counts toward the per-Provider circuit breaker; a failure to reach vCenter and a `NotAuthenticated` session fault still count.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/reconfigure.go` (new), `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`: `Reconfigure` sent every `spec.disks` size to `scsi0` (the root disk) and, after a disk grow, returned before sending the CPU/memory change while reporting success. It now changes no disk — the Proxmox `Create` attaches no `spec.disks`, and the VMClass size is not applied by `Reconfigure` — and always sends the CPU/memory change; a config update PVE fails is answered `Unknown` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` with a constant message. Validated against `pvefake` only.

### Added
- `internal/providers/contracts/errors.go`: `ReconfigureNeedsPowerOffReason` (`RECONFIGURE_NEEDS_POWER_OFF`), `ErrReconfigureNeedsPowerOff`, `IsReconfigureNeedsPowerOff`.
- `internal/transport/grpc/client.go`: maps `FailedPrecondition` + `RECONFIGURE_NEEDS_POWER_OFF` to a retryable error marked `ErrReconfigureNeedsPowerOff` (never counted toward the circuit breaker).
- `internal/k8s/conditions.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_reconfigure_result.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`: `Reconfiguring=False`, reason `ResizePendingPowerOff`, with a constant message (covering hot-add, the hot-plug memory limit, memory decreases, shared/multi-writer disks and suspended VMs), for that refusal; `status.currentResources` is untouched, it is re-sent on the per-VM reconfigure backoff and at once after a spec change (so `spec.powerState: Off` applies it), and it keeps the clustered memory ceiling from being lowered, like a failure.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/post_create.go`, `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go`: an additional disk's `spec.disks` name is recorded with it (`virtrigaud.disk.additional.<N>.name`, in the same task that attaches it, cleared on create like the file record).
- `internal/providers/proxmox/pvefake/server.go`: config keys a test seeds (`scsi1`, `boot`, ...) are served, and a resize rewrites the disk's `size=`.
- Tests: vcsim multi-disk VM (each size to its own disk, name matching after reorder/removal, name-less records and repeated names left alone, unattached entry, shrink refusal, task and start faults (TaskInProgress, InvalidState, InvalidPowerState, SOAP) answered `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` while transport and NotAuthenticated errors are not, root disk never grown by the VMClass size, hot-add on/off/remove, suspended VM, cores per socket), `planReconfigure` unit tests (delta, physical RDM, shared bus, multi-writer), pvefake `scsi0`+`scsi1` (no disk resized, CPU/memory applied, config failure answered `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`), transport mapping and breaker exclusion, controller unit tests and an envtest spec for the persisted `ResizePendingPowerOff` condition. The vSphere and Proxmox wrong-disk regression tests fail on `main`.

### Changed
- `internal/providers/vsphere/disk_capacity_test.go`: `TestReconfigure_WithheldDiskSizeIsNoOp` asserted the old behaviour (a `spec.disks` size growing the root disk); it now asserts the root disk is never grown by `Reconfigure`.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/reconfigure_disk_test.go`: rewritten for the new behaviour.
- `internal/controller/disk_size_limit.go`: comments; the Proxmox "zero every spec.disks size once one is withheld" rule is kept for Providers still running an older image.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go`: `GetCapabilities` documents that online reconfigure is per VM (hot-add); `supports_reconfigure_online` stays true (as libvirt's, same per-VM meaning) and `supports_honest_reconfigure` stays false.
- `docs/reconfigure-results.md` (new sections "Which disk a size goes to" and "vSphere: changes a running VM cannot take"), `docs/upgrading.md` (two rows, a rollback caveat).

### Why
A security review found that vSphere and Proxmox `Reconfigure` grew the root disk with an additional disk's size, and the rc1 lab (V1) found that a CPU/memory change of a running vSphere VM without hot-add was retried forever while reported as a plain provider failure.

### Impact
- [x] Breaking change — on Proxmox, a `spec.disks` size no longer grows `scsi0` and nothing replaces it in this release; on vSphere, a `spec.disks` size below its disk's now fails the `Reconfigure` (CPU/memory included) on VMs created by this release; alerting on `Reconfiguring` sees the new reason `ResizePendingPowerOff`.
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-17 08:30] - vSphere: a finder per call instead of one shared; libvirt: no fixed /tmp files on the host (rc2 R8, R9)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/vsphere/datacenter_finder.go` (new), `server.go`, `image.go`, `image_identity.go`, `s3import.go`, `export_cleanup.go`, `disk_guard.go`, `datastore_helper.go`, `template_source.go`, `vm_ownership.go`: the provider kept one shared `*find.Finder` and re-scoped it with `SetDatacenter` at the start of about twenty RPC paths. A govmomi `Finder` is not safe for concurrent use (`SetDatacenter` rewrites it and it fills a folder cache lazily), so concurrent RPCs raced on it (`go test -race` reports it), and a path that used the finder before scoping it ran against whatever the previous RPC had left behind (#390 was one such ordering bug). The shared finder and `Provider.finder` are gone. `Provider.dcFinder` returns a finder of the caller's own, already scoped to the default datacenter, and that datacenter; every RPC path takes one and passes it to the helpers that need it (`resolveVMFolder`, `createVirtualMachine`, `resolveDatastoreFromStoragePod`, `lookupTemplate`/`templateCandidates`, `findPreparedTemplate`, `resolveImportDatastore`/`resolveImportPlacement`, `removeExportCloneFiles`, `resolveImageFolder`; `imagePlacement` carries the finder the OVA importer uses). Behaviour is otherwise unchanged, including the error an RPC returns when the default datacenter cannot be resolved (no datacenter, or several and no default).
- `internal/providers/vsphere/datacenter_finder.go`: finding the default datacenter is a vCenter round trip, so the datacenter reference is cached on the `Provider` for 60 seconds and for the current vCenter client only (a reconnect in `Validate` builds a new client and the entry misses). A finder or inventory call that fails with "not found" (`find.NotFoundError` or `ManagedObjectNotFound`) drops the entry (`noteInventoryError`, called after each finder lookup), so a renamed or re-created datacenter costs at most the one failed call. Each caller gets its own copy of the object; a failed lookup is never cached. The RPCs that address a VM by managed object ID keep the datacenter lookup as a guard that only fails on a cache miss.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/storage.go`: `createDefaultStoragePool` wrote the pool XML to the fixed host path `/tmp/default-pool.xml` before `virsh pool-define`. Two concurrent calls on one host (two providers sharing it, or a clustered fan-out) overwrote each other's file, and a fixed name in a shared `/tmp` can be pre-created or linked elsewhere by anything on the host. The XML now goes to `virsh pool-define /dev/stdin` over stdin (as `vol-create` already does): no file is made, so there is nothing to clean up.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`: `syncPersistentXML` (the persistent-definition sync after a start or reboot) had the same flaw with `/tmp/<domain>-sync.xml`, which a failed define also left behind; it now re-defines from stdin (`virsh define /dev/stdin`). It also now connects with the provider's own `-c` URI like every other call (the file-based form ran `virsh define <path>` without one on a non-SSH transport).

### Changed
- `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go`: `createVSphereClient` returns `(*govmomi.Client, error)` (it no longer builds a finder). Tests use `testFinder` / `testDatacenter` (`datacenter_finder_test.go`).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/testdata/single_host_power_reconfigure.golden.json`: the single-host Power sequences that sync the persistent XML now end in `define /dev/stdin` where they had `define /tmp/<domain>-sync.xml` and `rm -f /tmp/<domain>-sync.xml`.

### Added
- Tests: `internal/providers/vsphere/datacenter_finder_test.go` (a finder and a datacenter copy per call; ambiguous datacenter is an error and not cached; cache rules: client, TTL, copy; expiry and client swap through `dcFinder` with a clock seam; not-found invalidation; `TestDCFinder_ConcurrentRPCs` runs Describe, ListVMs, ImportDisk target resolution and an ImagePrepare template lookup concurrently and fails under `-race` on the previous code, where the shared finder's `SetDatacenter` races); `internal/providers/libvirt/host_tempfile_test.go` (pool define and persistent-XML sync read stdin whole, concurrent calls share no file, a failed define leaves none, the old fixed paths are never created or touched, the `-c` URI of the persistent-XML sync for system, session, `qemu+tcp`, `qemu+tls` and `?socket=` URIs).

### Why
Two rc2 hardening items: the vSphere provider shared mutable state between concurrent RPCs, and the libvirt provider staged XML in predictable files in the hypervisor's shared `/tmp`. Neither changes what an operator configures. Not covered: the pod-local `/tmp/<export>.<fmt>` and `/tmp/<disk>-download.img` files of the libvirt PVC export/import (they live in the provider pod's own `/tmp`, not on a hypervisor host).

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-17 08:05] - Provider pods mount only the migration PVCs a live VMMigration references (rc2 R15)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Security
- `internal/controller/provider_migration_storage.go` (new), `internal/controller/provider_controller.go`: provider pods, which hold the hypervisor credentials, no longer mount every PVC in their namespace labelled `virtrigaud.io/component=migration-storage`. `discoverMigrationStorage` mounts a PVC only into the source Provider (the source VM's own, `migrationSourceProviderRef`) and the target Provider of a `VMMigration` in the Provider's namespace that uses the pvc backend, records the PVC in `status.storagePVCName` and is in flight (not deleting, not `Ready`, not `Failed` with no retry left). The PVC must carry the label (now a necessary-but-not-sufficient consent marker) and be either the PVC the migration created or the one `spec.storage.pvc.name` names, as long as it isn't another `VMMigration`'s (`migrationPVCReferenceError`). Before this, anyone who could create a PVC in a Provider's namespace could attach arbitrary storage read-write to every provider pod there.
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/vmmigration_types.go` (new `status.storagePVCUID`, CRDs regenerated), `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go` (`ensureMigrationPVC`), `internal/controller/provider_migration_storage.go` (`migrationCreatedPVC`): a migration identifies the PVC it created by the UID the API server returned for its own `Create`. It records that UID at once (`recordMigrationResult`, conflict-retried; a PVC whose UID can't be recorded is deleted again under a UID precondition), and only that object is accepted, mounted or deleted. A `<name>-storage` PVC carrying a forged controller `ownerReference` to the migration (its name and UID are readable) is refused: it fails `Validating` with `errMigrationPVCNotOwned` if it was there first (also on a lost `Create` race, `AlreadyExists`), and if it replaces the real PVC it is never mounted or deleted. The existence check reads live, so the cache can't hide the migration's own PVC. A migration whose PVC an older manager created has no recorded UID; for it, and only under the `<name>-storage` name, the controller `ownerReference` is still accepted.
- `internal/controller/provider_migration_storage.go`: a PVC that is being deleted, `Lost`, or `Pending` is not mounted. The one exception is a `Pending` PVC on a `WaitForFirstConsumer` StorageClass, which is mounted while its migration is `Validating` (where it waits for the mount, within the mount budget). So a PVC that never binds can't stall a provider rollout, or take down a `Recreate` (vSphere, clustered) Provider. If the StorageClass can't be read (namespace-scoped install), a `Pending` PVC is mounted during `Validating`, bounded by the mount budget.
- `internal/controller/provider_migration_storage.go`: a `Failed` migration that will be retried keeps its mount on a Provider only while a Running, Ready pod of that Provider carries the PVC (`providerPodCarriesPVC`). That pod is the proof the mount worked. Otherwise, for example with a `Bound` but `ReadWriteOnce` or node-pinned volume the pod can't attach, the mount is dropped, so the PVC can't keep a `Recreate` Provider down between retries. The retry mounts it again (one extra roll).
- `internal/controller/provider_migration_storage.go`: a Provider that is only a migration's target mounts its PVC read-only (imports only read the staged disk); the source mounts it read-write.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go` (`handleDeletion`): deleting a `VMMigration` deletes `status.storagePVCName` only when it is the PVC the migration created (`migrationCreatedPVC`, with a UID precondition on the delete). A user's PVC named in `spec.storage.pvc.name`, a squat, or any other PVC the migration didn't create is never deleted. It is unmounted and left for its owner, with a Normal `MigrationPVCRetained` event. Before, the manager deleted whatever PVC the migration had recorded, so anyone who could create and delete `VMMigration`s could have the manager delete a PVC they could not delete themselves.

### Changed
- `internal/controller/provider_controller.go`, `internal/controller/provider_migration_storage.go`: discovery runs once per Deployment render, sorted by PVC name. A read error (`errMigrationStorageDiscovery`) leaves the Deployment as it is and is retried after 30s without a reconcile error (`migrationStorageDiscoveryFailed`). Before, the Deployment was rendered without migration storage, unmounting it mid-migration. A Provider whose Deployment exists keeps its runtime phase and conditions. Without a Deployment, `ProviderRuntimeReady=False` gets reason `MigrationStorageDiscoveryFailed` and a constant message. Metrics reason: `migration-storage-discovery-failed`.
- `internal/controller/provider_migration_storage.go`, `internal/controller/provider_controller.go`: watches.
  - A PVC event (filtered to phase, deletion, label and controller changes) for a labelled PVC, or for one a migration records, re-renders every Provider in its namespace.
  - A `VMMigration` event re-renders its source and target Providers while it is in flight and its source VM resolves. When the migration is deleted, no longer in flight, or its source VM is gone, every Provider in its namespace is re-rendered instead, so a former source never keeps a stale read-write mount (or a Terminating PVC) until resync. Rendering is idempotent.
  - The `VMMigration` predicate fires when the migration records its PVC or its UID, enters or leaves `Validating` or `Failed`, finishes, or is deleted.
- `internal/controller/provider_migration_storage.go`: volume names stay `migration-<pvc>` when that is a valid DNS label; otherwise `migration-<prefix>-<16 hex of SHA-256>`. `assignMigrationVolumeNames` de-duplicates at render time: a name already used (a PVC literally named like another PVC's hashed name) falls back to a 53-hex hash-only name, and a mount that still clashes is left out and logged. The Deployment is never invalid.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`: `ensureMigrationPVC` fails `Validating` when the PVC can't be used (named PVC without the label or belonging to another `VMMigration`, or a `<name>-storage` PVC this migration didn't create) instead of waiting out the mount budget. Changing `spec.storage.pvc` after the PVC is recorded fails the migration with the constant `errMigrationPVCSpecChanged` (in `ensureMigrationPVC` and `generateStorageURL`), and the PVC is not mounted. The mount budget (`migrationMountWaitStart`) starts at the latest of the PVC's creation, the migration's start and its last retry, so an older named PVC, which is now mounted only once referenced, isn't timed out at once. Created PVCs use the label constants.
- `internal/controller/provider_controller.go` (kubebuilder RBAC markers), `config/rbac/role.yaml` (regenerated), `charts/virtrigaud/templates/manager-rbac.yaml` (ClusterRole): the manager may `get` `storage.k8s.io/storageclasses` and never lists or watches them. The kustomize role also gains `pods` get/list/watch, which the chart already granted and the migration controller already needed.
- `examples/migration/README.md` (new "PVC staging backend (legacy): what the provider pods mount" section, including when pods are rolled and the read-write/read-only flip of a shared named PVC), `examples/vmmigration-basic.yaml`, `docs/upgrading.md` (behaviour row).

### Added
- Tests: `internal/controller/provider_controller_migration_test.go` (rewritten), covering:
  - source rw / target ro / bystander none; labelled-but-unreferenced PVC; deleted and deleting migration
  - `Ready`, terminal, and retry-pending `Failed` with and without a Ready pod carrying the PVC
  - ownership, label and named-PVC cases, including a forged-`ownerReference` squat and the legacy fallback
  - cross-namespace migration and PVC
  - Bound / Pending WFFC / Pending Immediate / no class / missing class / Lost / deleting PVC / unreadable StorageClass
  - sorting and merge; read errors and `migrationStorageDiscoveryFailed`; volume naming and collision de-duplication
  - watch mappings (source VM gone, migration deleted, labelled and referenced PVCs) and predicates; mount-budget start
  - `ensureMigrationPVC`: refusals, UID recording, spec change; `handleDeletion`: own, legacy, squat, user-named and another migration's PVC
- `internal/controller/provider_migration_storage_envtest_test.go` (envtest), covering:
  - the Provider controller in a manager mounts the referenced PVC rw on the source and ro on the target, never the labelled rogue PVC, and drops it when the migration is `Ready`
  - foreign-namespace, unowned, unlabelled and deleted-migration PVCs; WFFC vs Immediate pending PVCs
  - deleting a migration deletes the PVC it created and leaves a PVC named in `spec.storage.pvc.name` with a `MigrationPVCRetained` event
  - a forged-`ownerReference` squat fails `Validating`; the migration's own PVC is created and its UID recorded against a real apiserver; a squat that replaces it is never mounted or deleted

### Why
Security review of #394: the migration-storage label was not reserved, so any principal able to create a PVC in a Provider's namespace could have it mounted read-write into the credentialed provider pods, or stall their rollout with a PVC that never binds. A mount now needs a live `VMMigration` that references the PVC, on the Providers that migration uses. The PVC a migration created is identified by the UID from its own create, not by a forgeable `ownerReference`. Deleting a migration no longer deletes a PVC it did not create.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-17 08:05] - VirtualMachine status.phase is derived on every status write; go-libvirt upstream race documented and skipped under -race (rc2 R10, R16)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_phase.go` (new), `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_reconfigure_result.go`: `VirtualMachine.status.phase` (the `PHASE` printer column) was empty on healthy running VMs, because only a few paths assigned it. It is now a pure function of the VM's state (`derivePhase`): `Deleting` (deletion timestamp, also while the delete is held), `Failed` (a `Ready=False` hold: `VMNotOwned`, `OwnerStampUnreadable`, `ProviderUnavailable`, `VMIsImageArtifact`, `CreateOutcomeUnknown`, `DeleteBlocked`, `ProviderRefMismatch`, `PlacementTopologyMismatch`, `ConsumerNotAllowed`, `VMMissingOnHost`, `RestorePending`, `OwnDomainOnAnotherHost`; for a VM with no id also the restore holds on `Placed`/`Provisioning` (`RestorePending`, `OwnDomainOnAnotherHost`, `UniquenessCheckFailed`, `ProviderLacksListOwnerFilter`); for a VM with no id also a refused or backing-off create; an `Unknown` power state), `Pending` / `Provisioning` for a VM with no id (create requested, task recorded, clustered pending host, or `Provisioning=True`), `Reconfiguring` (a resize in flight; a change pending a restart is not), and `Running` / `Stopped` by `status.powerState` (`Suspended` counts as `Running`). The existing direct `Phase =` assignments are removed.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go` (`updateStatus`), `virtualmachine_create_marker.go` (pre-create marker), `virtualmachine_create_record.go` (post-create record), `virtualmachine_clustered.go` (pending-host and excluded-host writes), `virtualmachine_clustered_restore.go` (re-attach): every VirtualMachine status write derives the phase from the status it writes (`applyDerivedPhase`), so it changes in the same write as the fact it summarizes and never causes a write by itself. `handleDeletion` writes `Deleting` once, with a status merge patch of the phase alone and an optimistic lock (`markDeleting`; a lost race retries after a second on a fresh read, and the caller's resourceVersion is never refreshed over content it has not seen). The hold paths that write only when a hold changed the status (`statusDiffers`) derive the phase before comparing, so a VM already held before the upgrade gets its phase. `Unknown` power state maps to `Failed` as the current observation (documented, not sticky).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/golibvirt.go`: the keepalive loop probes the client `connect` returned (`callOn`) and drops that client when the probe fails (`forgetClient`), after evicting it, so the next tick dials a fresh one (evict and forget are two steps, not one atomic one). Reason: after the go-libvirt race below, a client can report `IsConnected()` true for a dead transport, and the holder would hand it out indefinitely. Only a client whose probe failed is dropped, and only if it is still the published one.

### Added
- `docs/vm-status-phase.md` (new): the values, the rule that derives them, the `Ready` reasons that mean `Failed`, upgrade notes. `docs/README.md` index entry; `docs/upgrading.md` behaviour-change entry.
- Tests: `internal/controller/virtualmachine_phase_test.go` (the mapping table, no combination yields an empty phase, the central status write stores the derived phase), `internal/controller/virtualmachine_phase_envtest_test.go` (envtest: a created VM has a phase from its first status write and reaches `Running`, then `Stopped`, then `Deleting`; unchanged reconciles write nothing), `internal/controller/virtualmachine_phase_test.go` also covers the real restore-hold writers, the derive-before-compare upgrade case and a stale-resourceVersion `markDeleting`; `internal/providers/libvirt/golibvirt_test.go` (`forgetClient`).

### Changed
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/virtualmachine_types.go`, `config/crd/bases/infra.virtrigaud.io_virtualmachines.yaml`: the `status.phase` field description documents the derivation. The enum is unchanged, so no CRD ordering applies.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/golibvirt.go`, `golibvirt_test.go`, `golibvirt_race_test.go`, `golibvirt_norace_test.go` (new): `TestGolibvirtHolder_ConcurrentAccess_Race` is skipped when built with the race detector (`knownUpstreamRace`, a race-tagged constant). Cause: in `github.com/digitalocean/go-libvirt`, `(*Libvirt).ConnectToURI` starts `go l.waitAndDisconnect()` and then writes `l.disconnected` without synchronization, while `waitAndDisconnect` reads it; unfixed in the module's main branch (checked against `v0.0.0-20261013170128-efbbdf578ac8`, newer than the pinned `v0.0.0-20260814190004-1a83157e1858`), so no dependency bump. The package doc has a new "Known upstream race" section: what can trigger it from this package, why only an unpublished client or a transport that dies in the microseconds before the assignment is affected, and the self-heal above. The test still runs without `-race`.

### Why
`PHASE` was empty on healthy VMs, which made `kubectl get vm` useless for a quick health read and left automation reading conditions instead. The go-libvirt race is in a third-party module and made `go test -race` fail on a loaded machine; the test is skipped under `-race` until the upstream fix, and the one production consequence found is bounded.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-17 07:55] - ADR-0012 (Accepted): retiring the Proxmox legacy unstamped-name rule (rc2 R14)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Added
- `docs/adr/0012-proxmox-legacy-unstamped-name-rule.md`: design record (Status: **Accepted**, 2026-10-17) for security review finding M2 of #393. The single-host Proxmox owner check accepts an unstamped VM named like its owner. This keeps VMs working after an upgrade if they were created by v0.3.11 or earlier, adopted before #392, or cloned by a pre-rc2 manager. It also means a PVE principal with `VM.Allocate` can plant a look-alike at a freed VMID and pass every owner check. Decision:
  - **(A) A confirmed-stamp latch.** The manager records `status.ownerStamp.confirmedID` once `Describe` reports `owner_check=STAMPED`. From then on it sends `ObjectIdentity.require_owner_stamp`. Other `ObjectIdentity` uses ignore the field. Proto field numbers are assigned at implementation time.
  - **(B) One-time stamping of legacy VMs.** Legacy VMs are stamped once through the existing compare-and-swap `TransferOwner`. This is on by default, with a per-Provider opt-out (`virtrigaud.io/stamp-legacy-vms: "false"`). Each VM stamped gets one Normal audit event, and stamping is paced per Provider.
  - **Phase 1 timing.** Phase 1 targets **v0.4.1**, or v0.5.0 without a PVE lab. Validation on a real PVE cluster is its release gate.
  - **Dropping the rule.** The name rule is dropped by default in v0.5.0, gated on the unconfirmed-VMs gauge reaching 0. A one-minor escape hatch remains until v0.6.0.
  - **Rejected and scheduled.** A creation-time cutoff and the status quo are rejected. The `meta` ctime binding spike (Option E) is scheduled with the PVE lab's return.
  - **Accepted risk.** The forged-stamp residual is accepted for v0.4.0.
  - **Other providers.** vSphere and libvirt have no name rule and need no change.
- `docs/adr/README.md`: index row for ADR-0012.

### Changed
- `docs/vm-ownership.md` (Proxmox Limits): adds the v0.4.0 mitigation. Do not grant `VM.Allocate` on the pools and paths VirtRigaud's VMs live in to principals other than VirtRigaud's Provider tokens and its administrators. The entry also links ADR-0012 and its v0.4.1 plan. A new Limits entry records the accepted risk that a stamp can be copied by someone who knows the UID and holds `VM.Config.Options`.

### Why
M2 of the #393 security review touches both load-bearing contracts (proto and CRD status), so it needed a maintainer decision before any change. The fix is deferred to v0.4.1 behind real-PVE validation. v0.4.0 ships the ACL guidance and records the accepted risk.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only

## [2026-10-17 07:55] - Release notes: v0.4.0-rc2, "Changes since v0.4.0-rc1" (Wave 1)

## [2026-10-17 06:50] - Single-host VMClone targets are stamped with their owner; a re-sent Clone re-binds (rc2 R4)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/controller/vmclone_controller.go`, `internal/controller/vmclone_clustered.go`: a single-host `VMClone` now creates its target `VirtualMachine` before the `Clone` RPC, as a clustered one does (`ensureCloneTarget`, renamed from `ensureClusteredCloneTarget`), records its UID (`status.targetUID`) and sends it in `CloneRequest.target_vm`. The pre-clone existence check accepts only the target this clone created. A target carrying this clone's marker whose UID was never recorded (the manager stopped between its Create and the record) is recorded before any `Clone`. A clone whose own target was deleted after a `Clone` was requested fails with `TargetConflict` and is never sent again for a new target (the guard depends on `CloneRequested` only); `bindTargetVM` never re-creates a target whose UID is recorded. A failed single-host clone removes the unbound target it created (`removeFailedCloneTarget`, renamed from `removeFailedClusteredTarget`) unless the provider reported a cloned VM (`status.targetVMID`) or a `Clone` of unknown outcome is on record, in which case the target is kept for an administrator.
- `internal/controller/vmclone_target_stamp.go` (new): before a `Clone` to a provider that reports `supports_owner_rebind` (`providerRebindsOwnedVM`), the `VMClone` records `CloneRequested=True` with a resourceVersion precondition (nothing is sent without it); it is removed once the provider accepts the `Clone`, and dropped in the same write when the answer proves a first attempt made nothing. A `Clone` on record is never sent to a provider that does not report the capability (Failed, `CloneOutcomeUnknown`, target kept); nothing is sent while capabilities can't be read. Held attempts (`CloneRetrying`, `CloneOutcomeUnknown`, one streak) are paced by an in-process `cloneAttemptPacer`, whatever triggers the reconcile. `handleSingleHostCloneError`: an `AlreadyExists` to a first attempt fails the clone with `Ready=False/ProviderConflict` and the constant `cloneTargetConflictMessage` (the provider's answer in a Warning event); an outcome-unknown failure, or any failure answering a re-send, holds the clone (`Pending`, `Ready=False/CloneOutcomeUnknown`, constant `cloneOutcomeUnknownMessage`, one Warning event) and sends the `Clone` again with the blocked-VM backoff; `CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED` is held like a transient failure. A provider without the capability keeps failing an unknown outcome. Metrics reasons `clone-outcome-unknown`, `provider-clone-rejected`.
- `internal/controller/vmclone_target_stamp.go`, `internal/controller/vmclone_controller.go` (with #393): an owner refusal of the clone source (`VM_NOT_OWNED`, `OWNER_STAMP_UNREADABLE`) fails a first attempt with the constant `cloneSourceNotOwnedMessage`; answering a re-send it is held as `CloneOutcomeUnknown` (the provider re-binds before it checks the source), and a re-send skips the `GetDiskInfo` source-owner / disk-size gate, so it never fails the clone and removes its target.
- `internal/controller/vmadoption_singlehost.go`, `internal/controller/vmadoption_controller.go` (with #392): adoption never binds an unbound `VMClone` target (`virtrigaud.io/clone-uid`) to a listed VM that shares its name (legacy "Fixing Status.ID" path) and never treats it as a single-host adopter (`awaitingSingleHostAdoptionOf`): such a target waits for its clone's bind only.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/clone_target.go` (new), `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go`: `Clone` stamps the clone with `target_vm` (uid) in the same `CloneVM_Task`; before reading or changing the source it looks the target name up in the target folder exactly as `Create` does, returns a VM stamped with that UID (a re-sent `Clone`) and refuses anything else with `AlreadyExists`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_target.go` (new), `internal/providers/libvirt/clone.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`: the single-host `Clone` holds the domain-name lock from the target check to the define, reports a domain stamped with the target's UID as the clone (before the source's state is read), refuses any other same-named domain with `AlreadyExists` (was a non-retryable `codes.Unknown` InvalidSpec), and stamps the clone's definition with `target_vm`. `InvalidSpec` and `NotFound` refusals now carry `InvalidArgument` / `NotFound` on the wire (the NotFound message no longer embeds the virsh command).

- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_create_marker.go`, `internal/controller/owner_rebind.go` (new): a single-host `Create` whose outcome is unknown is re-sent only to a provider that reports `supports_owner_rebind` (was: by provider type, so a Proxmox image older than #380 could make a second VMID); any other is held (`CreateOutcomeUnknown`), and nothing is sent while the capability can't be read.

### Added
- `proto/provider/v1/provider.proto` (bindings regenerated), `internal/providers/contracts/capabilities.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/client.go`, `sdk/provider/capabilities/capabilities.go` (`CapabilityOwnerRebind`, `Builder.OwnerRebind`): `GetCapabilitiesResponse.supports_owner_rebind` (field 26; 25 is `supports_owner_transfer`, PR #392), reported by the vSphere, libvirt (single-host and clustered), Proxmox and mock providers.
- `internal/providers/mock/provider.go`: the mock `Create` and `Clone` stamp the VM with the owner / `target_vm` uid and re-bind a re-sent request; another VM of a clone's target name is `AlreadyExists`.
- Tests: capability round-trip and per-provider advertisement; a provider without the capability is never re-sent a `Create` or `Clone`; the review cases (unrecorded target UID then deleted target, missing target at bind, nothing-done drops the request, failed clone keeps a target with a request on record, attempt pacing); `internal/providers/vsphere/clone_target_test.go` (vcsim), `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_target_test.go` (fake virsh), `internal/providers/proxmox/clone_rebind_test.go` (`pvefake`: a re-send while PVE still clones, after a provider restart and after a lost answer makes no second VMID; unprovable ownership is `AlreadyExists`), `internal/providers/mock/clone_test.go`, `internal/controller/vmclone_target_stamp_test.go`, `internal/controller/vmclone_target_stamp_envtest_test.go` (envtest: lost record and unknown outcome are re-sent with the same target UID and re-bound; the conditions are written once with the clone's generation).

### Changed
- `proto/provider/v1/provider.proto`, `internal/providers/contracts/clone.go`: `CloneRequest.target_vm` carries the target's uid on every topology, and its stamp/re-bind contract is documented. Older managers send no uid and get today's unstamped clone.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/testdata/single_host_snapshot_clone_disk.golden.json`: the single-host clone's command sequence starts with the target-name check (`virsh list --all`, then `dumpxml` of a same-named domain).
- Existing controller tests updated for the target created before the `Clone` (fake clients assign UIDs on create).
- `docs/vm-ownership.md` (new "Clones: re-bind" section, vSphere "Clones" table, Proxmox notes; the single-host clone limitation is removed), `docs/libvirt-domain-ownership.md`, `docs/libvirt-clones.md`, `docs/vm-provider-binding.md` (the Create re-send table is capability-gated), `docs/upgrading.md` (behaviour rows; vSphere default-folder drift and in-flight re-bind notes).

### Why
The rc1 known limitation: single-host `VMClone` targets were not stamped with their owner, so a `Clone` re-sent after a manager restart or a lost record was not re-bound — it made a second clone on Proxmox and failed (leaving the first clone untracked) on vSphere and libvirt. `Create` already had this guarantee; `Clone` now has the same one. Proxmox behaviour is validated against `pvefake` only (no real PVE cluster).

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-17 06:39] - VMMigration acts only on the target VM it created; manager-owned virtrigaud.io keys reserved by an admission policy
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Security
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_target_binding.go` (new), `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`: a `VMMigration` is bound to the target `VirtualMachine` it created by the UID its own `Create` returned (`status.targetVMUID`). Before the `Create` it persists the SHA-256 digest of a fresh random claim token (`status.targetVMClaim`; the token goes only on the VM, as `virtrigaud.io/migration-claim`), so a `Create` whose UID write was lost (conflict, restart) is recognized on the next reconcile instead of being created again or mistaken for someone else's. Any other `VirtualMachine` under the target's name — whether the cache shows it (no `Create` is sent), it is found at `Validating-Target`, or it appears between the live check and the `Create` (`AlreadyExists`) — fails the migration with reason `TargetVMNotOwned` and a constant message, and is never read into the migration's status, annotated `migration-completed` or deleted. The check runs first at `Validating`, before the source is powered off, snapshotted or exported. Provenance annotations and `spec.importedDisk` (writable by whoever creates a VM) are no longer trusted anywhere: the `AlreadyExists` path (#388) and the deletion path (now a UID-precondition delete of the bound VM only) used them. A VM that is not proven fails only after the VMMigration and the VM are re-read from the API server, so a lagging cache never fails a migration over its own target. A recorded UID whose VM is gone (confirmed live) fails `Creating` with `TargetVMGone` instead of re-creating next to a stale UID; the claim write clears any UID in the same optimistic-lock write; a retry (`handleFailedPhase` → Pending) releases a binding whose VM no longer exists (a bound VM that still exists keeps it). `Validating-Target`, the committing step, re-reads the VM live and treats one being deleted as gone. `AlreadyExists` on a VM that carries another claim (only a manager writes one with the policy on: an overlapping leader) is re-checked, not failed.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_target_binding.go` (`migrationTargetLabels`): the reserved labels in `spec.target.labels` (`virtrigaud.io/adopted`) are no longer copied onto the target VM, with one Normal `TargetLabelsDropped` event naming them; every other label (any domain) is copied. The manager creates the VM, so the admission policy would not stop them (annotations were already filtered).
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`: `isOwnMigrationDisk` also requires the referenced migration to have created this VM (UID or claim; the claim is re-read from the API server when the cache lags). A same-named VM with a copied `spec.importedDisk` in the migration's namespace no longer gets the landing disk attached in place.
- `charts/virtrigaud/templates/admission-policy.yaml` (new), `charts/virtrigaud/values.yaml` (`admissionPolicy.reservedKeys`, default on), `config/admission-policy/` (new, included by `config/default`): a `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` + binding (Kubernetes 1.30+, not a webhook) that rejects creating a `VirtualMachine` with, or adding/changing on one, the manager-owned keys (`virtrigaud.io/migration`, `migration-claim`, `migrated-from`, `imported-disk-id`, `disk-checksum`, `migration-completed(-at)`, `clone`, `clone-uid`, `cloned-from`, `adopted-host`, `adopted-id`, label `virtrigaud.io/adopted`) by any identity but the manager's ServiceAccount and the configured `exemptUsernames` / `exemptGroups`. User-set keys (`orphan-on-delete`, `force-delete`, `create-outcome`, `placement-uid`) and updates that leave the reserved keys unchanged are allowed. Rendered only on 1.30+ (or when the API is reported); `--reuse-values` from releases without the block renders it on. Exempt identities are rendered as JSON-quoted CEL literals and a name outside `[A-Za-z0-9:._@+-]` fails the render (a malformed one would deny every VirtualMachine write under failurePolicy Fail). `config/default` fills the kustomize copy's manager identity from the ServiceAccount (`replacements`), so editing its namespace/namePrefix keeps the manager exempt. The policy is a security control for adoption (single-host: `adopted` + `adopted-id`, #392; clustered: `adopted-host`/`adopted-id`) and `VMClone` (`clone-uid`), which still bind from those markers; the residual risk below 1.30 is documented.

### Added
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/vmmigration_types.go`: `VMMigrationStatus.targetVMUID` and `targetVMClaim` (optional, additive); `config/crd/bases/infra.virtrigaud.io_vmmigrations.yaml` regenerated.
- `hack/verify-admission-policy-render.sh` (new), `Makefile` (`verify-admission-policy-render`), `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: render guard — default on for 1.30+, nothing below 1.30 or when disabled, ServiceAccount and exemptions in the match conditions, malformed exemptions refused, CEL identical to `config/admission-policy`, a renamed `config/default` (kustomize, when available) exempts its renamed manager, `--reuse-values` from v0.3.11 renders.
- Tests: `internal/controller/vmmigration_target_binding_test.go`, `vmmigration_creating_test.go` (rewritten; also stale UID → `TargetVMGone`, retry releases a gone binding then a fresh Create binds through a lost UID write, Validating-Target on the live VM, `AlreadyExists` with another claim, dropped-label event), `vmmigration_target_binding_envtest_test.go` (planted VM seen by the cache / at Validating-Target / on `AlreadyExists`; own VM re-recognized after a restart that lost its UID), `admission_policy_test.go` (key inventory vs. policy), `admission_policy_envtest_test.go` (the shipped policy on the envtest apiserver: tenant denied, user keys and unchanged updates allowed, manager and exempt group allowed); fixtures in `vmmigration_crossnamespace_test.go`, `vmmigration_ready_cleanup_test.go`, `virtualmachine_image_path_test.go`, `vmmigration_target_vm_test.go` bind their target VM.
- `docs/vm-ownership.md`: the adoption markers are reserved by the policy.
- `docs/admission-policy.md` (new; key inventory), `docs/cross-namespace-targets.md` ("The target VM must be the migration's own", upgrade note), `docs/upgrading.md` (two rows, installer privileges), `docs/README.md`, `charts/virtrigaud/README.md`.

### Changed
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`: constants for the migration's informational annotations; `transitionToFailedWithReason`; the Creating → Validating-Target transition requeues after `migrationPhaseAdvanceRequeue` instead of immediately; Validating-Target writes its waiting message only when it changes.

### Why
Security review M1 (rc1 known limitation "A cross-namespace migration adopts a same-named target VM"): anyone who could create a `VirtualMachine` in the target namespace could plant one under the target's name, with forged provenance, and the migration treated it as its own target — reported it, marked it completed, could hand it the landing disk and delete the source afterwards.

### Impact
- [x] Breaking change (behavioural: a migration whose target name is taken by a VM it did not create now fails; a migration in `Creating`/`Validating-Target` during the upgrade fails with `TargetVMNotOwned`; non-manager identities, e.g. restore tools, can no longer set the reserved keys unless exempted — see docs/upgrading.md)
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-17 00:52] - Proxmox: every per-VM call is owner-checked against a reused VMID (Describe, Power, Reconfigure, snapshots, disk reads and exports, clone sources)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Security
- `internal/providers/proxmox/vm_owner_check.go` (new), `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`: on a single-host Proxmox Provider only `Delete` checked the VM's owner stamp. `Describe`, `Power`, `Reconfigure`, `SnapshotCreate`, `SnapshotDelete`, `SnapshotRevert`, `GetDiskInfo`, `ExportDisk` and `Clone` (its source) acted on whatever VM held the recorded VMID. A `VirtualMachine` whose VM was deleted outside VirtRigaud could therefore read, power off, resize, snapshot or revert an unrelated VM (another tenant's) that PVE gave the freed VMID, and a `VMMigration` or `VMClone` of it read and copied that VM's disks. When the request carries an owner (`source_owner` for a clone source), the provider now reads the VM's config and checks the stamp first, with `Delete`'s rule: a VM stamped with the requester's UID, or unstamped and named like the owner (its name, or `contracts.AdoptedVMName`), is acted on as before; a VM stamped with another UID, or unstamped with another name, is `NotFound` + `VM_NOT_OWNED` and is neither read, copied nor changed; an unreadable or multiple stamp is `FailedPrecondition` + `OWNER_STAMP_UNREADABLE`; a config that cannot be read is retryable (for `Clone`: `Unavailable` + `CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`, nothing cloned). `Describe` answers `VM_NOT_OWNED`, never `Exists=false` (which would make the manager create the VM again for a VM it cannot prove gone). `Reconfigure` and `GetDiskInfo` reuse the config they already read; the other calls make one extra config read, only when an owner is sent. `SnapshotDelete` checks the VM on its actual node; `ExportDisk` checks before either backend (S3, NFS) path, and each path's own disk read (the config that yields the copied volume, `s3export.go`, `nfs.go`) is owner-checked too; `Clone` checks its source after the re-bind lookup (which never reads the source, so a retried `Clone` whose target exists still re-binds) and before the VMID allocation and the clone task. Requests without an owner (an older manager) are unchanged; templates keep their handling and are owner-checked like any VM.

### Changed
- `internal/controller/vmref.go`, `internal/providers/contracts/vmref.go`: `vmRefFor` gives a single-host ref the VirtualMachine's identity as `Owner` (`singleHostRef`; none without a UID).
- `internal/transport/grpc/client.go`: every per-VM request sends the owner for every VM (`vmOwner`), not only routed ones: `Describe`, `Delete`, `Power`, `Reconfigure`, the snapshot calls, `GetDiskInfo`, `ExportDisk`, and `CloneRequest.source_owner`. `routedOwner` is removed. vSphere, single-host libvirt (which reads `source_owner` and the disk-call owner only on its clustered path) and mock ignore it.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_owner_refusal_hold.go` (new), `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`, `internal/k8s/conditions.go`: a single-host `Describe`, `Power` or `Reconfigure` answered `VM_NOT_OWNED` holds the `VirtualMachine` as `Ready=False/VMNotOwned` (new reason), one answered `OWNER_STAMP_UNREADABLE` as `Ready=False/OwnerStampUnreadable`: constant message, one `Warning` event when the hold begins, status written only on change, blocked-VM backoff (up to 5 min), `status.id` kept and nothing re-created (the backoff counts from Ready's `LastTransitionTime`, documented). The hold message's resolution follows adoption re-stamping (#392). `internal/controller/snapshot_not_owned_release.go` (new), `internal/controller/vmsnapshot_controller.go`, `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`: a `SnapshotDelete` answered `VM_NOT_OWNED` (a `VMSnapshot` finalizer, a migration's source-snapshot cleanup) still releases, but with a `SnapshotLeftOnHypervisor` Warning (constant message: the snapshot may be left on the VM at this id), an error-level log line with the ids and the `vm-not-owned` metric, never as "already gone".
- `internal/controller/copy_source_owner_refusal.go` (new), `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`, `internal/controller/vmmigration_source_power.go`, `internal/controller/vmclone_controller.go`, `internal/controller/disk_size_limit_copies.go`: a `VMMigration` whose source the provider refuses as above — at the disk-size checks' `GetDiskInfo` (Validating, and right before export), the `powerOffBeforeMigration` `Describe`, the source snapshot or `ExportDisk` — fails with a constant message before anything is exported; the disk-size checks no longer hold such a source as "size unreadable". The power-off wait now describes the source before it sets the source `VirtualMachine`'s `spec.powerState` to `Off`, so a refused (or gone) source's spec is not changed. A `VMClone` whose source is refused at the disk-size check or at `Clone` fails (`Failed=True`, reason `VMNotOwned` or `OwnerStampUnreadable`) with a constant message and one `Warning` event, nothing cloned. The provider's answer goes to the manager log only.
- `proto/provider/v1/provider.proto`, `proto/rpc/provider/v1/provider.pb.go` (regenerated, comments only): the `owner` of every per-VM request and `CloneRequest.source_owner` are sent single-host too, and checked by a single-host Proxmox provider. No wire change.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/vm_owner_check_test.go` (new): every guarded call against pvefake with VMID reuse by another tenant's VM and by a VM made outside VirtRigaud, legacy unstamped and adopted names, unreadable, multiple and repeated stamps, a template, no owner, a config-read failure, a gone VM, a snapshot delete after a node move, `ExportDisk` on both backends and its export paths' own disk read, a retried `Clone` re-binding although its source VMID was reused, and a VM re-stamped by `TransferOwner` (#392) passing the checks for its new owner only; a refused call only reads the VM's `/config` and changes nothing. `internal/controller/virtualmachine_owner_refusal_hold_test.go` (new): unit and envtest holds for `Describe` and `Power`, no re-create, no status churn, release on delete. `internal/controller/snapshot_not_owned_release_test.go` (new): the snapshot release warnings. `internal/controller/copy_source_owner_refusal_test.go` (new): unit tests for every migration and clone failure point, and an envtest migration of a reused-VMID source that fails before the source's spec is changed. `internal/transport/grpc/client_routing_test.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_clustered_test.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_boundprovider_test.go`: single-host refs and every per-VM request carry the owner.
- `docs/vm-ownership.md`: new section "Per-VM calls: `Describe`, `Power`, `Reconfigure`, snapshots, disks and clone sources"; "When is a VM gone?", "Existing VMs" and "Limits" updated (the limitations that these calls do not check the stamp are removed; the check-then-act window, the unused PVE config `digest` for `Reconfigure`, and that `VM.Allocate` where VirtRigaud's VMs live is enough to claim the legacy name rule at a freed VMID are listed), the API cost of the checks (one extra `GET /config` per call except `Reconfigure` and `GetDiskInfo`), and how to resolve `VMNotOwned` with adoption re-stamping (#392); "VMs adopted before this release" notes the hold. `docs/upgrading.md`: behaviour-change row.

### Why
A reused Proxmox VMID let one tenant's `VirtualMachine` observe, change or copy another tenant's VM. Validated against the in-repo PVE fake (pvefake) only; there is no real PVE cluster in CI or the lab for this change.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-17 00:18] - Adoption stamps the adopted VM with its new owner (single-host)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Added
- `proto/provider/v1/provider.proto`, `proto/rpc/provider/v1/*.pb.go`: additive `GetCapabilitiesResponse.supports_owner_transfer` (field 25): `TransferOwner` re-stamps a VM a single-host provider listed, addressed by `id` alone (`target_host_id` empty, refused when set). The `TransferOwner` contract is documented for single-host providers: compare-and-swap (atomic on the hypervisor where it allows it), refusals `AlreadyExists` / `NotFound` with messages that never name another owner, retryable errors otherwise.
- `internal/providers/contracts/adoption.go`: `OwnerTransferDecision`, the compare-and-swap decision every provider's `TransferOwner` shares (unstamped, exactly the new owner's stamp, or one replaceable stale stamp; a stamp with the new owner's UID under another namespace or name is refused as edited). `internal/providers/contracts/capabilities.go`: `Capabilities.SupportsOwnerTransfer`. `internal/transport/grpc/client.go` maps it. `sdk/provider/capabilities`: `CapabilityOwnerTransfer` and `Builder.OwnerTransfer()`.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/transfer_owner.go` (new): `TransferOwner` stamps the VM's ExtraConfig owner keys with `ReconfigVM_Task` carrying the `config.changeVersion` it decided on (vCenter refuses the write if the configuration changed since), refuses a template, an image artifact or an unreadable stamp (`listExclusionFor`), checks the instance UUID when one is sent, and reads the stamp back. Retryable failures carry `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`. Reports `supports_owner_transfer`. Replaces the `Unimplemented` stub in `hosts.go`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/adoption_transfer_owner.go` (new): single-host `TransferOwner` runs the clustered core (`transferOwnerOn`: domain name and UUID, both definitions of a running domain, `virsh metadata` and read-back) on the provider's one host under the per-host lock. `server.go` no longer answers `Unimplemented` on a single-host provider and reports `supports_owner_transfer` there.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/transfer_owner.go` (new): `TransferOwner` writes the `virtrigaud.owner` description line (`phase=ready`, other notes kept) with the config `digest` it read (PVE refuses the update if the configuration changed since). Refuses a template, an unreadable or multiple stamp, a stamp whose create has not finished, and a VM whose PVE name is not the new owner's (a reused VMID; the rule an unstamped VM's `Delete` uses); a VM locked by a PVE task is retried; a VM on another node is found cluster-wide (refused outside the Provider's node selector). Reports `supports_owner_transfer`. Replaces the stub in `hosts.go`.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/pvefake/server.go`: the fake returns a config `digest` and refuses an update whose `digest` is stale, as PVE does; `Fault.PassThrough` runs a hook and serves the request normally (to change a VM between a client's read and write).
- `internal/providers/mock/transfer_owner.go` (new): in-memory compare-and-swap `TransferOwner`; `ListVMs` reports the stamp as `owner_uid`; reports `supports_owner_transfer`.
- `internal/controller/vmadoption_singlehost.go` (new): through a provider that reports `SupportsOwnerTransfer`, single-host adoption creates the adopting VirtualMachine without status (annotated `virtrigaud.io/adopted-id`), re-reads it uncached, stamps the VM with it (`TransferOwner`), and only then writes `status.id`/`boundProvider` (re-read, retried on conflict, only while it still waits). Stale stamps are replaced only with `adopt-stamped-vms` and after one uncached list of every VirtualMachine shows none has the UID (fail closed without an uncached reader). A VM bound by `status.id` to a VirtualMachine of another single-host Provider object of the same type and endpoint is never adopted or stamped. A stamped-but-unbound adoption is completed from the stamp; a refused transfer, or a waiting adopter whose VM can no longer be adopted, is removed again (re-read, preconditioned delete, no provider call). Constant skip reasons in `Provider.status.adoption.message`; metric reason `adoption-owner-transfer`. Only a VirtualMachine with the adopted name (`contracts.AdoptedVMName`), no create marker and no pending host is ever handed a VM or bound; the adoption filter applies to waiting adopters too; the binding re-checks consumer grants on the object it writes; libvirt domains listed without a UUID are skipped.

### Changed
- `internal/controller/vmadoption_controller.go`: single-host discovery reads the provider's capabilities first: stamped adoption when `SupportsOwnerTransfer`, the previous flow otherwise (its message now says adopted VMs are not stamped), and no adoption at all while the capabilities cannot be read. `discoverUnmanagedVMs` takes the resolved provider.
- `internal/controller/vmadoption_clustered.go`: `removeStrandedAdoptedVM` reuses the shared `removeWaitingVM`; a skipped VM without a host is named by its id alone. Clustered adoption is otherwise unchanged.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_transfer_owner.go`: the decision delegates to `contracts.OwnerTransferDecision`; TransferOwner validation runs before the topology dispatch.
- `examples/vm-adoption-example.yaml`: notes that adopted domains are stamped.
- `docs/vm-ownership.md`: new section "Adoption stamps the adopted VM" (which VMs, the per-provider compare-and-swap, order and every intermediate state, older providers and managers, VMs adopted before this release); the Proxmox `Delete` and "Existing VMs" text no longer says adoption leaves the stamp; vSphere privilege row. `docs/libvirt-domain-ownership.md`, `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md`: single-host adoption now stamps. `docs/upgrading.md`: new behaviour row, privilege bullets, rollback caveat.

### Why
Adoption left the adopted VM's owner stamp as it was. A VM detached with `orphan-on-delete` and adopted again kept the deleted VirtualMachine's stamp, so its new VirtualMachine's (Proxmox) delete answered `VM_NOT_OWNED` and left it on the hypervisor (v0.4.0-rc1 known limitation), and an unstamped adopted VM could be adopted again through another Provider object. Re-stamping must never let one namespace take over a VM a live VirtualMachine owns, hence the uncached proof, the sibling-Provider guard and the compare-and-swap on the hypervisor.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-16 22:45] - vSphere: a disk import is no longer refused on a freshly started provider
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/vsphere/s3import.go`, `internal/providers/vsphere/nfs.go`: `ImportDisk` (S3 and NFS) resolved the target datastore before scoping the shared finder to the default datacenter. govmomi's finder resolves a relative name such as the `DefaultDatastore` only inside a datacenter, and a freshly started provider has none until an RPC sets it. So a migration into vSphere whose `ImportDisk` was the first such RPC after a provider (re)start failed for good with `failed to resolve target datastore: datastore/StoragePod "<name>" not found`, after the source disk was already exported and converted. The datacenter, datastore and NFC import placement are now resolved together by `resolveImportTarget`, which sets the datacenter first.

### Changed

### Why
A migration into vSphere must not depend on which RPC the provider happened to serve first after a restart; the failure was terminal and wasted the export.

## [2026-10-16 21:00] - Status writes never replace a newer status with a stale copy (VMMigration, Provider, VMAdoption)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_status_write.go` (new), `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`: `updateStatus` no longer copies the reconcile's in-memory status onto the re-read object after a conflict. That copy was a blind last-writer-wins write: a reconcile that started from a stale cache replaced the whole live status. Pre-existing since df7e440 (2025-11, so in v0.3.11); exposed by the v0.4.0-rc1 lab run, where a libvirt → S3 → vSphere migration failed with "import did not record disk info". Reconcile A recorded `status.diskInfo` and moved to `Creating`. Reconcile B, from a cache predating A's write, took the already-imported branch, and its write dropped A's `diskInfo`. The same write could drop or bring back `sourceSize`, the staging marker / layout / digest / import target, `sourceVMUID`, the `PostMigrationCleanup` marker, `taskRef` or the phase. A brought-back phase can resend a non-idempotent RPC. Now:
  - `updateStatus` writes under the resourceVersion the reconcile read. A conflict is never retried onto a re-read object. `Reconcile` turns it into a requeue after 2 s (`migrationStatusConflictRequeue`; not an error, not immediate), and the next reconcile starts from the live state.
  - The results of `SnapshotCreate`, `ExportDisk` and `ImportDisk` are written with `recordMigrationResult`. On a conflict it re-reads the `VMMigration` from the API server. While that is the same object (UID) and still in the RPC's phase, it applies only the result's fields (and the phase transition the result completes) to the live object, with retry-on-conflict. A live status in another phase, or a re-created object, is not written: the result is dropped, logged at `ERROR` with the provider's ids, and reported with a `Warning` event `ProviderResultNotRecorded` (constant message).
  - A snapshot, export or import result that still cannot be written (for example, the API server is unavailable) is held in memory (for export / import in place of the in-flight guard), bound to the migration attempt. The next reconcile of the phase writes it first, before resolving any source, provider or target, instead of advancing to `Importing` / `Creating` without it or taking the snapshot again. This manager process therefore does not re-send the RPC. The held result is in memory only: a manager restart or leader change between the RPC and its write, or while a result is held, loses it, and the new leader can re-send `ExportDisk` / `ImportDisk` / `SnapshotCreate` (pre-existing, not closed by this change). Held results and guards of a `VMMigration` are dropped once its finalizer is released.
- `internal/controller/provider_status_write.go` (new), `internal/controller/provider_controller.go`, `internal/controller/provider_inuse.go`: `writeProviderStatus` copied the whole in-memory status onto the re-read Provider on every attempt, dropping `status.adoption` written by the VMAdoption controller (the two conflicted in the lab). It now writes under the resourceVersion it read. On a conflict it re-reads the Provider. Only when the Provider controller's own fields still equal what it read does it write them onto the live object, keeping the live `status.adoption`. Otherwise it writes nothing and the reconcile runs again.
- `internal/controller/vmadoption_controller.go`, `internal/controller/vmadoption_clustered.go`: every adoption status write sets `status.adoption` alone on the Provider re-read from the API server, with retry-on-conflict (`writeAdoptionStatus`). Before, it wrote the whole status from the reconcile's read, and the Provider controller's frequent writes made it conflict and lose the discovery result. A message-only write keeps the stored discovery time and counts.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_create_marker.go`: removing the create-outcome annotation is an optimistic-locked patch. The reconcile keeps its own `VirtualMachine` status under the patch's new resourceVersion, and that status can no longer be older than one another writer stored meanwhile. A conflict requeues.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go` (pre-existing): in `Creating`, a target-VM `Create` that answers `AlreadyExists` no longer fails the migration when the existing VirtualMachine is the one this migration created. That happens when an earlier `Create` is not yet in the cache. The VM is re-read from the API server and must carry the migration's `virtrigaud.io/migration` provenance annotation and attach this migration's imported disk (`spec.importedDisk`: source `migration`, this migration's name and `status.importID`). Any other VM of that name still fails the migration as before.

### Changed
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_update_status_test.go`, `internal/controller/vmmigration_pending_result_test.go` (new), `internal/controller/status_write_clobber_envtest_test.go` (new): unit and envtest coverage. Envtest specs, and how each behaves against the pre-fix writers (checked by swapping the old `updateStatus` / `writeProviderStatus` / adoption writes back in):
  - The lab race: reconcile B from a stale cache leaves A's `diskInfo` in place, and the next reconcile creates the target VM on the imported disk. **Fails on the old code** (B's write empties `diskInfo.targetPath`).
  - `status.adoption` is kept when the Provider controller reconciles from a read that predates the adoption write (its cache catches up right after its first read, as in the lab). **Fails on the old code** (adoption dropped without any conflict).
  - A Provider controller write whose own fields moved past its read is refused, and a reconcile from that read requeues. **Fails on the old code** (the stale write overwrites the newer field).
  - An `ImportDisk` result is recorded on the live object when the `VMMigration` was edited during the import. **Passes on the old code too**: a regression guard for the new rule that an ordinary status conflict is requeued, not retried.
  - The create-outcome annotation removal is refused (a conflict, nothing patched) from a VirtualMachine read that another status write has moved past. **Fails on the old code** (the unlocked patch succeeded).
  Unit tests (`vmmigration_creating_test.go` too) cover the held-result paths (snapshot sync and task, export before provider resolution, import), the dropped-result event, attempt binding, guard eviction, and `AlreadyExists` in `Creating` for the migration's own VM and for other VMs.
- `docs/release-notes/next.md`: Fixes entry.

### Why
The v0.4.0-rc1 lab run lost an imported disk's record to a stale status write and failed the migration. The same blind copy could undo any status field another reconcile or controller had written, and on a migration it could resend a non-idempotent RPC.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-16 21:00] - rc1 lab fix: vSphere ExportDisk no longer leaks a full copy of the disk on the source datastore
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note.** Exports by earlier releases (also v0.3.11) left `virtrigaud-export-*` files, a full copy of each exported disk, in the source VMs' folders on the datastores. This release stops leaking but does not remove them: delete them by hand (see `docs/upgrading.md`, "Leftover `virtrigaud-export-*` files on vSphere datastores").

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/vsphere/export_cleanup.go` (new), `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go`: `ExportDisk` cloned the source disk to a temporary `virtrigaud-export-<vm id>-<unix time>.vmdk` and deleted it with the datastore file manager. On VMFS the clone is a descriptor plus a `-flat.vmdk` extent; deleting the descriptor path left the 12 GiB extent in the source VM's folder (rc1 lab, vCenter 8), which then also kept the folder alive after the VM was destroyed. The clone is now removed with `VirtualDiskManager.DeleteVirtualDisk` (descriptor and all extents; same datacenter as the copy; the task is awaited). If that fails (for example the descriptor is already gone), the fallback deletes, with the datastore file manager, only files in the clone's folder named exactly `<temp name>-flat.vmdk`, `<temp name>-s<NNN>.vmdk` or `<temp name>-sesparse.vmdk` (and the descriptor); the temporary name is anchored and quoted, never a broader glob, and a non-export file is refused. A failed removal is logged provider-side at `ERROR` and never reaches the caller or tenant-visible status.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go`: the cleanup is registered before the clone starts, so a clone task that failed or was cancelled after it created (part of) its files is removed too. Before, the cleanup was registered only after a successful clone. A clone task whose wait was abandoned (cancelled request) is cancelled on vCenter and awaited before the cleanup runs, so the cleanup does not race a copy that is still writing.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/export_cleanup.go`: the cleanup runs on a fresh context with a 10 minute bound (was 30 s, too short to delete a large extent); the request's context may already be cancelled.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/export_cleanup.go`, `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go`: the temporary name gains a random suffix (`virtrigaud-export-<vm id>-<unix time>-<8 hex>.vmdk`), so two exports of the same VM in the same second can never share a name; with the cleanup now also running after a failed clone, a shared name would let one export delete the other's clone. The `virtrigaud-export-` prefix is unchanged.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/disk_guard.go`, `internal/providers/vsphere/s3import.go`: reviewed, no change. The vSphere provider makes no other temporary clone: `CopyVirtualDisk` is called only by `ExportDisk`, and `cleanupFailedImport` deletes a whole landing folder (every file in it), not a single descriptor.

### Security
