- `internal/providers/vsphere/export_cleanup.go`: closes a storage leak on the tenant's side of the datastore: a full, readable copy of a tenant's disk stayed on the datastore after every vSphere export, in the source VM's folder, outliving the migration and the VM. Pre-existing (v0.3.11 and earlier).

### Changed
- `internal/providers/vsphere/export_cleanup_test.go` (new): vcsim tests. After `ExportDisk` on the S3 relay path (success, forced datastore-download failure, and a clone that fails after vCenter created its files) no `virtrigaud-export-*` file, descriptor or extent, remains in the VM folder, and the folder is as before the export. vcsim stores a copied disk as a descriptor plus a `-flat.vmdk` file like VMFS; the tests fail on the previous cleanup (the extent remained). `DeleteVirtualDisk`, the descriptor-gone fallback (decoys with the same prefix are untouched), a clone that does not exist, and a refusal to delete a non-export disk are tested directly.
- `docs/upgrading.md`, `docs/release-notes/next.md`: how to find and delete the leftovers of earlier exports.

### Why
A rc1 lab export on a real vCenter 8 / VMFS datastore left a 12 GiB `virtrigaud-export-…-flat.vmdk` in the source VM's folder. It was a full copy of the tenant's disk, outside any VM and any quota, and it blocked the VM folder's removal.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout (vSphere provider pods)
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-13 00:22] - rc1 lab fixes: one-actor source power-off for migrations, idempotent Power, libvirt default pool never rewritten, snapshot overlay cleanup
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note.**
> - **libvirt hosts: the `default` storage pool must be at `/var/lib/libvirt/images`.** The provider no longer destroys and recreates a `default` pool at another path (it did since v0.3.11 — it rewrote an NFS-backed pool on the lab). Such a pool is now left untouched and creates / disk imports on that host fail with `InvalidSpec`. Check every host with `virsh pool-dumpxml default` before upgrading; mount shared storage **at** `/var/lib/libvirt/images`.
> - `powerOffBeforeMigration` now waits for the VirtualMachine controller to power the source off (at most 10 minutes) instead of powering it off itself.

### Fixed
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_source_power.go` (new), `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`: a `VMMigration` with `spec.source.powerOffBeforeMigration: true` on a running source failed terminally (rc1 lab, F3). The migration set the source VM's `spec.powerState` to `Off` and also sent its own `Power(Off)`. The VirtualMachine controller powered the source off as well, and the second `virsh destroy` failed on the stopped domain. The migration now has one actor: it sets the desired state and waits on a read-only `Describe`. The wait is recorded as `Validating=False` and `SourcePowerOff=False` (reason `WaitingForSourcePowerOff`) with a constant message, written only on change, with an event when the wait starts. It requeues every 5 s for at most 10 minutes, measured from the `SourcePowerOff` condition (other Validating checks do not restart it; a retry from Pending starts a fresh budget), then fails with a constant message. A failed `Describe` or an unresolvable provider instance is waited out; a source the provider does not find (`Exists=false` or NotFound) fails at once with a constant message. The migration never calls `Power`. The source is still not powered back on. VMClone only waits for its source (no power call) and is unchanged.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`, `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`, `internal/providers/mock/provider.go`: `Power` is idempotent. An `Off` / `ShutdownGraceful` of a VM that is already off, or an `On` of a running one, succeeds, also when another actor won the race:
  - libvirt re-reads `domstate` after a failed `start` / `destroy` / `shutdown`; an unreadable state or `Reboot` keeps the failure;
  - vSphere re-reads the power state after a failed task (`InvalidPowerState`);
  - Proxmox returns no task when the VM is already in the requested state, and re-reads the status after a failed request;
  - mock returns no task.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/storage.go`: `EnsureDefaultStoragePool` (called by Create, `ImportDisk` and the NFS / S3 imports) never destroys, undefines or redefines an existing pool (rc1 lab, F1; since 19499ea). It reads the pool definition structurally:
  - no `default` pool: created at `/var/lib/libvirt/images`;
  - at that path (lexically, or once both are resolved on the host): started only if inactive;
  - at any other path: untouched, `InvalidSpec` with a constant message (no host, no path: it reaches tenant-visible status); the host and the pool's path are logged by the provider;
  - unreadable: retryable, nothing done.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`: a Create failure that is `InvalidSpec` is returned unwrapped (non-retryable, `InvalidArgument` on the wire) instead of as a retryable error.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/snapshot_overlay_cleanup.go` (new), `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/conn.go`: `SnapshotDelete` removes the overlay file `<domain>-disk.<snapshot>` that libvirt 10 leaves in the pool after deleting an external snapshot (rc1 lab, F2). It records the snapshot's overlays before the delete, and after it removes only the domain's own overlay when it is out of every current chain, referenced by no other snapshot, a regular file inside the storage directories, and used by no other domain (cluster-wide on a clustered Provider), using Delete's helpers. Anything unestablished keeps the file. A failed removal is logged only and never fails the RPC. `Provider.SnapshotDelete` now shares the gRPC core.

### Security
- `internal/providers/libvirt/storage.go`: the misplaced-`default`-pool refusal is a constant message. It reaches tenant-visible status (`VirtualMachine` `Ready`, `VMMigration` status), so it names neither the hypervisor host nor the operator's pool path. Both are in the provider's `ERROR` log line.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`: `SnapshotDelete` and `SnapshotRevert` refuse, on single-host providers too, a snapshot id that is empty, starts with `-` (read by virsh as an option), or contains `/` or a control character (the overlay cleanup builds a file name from it). The check returns `InvalidSpec` before any host call. It is looser than the clustered pattern, so snapshots an earlier release named otherwise can still be deleted.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/virsh_probe_log.go` (new), `internal/providers/libvirt/virsh.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/sshclient.go`, `internal/providers/libvirt/guest_agent.go`: `Describe`'s best-effort probes no longer log two `ERROR` lines per poll. These are `dommemstat`, `cpu-stats` and `domblkstat` on a shut-off domain, and `domifaddr --source agent`, `guestinfo` and `guest-ping` without a guest agent. Their failures are `DEBUG`; every other failed command keeps `ERROR`.

### Changed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/testdata/single_host_power_reconfigure.golden.json`, `internal/providers/libvirt/testdata/single_host_snapshot_clone_disk.golden.json`: regenerated. Only failing power operations gain a read-only `domstate`, and `snapshot-delete` gains a read-only `snapshot-dumpxml`. Every successful sequence is unchanged.
- `docs/upgrading.md`, `docs/release-notes/next.md`, `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md` (new "Host prerequisites"), `docs/libvirt-clones.md` ("What SnapshotDelete removes"), `README.md`: the default-pool requirement, the shared-pool recommendation, the migration power-off wait, idempotent Power and the overlay cleanup.

### Known follow-ups
- `createDefaultStoragePool` still stages the pool definition at the fixed path `/tmp/default-pool.xml` on the host (pre-existing; tracked separately).
- Overlays of additional data disks (`<domain>-disk-<n>.<snapshot>`), and overlays left by snapshots deleted before this release, are not removed.

### Why
Three bugs found while lab-testing the v0.4.0-rc1 candidate on a two-host clustered libvirt Provider. Migrations with `powerOffBeforeMigration` failed. An operator's NFS-backed `default` pool was silently rewritten. Every deleted snapshot leaked its overlay file.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-12 15:38] - VMMigration: delete nfs/s3 staged disks through a new provider RPC (ADR-0011); guarded Ready cleanup; staged-image checks on every import
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note.**
> - **Behavior change:** a migration's `nfs` / `s3` staged disk (a full, unencrypted copy of the source disk) is now deleted by the migration's **target** `Provider`. This happens when the migration is `Ready`, when the `VMMigration` is deleted, and when the migration fails for good with `cleanupPolicy: Always`. The default `OnSuccess` keeps a failed migration's staged disk until the `VMMigration` is deleted, and `Never` keeps it in every case. Deleting such a `VMMigration` waits while the delete can still succeed (`StagingCleanup=False/StagingCleanupPending`, retried 15 s→5 min), and while an export task still runs. `virtrigaud.io/force-delete=true` releases it.
> - **Roll the providers with the manager.** An older provider image cannot delete. The delete is held for up to 24 hours, then recorded `StagedDiskLeftBehind` (Warning) and released.
> - **Ready cleanup only for migrations completed by this release.** A `Ready` migration completed before the upgrade deletes neither its source snapshot nor its source VM (one `SourceDeletionSkippedPreUpgrade` Warning). `deleteAfterMigration` deletes only the source VM whose UID the migration recorded.
> - **New NFS staging name** `vmmigrations_<ns>_<name>_export.qcow2` for new migrations; in-flight ones keep the old name.
> - **Versioned / object-lock S3 buckets and NFS snapshots** keep the data after the delete. Expire noncurrent versions on `vmmigrations/`, and exclude the staging export from snapshots.

### Added
- `docs/adr/0011-migration-staging-cleanup.md`, `docs/adr/README.md`: ADR-0011 (Accepted; Option A chosen by the maintainer on 2026-10-11, amended 2026-10-12 after the security review). It records:
  - which provider deletes (the target), and the RPC shape;
  - when the RPC is sent (a decision table by `cleanupPolicy`);
  - the hold, backoff and force-delete behavior;
  - the confinement: staging layouts and the staging digest;
  - capability negotiation, with the 24 h grace for older providers;
  - D9: the post-migration cleanup guard;
  - D10: the staged-image header checks;
  - the residual risks: versioned buckets, NFS snapshots and libnfs symlinks;
  - the alternatives: B (the manager deletes directly) and C (documentation or lifecycle policies only).
- `proto/provider/v1/provider.proto`, `proto/rpc/provider/v1/*.pb.go` (regenerated with buf, protoc-gen-go v1.34.2, protoc-gen-go-grpc v1.5.1):
  - RPC `DeleteStagedDisk`. Its request carries the migration identity, the stage, the backend, the options JSON, the credentials, the staging `layout` (field 6) and, when the migration sent an import, its `target_vm` (field 7). It carries no key, path or URL.
  - enum `StagedDiskDeleteOutcome` (`DELETED`, `NOT_FOUND`, `EMPTIED`).
  - capability `supported_staged_disk_delete_backends` (field 23).

  Additive; no package bump.
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/vmmigration_types.go` (regenerated CRD; additive status fields written by the controller only):
  - `status.storageInfo.stagingLayout` (`v1`/`v2`);
  - `status.storageInfo.stagingDigest`;
  - `status.sourceVMUID`;
  - `status.storageInfo.importTarget` (namespace and name of the VM the import was sent for, persisted before `ImportDisk`).
- `internal/storage/migration/staging.go` (new):
  - `StagedObjectKey`: the single layout source for the export URL, the import URL and the delete. Layout `v2` is unambiguous: NFS `vmmigrations_<ns>_<name>_<stage>.qcow2`.
  - `ResolveStagedDisk`: validates a request. The namespace must be a DNS-1123 label, the name a DNS-1123 subdomain, the stage `export`, and the layout `v1` or `v2`. NFS paths go through `NFSURL`.
  - `DeleteS3StagedDisk` and `EmptyNFSStagedDisk`.
  - `StagedDiskError`: the gRPC status carries no location.
- `internal/storage/migration/staged_image.go` (new): `CheckStagedImageHeader`.
- `internal/storage/s3.go`: `RemoveObjectIfExists`.
- `internal/storage/s3fake/s3fake.go` (new): an in-process S3 server for tests.
- `internal/providers/{proxmox,libvirt,vsphere,mock}/staged_disk.go`, plus the capabilities of each provider:
  - Proxmox: deletes the S3 object from the pod, and unlinks the NFS file through the kernel mount as the migration's uid/gid. A failed `rm`, or a file still present, is an error, never `DELETED`.
    - With `target_vm` it first removes that VM's node-side import stage: `rm -f --` in every stage format, confined to `isImportStagePath`. A failed removal is retryable and leaves the staged object untouched.
    - The manager's `target_vm` is only the VM recorded in `status.storageInfo.importTarget` when the import was sent, never the current, editable `spec.target`. It is left unset in three cases: the recorded VM's namespace no longer grants the migration's namespace; another in-flight migration (including a `Failed` one waiting for a retry) targets the same VM; or another in-flight migration recorded an import for it (`stagedImportTarget`).
  - libvirt (single host) and vSphere: delete the S3 object, and empty the NFS object with qemu-img over libnfs.
  - libvirt clustered and mock: `Unimplemented`; they advertise nothing.
- `internal/providers/contracts/staged_disk.go` (new), `capabilities.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/client.go`, `sdk/provider/capabilities/capabilities.go`: `StagedDiskDeleter`, the client's `DeleteStagedDisk`, and the capability plumbing.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_staging_cleanup.go` (new):
  - the `StagingCleanup` condition, with constant messages that name no location;
  - the decision table;
  - the hold, with the blocked-VM backoff;
  - the deletion release, with force-delete;
  - the staging marker, layout and digest, written before the export URL is built;
  - waiting for a running export task;
  - the 24 h grace for unsupported providers;
  - a DNS failure is a hold;
  - the outcome is persisted before the finalizer is removed.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_ready_cleanup.go` (new): the `PostMigrationCleanup` marker, written with Phase=Ready. It also closes legacy Ready migrations (`SourceDeletionSkippedPreUpgrade`) and handles the live-object check.

### Changed
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`:
  - Validating records `status.sourceVMUID`.
  - The Ready transition stamps `PostMigrationCleanup`.
  - `handleReadyPhase` acts only on the live object. It runs the staging cleanup, and runs the source snapshot and `deleteAfterMigration` only for stamped migrations.
  - `deleteSourceVM` reads the VM live and deletes with a UID precondition. A re-created VM is refused (`SourceDeletionRefused`), and a VM that is already gone counts as done.
  - The export phase writes the staging marker before the URL is built.
  - `generateStorageURL` uses the recorded layout.
  - The `ExportComplete` event no longer names the destination.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_snapshot_cleanup.go`: `handleTerminalFailure` runs the staging cleanup (`Always`), then the snapshot cleanup.
- `internal/controller/provider_inuse.go`: a Ready or Failed migration whose staged disk is still to be deleted holds its Providers.
- `internal/storage/migration/addrpolicy.go`: name-resolution failures are marked `ErrHostUnresolvable`.

### Fixed
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`: removed `cleanupIntermediateStorage`. It built a PVC client **in the manager**, which never mounts migration PVCs, so it failed for every migration with `spec.storage` and blocked the Ready cleanup (the source snapshot and `deleteAfterMigration`). The cleanup is now guarded, see the operator note.

### Security
- Staged migration disks no longer stay on the staging backend. Deletion is confined to the object the provider derives from the migration identity. A delete is never aimed at a location changed after the export (staging digest).
- The NFS staging name is now unambiguous (layout v2). Before, two namespaces could share a staged file: one tenant's export, import or delete could reach another's.
- **Pre-existing High, fixed.** NFS and S3 imports on Proxmox and vSphere ran `qemu-img convert` / `qm importdisk` on a tenant-controlled image without a header check. A backing file, data file or `json:` target could flatten node or pod secrets (`/etc/pve/priv/*`, `/root/.ssh/*`, the service-account token, provider credentials) into the tenant's disk.
  - `internal/providers/proxmox/nfs.go`, `import_stage.go`, `s3import.go`: the object is copied by the imported-disk confinement's stage builder (#384) into a root-owned temp in the root-only `/var/lib/virtrigaud/import-stage`, then renamed onto the stage. `nfsStageCopy` refuses a non-regular file and is bounded. The stage's header is then checked as `qm importdisk` probes it, and a refused stage is removed. `Create` (`recheckImportStage`) parses and checks the stage again, in its extension's format, before it builds anything. A refused stage is removed and nothing is created.
  - `internal/providers/vsphere/nfs.go`, `s3import.go`, `staged_disk.go`: the object is byte-copied into the pod, its header is checked, and that copy is converted with `-f qcow2`.
  - `internal/providers/libvirt/nfs.go`: already had the check, but its convert read the NFS object a second time. It now copies once, then checks and converts the copy.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/nfs.go`: migration NFS exports are mounted `nosymfollow,nosuid,nodev,noexec`.
- `internal/storage/migration/image_header.go` (new): `CheckStagedImageBytes` parses a staged image's first 64 KiB in Go **before** qemu-img opens it. qemu opens a qcow2 external data file and VMDK extents while reading a header, so a crafted image could otherwise make the node or pod open device nodes, host files or `nbd:`/`http:` targets, as root on PVE.
  - qcow2: magic and version; no backing file; no encryption; no data-file bit or extension; only known incompatible features.
  - VMDK: only monolithicSparse/streamOptimized, with one SPARSE extent and no parent.
  - raw: must not start with a foreign magic.
  - It is wired into the Proxmox, vSphere and libvirt staged imports. `qemu-img info` then runs with `-U`, and on Proxmox under `unshare -n`.
- `internal/storage/migration/staged_limit.go` (new) and the three NFS imports: the staged copy is bounded. Its size is read first and refused above `VIRTRIGAUD_MIGRATION_IMPORT_MAX_GIB` (default 1024), lowered by #382's `max_virtual_size_bytes` plus metadata room (1/64 + 16 MiB, `StagedCopyLimit`), or when less than twice its size is free. On Proxmox the migration's uid/gid only measures the object; root checks the bound and the free space. The copy reads at most bound+1 bytes (`qemu-img dd`, or `head -c` on Proxmox), and a copy that grew is refused. Refusals are constant and nothing is left behind.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_staging_cleanup.go`:
  - the v1 layout is kept for any legacy export trace;
  - the staging digest is computed over a versioned canonical struct;
  - a held delete is checked for being due before the export task is polled.
- Docs: tenants must never get `vmmigrations/status` (ADR-0011 D11).
- Second re-review:
  - Staged copies are bounded by the **measured** size, not the limit (Proxmox `head -c` of the measured size + 1 in the pipe form; `qemu-img dd` of the measured size + under 1 MiB). A copy longer than measured is refused.
  - VMDK: capacity 0 is refused (qemu's descriptor-file path), as is a grain directory at end (an unverifiable footer). The descriptor must be NUL-terminated within its declared size, the extent file must be a plain name, and qemu's parent region is scanned.
  - vSphere: staged copies are bounded by the `/tmp` emptyDir `sizeLimit`, read from `VIRTRIGAUD_TMP_SIZE_LIMIT`, which `internal/controller/provider_controller.go` and `charts/virtrigaud/templates/provider-vsphere-deployment.yaml` set, minus the current `/tmp` usage. Free space uses Bavail × Frsize.
  - `CheckStagedImageBytes` returns the declared virtual size and refuses one above the limit.
  - All three providers' S3 downloads are bounded by the object's reported size (`BoundedWriter`), with a free-space pre-check.
  - A raw image that qemu would probe as a VMDK descriptor is refused.
- Final review:
  - `internal/storage/migration/image_header_test.go`: real qemu-img `streamOptimized` and `monolithicSparse` VMDKs pass the header check. Both keep the grain directory offset in the header, as VirtRigaud's vSphere export does (a `sparseMonolithic` clone, or a qemu-img flatten). A grain directory at end (VMware NFC/OVF footer layout) stays refused; ADR-0011 records why.
  - ADR-0011, `docs/upgrading.md`: the import's free-space check covers twice the staged file size. A compressed staged image can expand up to its virtual size when converted. Set a disk-size limit (#382) on Providers whose hosts are shared.
- Logging: left-behind causes are logged at V(1). Provider delete failures log the reason at Warn, and the stderr, host and path at debug.

### Why
Option A from the v0.4.0-rc1 backlog (#15): staged migration disks on NFS and S3 were never deleted, and the manager-side cleanup could not reach them while it silently blocked the Ready cleanup. The security review (REQUEST CHANGES) added: the maintainer decisions D1 (guard), D2 (`EMPTIED` accepted) and D3 (fix the NFS name in rc1); findings M1–M4 and L; and the pre-existing import header gap.

### Impact
- [x] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-12 15:36] - Proxmox: imported-disk Create confined to the VM's own namespaced migration stage
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note.** Upgrade the manager before the Proxmox provider: an older manager sends neither `VMImage.ImportedDisk` nor `ImportDiskRequest.target_vm`, and the new provider refuses every Proxmox-target migration without them. A migration into another namespace through a Proxmox target Provider now fails at `Validating` (`ProxmoxCrossNamespaceTarget`) before anything is exported. Stale stages (a migration failed or deleted between import and create) are not removed yet: sweep `/var/lib/virtrigaud/import-stage` periodically (docs/upgrading.md, "Stale Proxmox import stages"). **A Proxmox-target migration between its import and its create at upgrade time must be run again**: its stage carries the old bare name and is refused. Remove leftover `/var/tmp/.virtrigaud-import-*` files on the PVE nodes by hand once no migration is in flight; the provider never removes a bare-name stage. See `docs/upgrading.md`.

### Security
- `internal/providers/proxmox/import_stage.go` (new), `server.go` (`parseCreateRequest`), `s3import.go` (`createFromImportedDisk`, `cleanupNodeFile`, `buildImportDiskCommand`), `create_errors.go` (`importStageReady`): Proxmox Create no longer imports and deletes an arbitrary node file. High/Critical; affects v0.3.11 and later (#259). Precondition: the Proxmox migration SSH data plane is configured.
  - **Before:** any `contracts.VMImage.Path` without a `TemplateName` was taken as a migration stage. Create ran `qm importdisk <vmid> <path>` over SSH and then `rm -f <path>`, ignoring `VMImage.ImportedDisk`. `VirtualMachine.spec.importedDisk.path` is tenant-writable, so a tenant could copy any file or block device the SSH user can read on the PVE node (another tenant's VM disk, `/etc/pve/priv/*`, keys) into their own VM, and the provider then deleted the source. It also bypassed any disk-size cap.
  - **Now:** Create takes the importdisk path only when `ImportedDisk` is true, which the manager sets only for the VM's own verified migration disk (`isOwnMigrationDisk`). The path must also be byte-for-byte this VM's stage, `/var/lib/virtrigaud/import-stage/<namespace>_<vm name>-migrated.<qcow2|raw|vmdk>`. The namespace comes from `CreateRequest.owner`, and the owner's name must match the VM name. A name over 200 bytes is bounded with a SHA-256 hash, as vSphere landing names are. Anything else is refused with `InvalidArgument` and a constant message (`importedDiskRejectedMessage`, never the path) before any PVE or SSH call. Nothing is created.
  - `qm importdisk` runs in the same shell command as a node-side check (`importStageNodeCheck`). The stage must be a regular file, not a symbolic link, with one hard link, owned by the running user (root on a PVE node, `stat -c %u` = `id -u`), and with no group or other write bit (`stat -c %a` & 022 = 0). The check is tested against real files with the local `sh` and `bash`. A failed check fails the import, and the VM shell is rolled back. `cleanupNodeFile` removes only paths matching the anchored stage pattern (`isImportStagePath`), with `rm -f --`. The interrupted-create rebuild (`importStageReady`, #380) re-validates the path and runs the same node check.
  - **Legacy:** a stage an earlier release wrote under the bare name `/var/tmp/.virtrigaud-import-<vm name>-migrated.<ext>` is refused even for the VM's own verified migration, as vSphere (#379) refuses bare-name landings: same-named VMs in different namespaces shared that file, so it cannot be proven to be this VM's disk. The refusal is `InvalidArgument` with the constant `legacyImportStageMessage` ("run the migration again"); nothing is created and nothing runs on the node. `isImportStagePath` matches only namespaced stages (`<ns>_<...>-migrated.<ext>`), so the provider never removes a bare-name file; it is left for manual cleanup. ImportDisk never writes that name again.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/s3import.go` (`importDiskFromS3`), `nfs.go` (`importDiskFromNFS`): ImportDisk names the stage from `ImportDiskRequest.target_vm` (namespace and name), never from the bare `target_name`. A same-named VM in another namespace therefore gets a different stage, and neither can name the other's. A request without `target_vm`, with an invalid identity, or whose `target_name` is not `<vm>-migrated` is refused with `InvalidArgument` before any node command. The `imported-disk-<unix time>` fallback name is gone.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/import_stage.go` (`proxmoxImportStageDir`, `importStagePath`, `isImportStagePath`, `buildImportStageScript`, `buildNFSImportStageScript`), `s3import.go`, `nfs.go`: stages no longer live in world-writable `/var/tmp` under a predictable name. Before, another account on the PVE node could pre-create, link or swap a stage there.
  - **Location:** stages now live in `/var/lib/virtrigaud/import-stage/<namespace>_<vm name>-migrated.<format>`. ImportDisk (re)creates that directory with `install -d -m 0700` and verifies it is not a symlink, is owned by the SSH user, and has mode 700, or fails.
  - **Write:** the disk is written to a fresh `mktemp` file in that directory (umask 077), then renamed onto the stage with `mv -T`. A failure or SSH hang-up removes the temp file.
  - **NFS (`nfsStageCopy`, the one producer of the root-owned copy):** the staged object is copied byte for byte into the root-owned `$TMP`; no qemu-img convert runs. With `nfs.uid`/`gid`, the reader runs under setpriv and holds **only the write end of a pipe**: `setpriv … cat -- "$MNT"/<rel> | cat > "$TMP"`, where the root side opens the copy.
    - The tenant-chosen identity may be a node account (33/www-data runs pveproxy). It therefore never gets a descriptor on the copy, nor ownership of it, and cannot rewrite the copy after it is checked (review N1).
    - An earlier revision of this branch converted as that identity and adopted the inode it wrote; that is gone.
    - The reader's exit status is recorded by the root side in a status file (fd 3, closed for the reader), and a failed read fails the script; POSIX sh has no pipefail.
    - Without uid/gid, the root shell reads the export.
    - Tested with a fake `setpriv` that records its open descriptors.
  - **Single source of truth:** one builder (`importStagePath`) and one predicate (`isImportStagePath`) define the stage location.
  - **Verification:** the S3 script and the uid-less NFS script are tested against real files with the local `sh` and `bash` (and `qemu-img`).
  - **Legacy `/var/tmp` stages:** they stay refused and are never removed.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/import_size_limit.go` (`checkNodeImportSize`, #382): the target-side disk-size check reads and removes only an import stage (`isImportStagePath`); any other path is refused untouched. It runs on the root-owned stage in the stage directory, never on the NFS object. `import_size_limit_test.go` now sends `target_vm` and expects the new stage path and `rm -f --`.
- `internal/storage/migration/nfs.go` (`ValidateNFSIdentity`, `ErrNFSRootIdentity`), `options.go` (`ParseStorageOptions`): an NFS uid or gid of 0 is refused by `NFSURL` (libvirt, vSphere) and by `ParseStorageOptions` (Proxmox presents the identity with setpriv), with the constant `ErrNFSRootIdentity` (review N4). The accepted range is now [1, 2^32-1]. The manager already refused it at Validating (`NFSRootIdentityNotAllowed`); this covers any other sender. No minimum beyond 0 is imposed.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_proxmox_target.go` (new), `vmmigration_controller.go` (`handleValidatingPhase`, `handleImportingPhase`): the manager refuses a VMMigration whose target Provider is Proxmox and whose target VM is in another namespace than the migration. The target VM's create would be refused anyway, because the disk is not verified as its own-namespace migration disk.
  - It fails at Validating, before any export or import: `Phase=Failed`, `Validating=False`, reason `ProxmoxCrossNamespaceTarget`, the constant `proxmoxCrossNamespaceTargetMessage`, one `MigrationFailed` event, and no immediate requeue.
  - A migration that passed Validating before this check existed fails the same way at Importing, before `ImportDisk`.
  - Proven in envtest and with fake-client phase tests.
  - Same-namespace Proxmox migrations and other provider types are unchanged.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/import_stage.go` (`importedDiskFormat`), `server.go`, `s3import.go`, `pveapi/client.go`: `spec.importedDisk.format` is tenant-writable and becomes the `qm importdisk --format` value. Only `qcow2`, `raw` or `vmdk` is accepted; empty still defaults to qcow2. Any other value (another string or JSON type) is refused with `InvalidArgument` and the constant `importedDiskFormatRejectedMessage`, before anything is created. The comments are corrected: `--format` is the **target** format written into the VM's storage, and PVE still probes the stage's own format. A Create-side header check of the stage is not part of this change.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/nfs.go`, `s3import.go`: the node-side `qemu-img check` of a staged disk pins `-f qcow2`, so a vmdk descriptor or raw file published as a stage is refused instead of being probed (the staged image's header is checked in full by the migration staging-cleanup branch's header pre-parser).

### Changed
- `internal/providers/proxmox/s3_test.go`, `ssh_errors_test.go`, `importdisk_rebuild_test.go`, `import_stage_test.go` (new): imported-disk tests use the VM's own verified stage. New tests cover:
  - a foreign absolute path, another VM's block device, `ImportedDisk` false, missing or non-bool, traversal, another namespace's or VM's stage (new and legacy names), the VM's own legacy stage (its own constant message, every format, with or without an owner), other directories and extensions, and whitespace variants: each refused with the constant message, no node command, no PVE change;
  - an owner mismatch;
  - the own stage (qcow2/raw/vmdk) imported behind the node check, then removed;
  - a failed node check (symlink), with the shell rolled back and the stage kept;
  - `cleanupNodeFile` refusing non-stage paths;
  - the rebuild check;
  - stage naming and bounding;
  - ImportDisk (S3 and NFS) refusing a request without `target_vm`.
- `docs/upgrading.md`, `docs/release-notes/next.md`, `docs/image-preparation.md`, `docs/cross-namespace-targets.md`, `docs/vm-ownership.md`, `examples/migration/README.md`: document the Proxmox stage rule, the upgrade order and the in-flight handling, a periodic sweep of stale stages, and that each PVE node must be used by **one VirtRigaud installation** only (stage names are unique within one Kubernetes cluster, and every installation uses the same stage directory).

### Why
The Proxmox provider was the only one that did not confine `spec.importedDisk.path`; libvirt (#334) and vSphere (#379) already did. Any tenant could read any node file through it and have the provider delete the original.

### Impact
- [x] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only

## [2026-10-12 13:08] - v0.4.0-rc1 follow-ups: image-artifact holds, owner on single-host deletes, live Provider check before creating RPCs, force-delete gate for snapshots and migrations, observedGeneration, shared finalizer constants, RBAC group fix
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note.**
> - **Behavior change (clustered Providers):** `virtrigaud.io/force-delete` on a `VMSnapshot` or `VMMigration` whose VM is in **another namespace** than its `topology: cluster` Provider is ignored unless the Provider carries `infra.virtrigaud.io/allow-consumer-orphan-on-delete: "true"`, as for a `VirtualMachine` (#381). The object shows `ForceDeleteRefused=True/ForceDeleteNotAllowed` and its delete keeps being retried.
> - **Behavior change (Proxmox):** every delete now carries the VM's owner (adopted VMs and clone targets included), so the owner-checked Delete (#380) applies. A VM at the VMID that is not the VirtualMachine's (a reused VMID, a stale stamp from a previous owner, an unstamped VM renamed on the hypervisor) is left in place: the VirtualMachine is released with a `VMLeftOnHypervisor` Warning. A Proxmox template is never deleted (`Ready=False/VMIsImageArtifact`).
> - **Known limitations:** adoption does not re-stamp the VM it adopts, so an adopted Proxmox VM still carrying a previous owner's stamp is left in place on delete (`VM_NOT_OWNED` Warning); re-stamping is post-rc1. On single-host Proxmox only `Delete` is owner-checked: `Describe`, `Power`, `Reconfigure` and snapshot calls act on whatever VM holds the recorded VMID (a VMID reused after an out-of-band delete); owner-checking them needs a hold-and-reattach design.
> - **Behavior change (RBAC):** the `config/rbac` helper ClusterRoles now grant `infra.virtrigaud.io`; subjects already bound to them gain that access. Review the bindings before applying.

### Security
- `internal/controller/consumer_force_delete.go` (new), `vmsnapshot_controller.go` (`handleDeletion`), `vmmigration_snapshot_cleanup.go` (`releaseSourceSnapshotForDeletion`), `virtualmachine_clustered_orphan.go`: the cross-namespace force-delete gate now covers `VMSnapshot` and `VMMigration`. Low; capacity-accounting bypass on shared hosts.
  - **Before:** a consumer's `force-delete` released a `VMSnapshot` whose provider delete failed or could not be sent, or a `VMMigration` whose source snapshot delete failed, leaving the snapshot on a shared clustered host outside the accounting.
  - **Now:** honoured only when the VM's Provider is not clustered, is in the object's namespace, or allows consumers to leave state behind. Otherwise `ForceDeleteRefused=True/ForceDeleteNotAllowed` (constant message per object, one `Warning` event, status written only on change) and the delete is retried as if the annotation were not set. The Provider check is shared with the VirtualMachine gate (`consumerDetachDeniedFor`).
- `internal/controller/vmref.go` (`deleteRef`), `virtualmachine_controller.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/client.go` (`Delete`): single-host `DeleteRequest.owner` is now sent (the VM's UID, namespace and name), so Proxmox never destroys an unrelated VM that reused the VMID. vSphere, single-host libvirt and mock ignore it (tests added for each). Adopted `VirtualMachine`s (`virtrigaud.io/adopted=true`, clone targets included) send none: their VM may carry a previous owner's stamp.
- `internal/controller/provider_deleting_live.go` (new), `virtualmachine_controller.go` (`createVMOn`), `vmclone_controller.go` (`startClone`), `vmclone_clustered.go` (`startClusteredClone`), `vmmigration_controller.go` (`handleImportingPhase`): right before `Create`, `Clone` and `ImportDisk`, after the object recorded its use of the Provider, the Provider is re-read through the `APIReader`. A Provider being deleted, gone or replaced (other UID) holds the object with `Ready=False/ProviderDeleting` (constant message, one event, re-check every minute); nothing is sent. Closes the ADR-0010 race where a stale cache let a creating RPC run through a Provider whose in-use finalizer had already been released.

- `internal/providers/proxmox/vm_ownership.go` (`checkDelete`), `server.go` (`Delete`), `internal/providers/contracts/errors.go` (`VMNotOwnedReason`, `OwnerStampUnreadableReason`), `internal/transport/grpc/client.go` (`statusHasReason`, `mapGRPCError`), `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go` (`handleDeletion`): a Proxmox owner mismatch is answered `NotFound` + `VM_NOT_OWNED` (constant message) and the manager records it (`VMLeftOnHypervisor` Warning naming the VM's `status.id`; error-level log with the id, Provider and namespace/name; metric reason `vm-not-owned`) instead of releasing silently as if the VM were gone. A CR re-created under a new UID (e.g. a restore) no longer loses its running VM without a trace. A template at the VMID answers `FailedPrecondition` + `VM_IS_IMAGE_ARTIFACT` with or without an owner (before: an owner-less delete destroyed a VM converted to a template). An unreadable or multi-owner stamp carries `OWNER_STAMP_UNREADABLE`.
- `internal/controller/provider_inuse_live.go` (new), `provider_inuse.go` (`handleDeletion`), `provider_controller.go` (`APIReader`), `cmd/manager/main.go`: before a deleting Provider's in-use finalizer is removed, its usage is counted again from the API server (`liveIndexedReader`: one List per kind, paginated by 500, filtered by the cache index extractors). A use the cache had not seen (a just-written create marker) holds it. Closes the Provider side of the ADR-0010 race.
- `internal/controller/vmref.go` (`deleteRef`): the owner on deletes no longer depends on the tenant-editable `virtrigaud.io/adopted` label (it turned the reused-VMID protection off). Adopted VMs whose VM carries a stale stamp are left in place with a Warning (fail-safe). `contracts.AdoptedVMName` stays in the Proxmox name rule so unstamped adopted VMs still match. `virtualmachines/status` write is documented as platform-admin only.
- `config/rbac/*_admin_role.yaml`, `provider_*_role.yaml`: explicit verbs instead of `*`; the Provider roles carry `virtrigaud.io/role-scope: platform-admin`.

### Fixed
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_image_artifact_hold.go` (new), `virtualmachine_controller.go` (`handleDeletion`, `adjustPowerState`, `clearStaleDeleteHold`), `internal/k8s/conditions.go` (`ReasonVMIsImageArtifact`): a vSphere `Delete` or `Power` refused with `VM_IS_IMAGE_ARTIFACT` (`contracts.IsVMIsImageArtifact`) is held instead of retried every 15 s / 5 s as a generic failure. Delete: finalizer kept, `Ready=False/VMIsImageArtifact` (clustered: `DeleteBlocked=True/VMIsImageArtifact`, `Ready=False/DeleteBlocked`). Power: `Ready=False/VMIsImageArtifact`. Constant messages pointing at `virtrigaud.io/orphan-on-delete: "true"`, one `Warning` event, blocked-VM backoff (15 s to 5 min), no write on a repeated refusal; metric reason `vm-is-image-artifact`. `force-delete` and `orphan-on-delete` still release a held delete.
- `internal/k8s/conditions.go`, `internal/util/k8s/conditions.go` and every caller in `internal/controller` (114 call sites): `SetCondition` and the `Set*Condition` helpers take the owning object's generation and record it as `observedGeneration`. `internal/k8s` never set it; `internal/util/k8s` stored a per-change counter. `LastTransitionTime` semantics are unchanged in both, and a repeated call with the same values changes nothing (envtest pins that an unchanged VM reconcile writes nothing, before and after a spec change).
- `config/rbac/*_{admin,editor,viewer}_role.yaml`: the 15 helper ClusterRoles named the API group `infra.virtrigaud.io.infra.virtrigaud.io` and granted nothing; they now grant `infra.virtrigaud.io` (`internal/controller/rbac_helper_roles_test.go` pins it). The chart has no such roles; its manager RBAC already used the right group.

- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_image_artifact_hold.go` (`retainForRefusedDelete`), `internal/k8s/conditions.go` (`ReasonOwnerStampUnreadable`): a delete refused with `OWNER_STAMP_UNREADABLE` is held like the image-artifact refusal (`Ready=False/OwnerStampUnreadable`, constant message, one event, blocked-VM backoff; metric reason `owner-stamp-unreadable`) instead of retried every 15 s.
- `internal/controller/provider_deleting_live.go` (`holdIfProviderDeletingLive`, `markerDroppableUnsent`): a single-host Create stopped by the live Provider check replaces the create marker it wrote for that attempt alone with `Provisioning=False/ProviderDeleting` (nothing was sent), so it never ends as `CreateOutcomeUnknown`; a re-send keeps the earlier marker. The hold compares against the status as written.
- `internal/controller/vmsnapshot_conditions_envtest_test.go` (new): envtest pins that a repeated reconcile of a Ready VMSnapshot writes nothing after the `internal/util/k8s` change.

### Changed
- `internal/providers/contracts/adopted_name.go` (new), `internal/controller/vmadoption_controller.go`, `vmadoption_clustered.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/vm_ownership.go`: the adoption controller's `sanitizeVMName` is now `contracts.SanitizeVMName`, with `contracts.AdoptedVMName` (sanitized name or `vm-<id>`) as the single owner of the adopted-VM naming rule. Proxmox's owner-checked Delete accepts an unstamped VM whose adopted name is the owner's; any other name is still refused as a reused VMID.
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/vmsnapshot_types.go`, `vmclone_types.go`, `vmmigration_types.go`: exported `VMSnapshotFinalizer`, `VMCloneFinalizer` and `VMMigrationFinalizer` (values unchanged; no CRD or deepcopy change). Every finalizer literal and duplicated local constant in `internal/controller` uses them.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/pveapi/client.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/snapshot_node.go`: `VMIDInUse` removed; the snapshot node lookup uses `VMIDFree`, the one `/cluster/nextid?vmid=` probe (any answer other than 200 or 400 "already exists" is an error). Unit test added.
- `docs/upgrading.md`, `docs/release-notes/next.md`, `docs/vm-ownership.md`, `docs/vm-provider-binding.md`, `docs/adr/0010-provider-in-use-finalizer.md`: the behavior changes above.

### Why
Follow-ups from the v0.4.0-rc1 review after #376–#381: an image-artifact refusal hot-looped like a transient failure, single-host Proxmox deletes skipped the owner check #380 added, the cached Provider check left the ADR-0010 race open for creating RPCs, and snapshot/migration force-delete bypassed the consumer gate #381 added for VMs. The rest is cleanup the review asked for: correct `observedGeneration`, one finalizer constant per kind, one VMID probe, one adopted-name rule, and helper RBAC roles that grant something.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-12 13:32] - Administrator disk-size limit: --max-disk-size, per-Provider max-disk-size annotation, real-size checks for clones and migrations, opt-in VM/VMClass disk-size webhooks
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note.**
> - Nothing changes unless `manager.maxDiskSize` (`--max-disk-size`) is set or a Provider carries `infra.virtrigaud.io/max-disk-size`.
> - Before setting a limit, list the VMs and VMClasses above it: they keep running, but cloning, migrating or re-creating them, or growing their disks, is refused.
> - **Roll the provider images with the manager.** `GetDiskInfo` now lists every disk's size, and `ImportDisk` now enforces the limit on the disk it lands. An older provider image does neither: while a limit applies, clones through it are refused (`DiskSizeLimitUnverifiable`), and while a limit applies a migration into it is held (`DiskSizeLimitUnverifiable`, "upgrade the provider image"), because it does not report `supports_import_size_limit`.
> - Keep `vmmigrations/status` (like `virtualmachines/status`) writable by the manager only: the pre-import check trusts `status.diskInfo.sourceSize`.
> - A migration exported before a limit was set is held before its import (no recorded size). Delete it and migrate again.

### Added
- `cmd/manager/main.go`: `--max-disk-size` — the administrator's ceiling on every disk VirtRigaud creates or grows.
  - The value is a whole number of bytes from `1Gi` to `64Pi`; a larger value (e.g. `1e30`, which would otherwise read as no limit) or a fraction of a byte (`1.1Gi`) is refused, never clamped. Empty means no ceiling beyond the CRD's 64Ti per disk.
  - It is parsed before anything else starts. An invalid value (`500`, `0`, `none`, `1G`, `1023Mi`, ...) stops the manager with exit 1.
  - It is passed to the VirtualMachine, VMClone and VMMigration controllers.
  - The VM/VMClass disk-size webhooks are registered whenever webhooks are on.
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/disk_size_limit.go` (new):
  - `ProviderMaxDiskSizeAnnotation` (`infra.virtrigaud.io/max-disk-size`): a Provider's owner lowers the limit for that Provider. The limit that applies is the smaller of the two (`EffectiveMaxDiskSize`), so the annotation can never raise the ceiling.
  - On a clustered Provider shared with other namespaces, the Provider's owner is the administrator of its consumers.
  - Helpers: `ParseMaxDiskSize`, `DiskSizeGiBQuantity`, `ClassDiskSizeRequest`, `SpecDiskSizeRequests`, `FirstDiskOverLimit`.
  - Sizes are compared as `resource.Quantity`, so `500G` (about 465.7Gi) is smaller than a 500 GiB disk.
  - No CRD schema change.
- `proto/provider/v1/provider.proto`: `GetDiskInfoResponse.disks` (new `DiskCapacity` message, tag 10) — every disk of the VM, with its current virtual size, whatever `disk_id` asked for. The change is additive and backward-compatible.
  - Implemented in vSphere (every `VirtualDisk`'s capacity), libvirt (`qemu-img info` of every file-backed disk; a block, volume or network disk reports 0) and Proxmox (the `size=` of every attached bus disk; CD-ROM, cloud-init, unused and EFI/TPM volumes are skipped).
  - The mock provider still answers `GetDiskInfo` with Unimplemented, so clones through it fail closed under a limit.
  - Bindings regenerated. The transport client maps the new field.
- `proto/provider/v1/provider.proto`: `ImportDiskRequest.max_virtual_size_bytes` (field 12; additive) — the target Provider's limit for the import, 0 = none.
  - **Why:** the staged object can be replaced between the export and the import (a tenant-chosen NFS export, a staging PVC in the tenant's namespace), and the manager's earlier checks trust the source provider's report. The target provider now checks the disk it is about to land.
  - The provider reads the virtual size of the disk it is about to land, in a location the tenant cannot change, and refuses a larger one before anything is landed: `FailedPrecondition` with the ErrorInfo reason `DISK_SIZE_EXCEEDS_LIMIT`, or `DISK_SIZE_UNVERIFIABLE` when it cannot read the size. The message is constant.
  - Shared helper: `internal/providers/importlimit` (new).
  - **vSphere** (`import_size_limit.go`): the pod-local vmdk, right before the datastore upload or the NFC lease (pvc, s3, nfs).
  - **libvirt** (`import_size_limit.go`, `imagepath.go` `inspectHostImageInfoAs`):
    - s3: the private staged copy, reusing the existing header read;
    - nfs: early from the existing header read, and again on the converted disk in the private directory before it is published;
    - pvc: a private copy of the staged file before it becomes the volume — the host copy over SSH (removed on refusal), or, over a local connection, a copy in the provider's own container (`privateLocalImportCopy`; previously the tenant's file was read in place twice).
  - **Proxmox** (`import_size_limit.go`): the node-local stage that `qm importdisk` lands (s3, nfs), removed on refusal. The pvc path is rejected earlier and is unchanged.
  - The mock provider ignores the field.
  - `GetCapabilitiesResponse.supports_import_size_limit` (field 24; additive), advertised by vSphere, single-host libvirt and Proxmox (`sdk` `CapabilityImportSizeLimit`). While a limit applies, a migration into a target that does not report it is held in `Validating` (before any export) or `Importing`. Without a limit, nothing changes.
  - `internal/transport/grpc/client.go` sends the field and maps the two refusals to a non-retryable Conflict marked `ErrDiskSizeExceedsLimit` / `ErrDiskSizeUnverifiable` (`contracts`), never counted toward the circuit breaker.
- `internal/controller/disk_size_limit.go`, `disk_size_limit_copies.go` (new): enforcement before the provider call that would create or grow a disk, whether or not webhooks are on.
  - **VirtualMachine create and re-create**: a VMClass `spec.diskDefaults.size` or any `spec.disks[].sizeGiB` above the limit holds the VM. On a libvirt Provider, a class with no size counts as the libvirt default primary disk, 20Gi.
    - No image prepare, placement or Create is sent.
    - Conditions: `Ready=False` and `Provisioning=False`, reason `DiskSizeExceedsLimit`. If the create marker is set, only `Ready` changes and the marker survives.
    - Status is written only on change, with one Warning event per hold, and the VM is re-checked every 2 minutes.
  - **Reconfigure**: a disk size above the limit is sent as 0, which every provider reads as "leave this disk as it is".
    - CPU and memory changes go ahead. No disk is grown beyond the limit, and none is shrunk.
    - It is recorded as `DiskSizeWithinLimit=False` (new condition type) on every outcome (done, async task, pending restart, failure), with one Warning per VM and message. It is removed by the next Reconfigure that withholds nothing, or by a reconcile once the spec's sizes fit the limit again.
    - On a Proxmox Provider no `spec.disks` size is sent once one is withheld. Proxmox applies every entry to scsi0 and refuses a smaller one as a shrink, so withholding one entry would otherwise expose a later, smaller entry to that check and turn the Reconfigure into a retried failure.
  - **VMClone**: before the Clone RPC, every disk of the source is checked by the size its provider reports (`GetDiskInfo` `disks`), never by its VMClass or `spec.disks`. A lowered class, a removed `spec.disks` entry or an adopted VM can no longer bypass the limit. The target-class override is checked too. A held clone stays `Pending` with `Ready=False`.
  - **VMMigration**: checked against the target Provider's limit at three points:
    - in `Validating`, the source's primary disk (real size, `GetDiskInfo`) and the target VMClass;
    - right before `ExportDisk`, the disk being exported (same VM, disk and snapshot), whose size is recorded in `status.diskInfo.sourceSize`;
    - right before `ImportDisk`, that recorded size, and the provider then enforces the limit on the disk it lands (`max_virtual_size_bytes`).
    - A provider refusal at import holds the migration in `Importing`. A `DISK_SIZE_EXCEEDS_LIMIT` refusal is not re-sent until the limit changes (its message names the limit). An unverifiable size is re-sent on a doubling backoff (2 minutes to 32 minutes; each attempt is a full download or convert), reset by a successful import.

    A held migration stays in its phase, with `Validating`, `Exporting` or `Importing` set to False.
  - Fail closed (`DiskSizeLimitUnverifiable`) in these cases:
    - an invalid Provider annotation;
    - a disk size the provider does not report, or a read error (the provider's error text and disk paths never reach status);
    - an import with no recorded size while a limit applies.
  - Without a limit, no `GetDiskInfo` is sent, and an unreadable target Provider never delays an export.
- `internal/k8s/conditions.go`: `ConditionDiskSizeWithinLimit`, `ReasonDiskSizeExceedsLimit`, `ReasonDiskSizeLimitUnverifiable`.
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/disk_size_webhook.go` (new): `vvirtualmachine-disksize.kb.io` and `vvmclass-disksize.kb.io` validating webhooks.
  - They refuse a `spec.disks[].sizeGiB` or `spec.diskDefaults.size` above `--max-disk-size`, or growing one beyond it.
  - A stored size already above it can be kept or lowered. Repeated disk names are matched by occurrence.
  - They check only the manager's ceiling. The controllers enforce both the ceiling and the Provider annotation.
  - Served whenever webhooks are on. Without a ceiling they admit everything.
  - `config/webhook/manifests.yaml` regenerated. It always lists them with `failurePolicy: Fail`; see the chart README for kustomize installs.
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/provider_webhook.go`: refuses an invalid `infra.virtrigaud.io/max-disk-size` value on create, and on update when it is new or changed.
- Chart (`charts/virtrigaud/values.yaml`, `templates/manager-deployment.yaml`, `templates/_helpers.tpl` `virtrigaud.maxDiskSizeValue`, `templates/webhooks.yaml`): `manager.maxDiskSize` becomes `--max-disk-size`.
  - Anything the manager refuses fails the render: no unit of at least G, zero, `none`, or a value below 1Gi such as `1G` or `0.5Gi`.
  - The two disk-size webhooks render only with webhooks on and `manager.maxDiskSize` set, with the same caBundle and `failurePolicy` as `vprovider.kb.io`.
- `hack/verify-max-disk-size-render.sh` (new), `make verify-max-disk-size-render`, and a CI step. The check asserts:
  - no flag and no webhooks by default;
  - the flag is rendered when set;
  - the webhooks render coherent and in sync with `config/webhook/manifests.yaml`;
  - invalid and sub-1Gi values fail the render while boundary values (`1Gi`, `1.1G`) render;
  - `--reuse-values` from v0.3.11 still renders.
- Tests:
  - API: parsing (aligned with the chart boundaries), the effective limit, webhook table tests (including repeated names), the Provider annotation.
  - Controller: create, re-create, the libvirt default, the create marker surviving a hold, Reconfigure withholding on every outcome, the Proxmox guard, clone and migration by real sizes (unknown size, read error, old provider), the export and import re-checks, no read without a limit.
  - Envtest: VM, VMClone and VMMigration condition writes, written once.
  - Providers: vSphere (vcsim) and Proxmox (pvefake) `GetDiskInfo` disk lists, and `SizeGiB=0` is a no-op in vSphere, Proxmox and libvirt Reconfigure.
  - Manager: an invalid flag exits 1.
- Docs:
  - `charts/virtrigaud/README.md` ("Disk-size limit"), including that Proxmox Create does not apply `Class.DiskDefaults` and that VMImage `status.providerStatus[].size` is never filled;
  - `docs/upgrading.md`, `docs/release-notes/next.md`;
  - `docs/vm-provider-binding.md`: keep `vmmigrations/status` manager-only.
- Tests (import enforcement):
  - `importlimit` unit tests;
  - vSphere: a 2 TiB sparse streamOptimized vmdk refused against 100 GiB, with real qemu-img;
  - libvirt: the host check and the shared header read on real qcow2 images;
  - Proxmox: `ImportDisk` over NFS end to end against a fake node — oversized and unreadable sizes refused with the stage removed; within the limit, or with no limit, staged;
  - the client's wire field and refusal mapping;
  - the migration controller holding on a provider refusal, not re-sending it for the same limit, and re-sending after a limit change.

### Why
Until now the only bound on a VM disk was the CRD's 64Ti. A tenant who owns its namespace could fill a shared datastore or pool through new disks, resizes, VMClass `diskDefaults`, additional disks, clones and migrations. In regulated multi-tenant deployments the cap must be one a tenant cannot raise.

A clone or migration copies the source's real disks, so it is checked by their real sizes. Images or templates larger than the class are not covered: no image's size is known before the Create, and refusing every image-based create under a limit would break normal use.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [x] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-12 10:37] - VirtualMachine controller: durable single-host create marker, force-delete gated for clustered consumers, no transport errors in status, quieter deleting VMs, OffGraceful loop fixed, no create on a deleting Provider, create backoff and refusals
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note.**
> - **Behavior change (clustered Providers):** `virtrigaud.io/force-delete` on a VM in **another namespace** than its `topology: cluster` Provider is now ignored unless the Provider carries `infra.virtrigaud.io/allow-consumer-orphan-on-delete: "true"` (the orphan-on-delete permission). The VM shows `ForceDeleteRefused=True/ForceDeleteNotAllowed` and its delete keeps being retried. Same-namespace VMs and single-host Providers are unchanged.
> - **Behavior change (single-host Providers):** before a Create, a VM now records `Provisioning=True/CreateRequested`. If the Create's outcome is never recorded, vSphere, libvirt and Proxmox are sent the Create again: they re-bind the VM they stamped. Roll the Proxmox provider with the owner stamp (#380) with or before this manager; an older Proxmox image does not stamp, and a re-send there makes a second VM. A delete that cannot find the VM by its stamp waits with `Ready=False/CreateOutcomeUnknown`. The operator records `status.id`, or annotates `virtrigaud.io/create-outcome=not-created@<attempt id>` (the marker's `lastTransitionTime`), or (delete only) uses force-delete. See `docs/vm-provider-binding.md`.
> - Search events for `VMRecordNotSaved` (a provider VM id the manager created but could not record) and `CreateOutcomeUnknown`.

### Security
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_clustered_orphan.go` (`forceDeleteHonoured`, `consumerDetachDenied`), `virtualmachine_controller.go` (`handleDeletion`, `retainForUnavailableProvider`), `virtualmachine_clustered.go` (`retainForUnroutableDelete`), `internal/k8s/conditions.go`: force-delete is gated like orphan-on-delete for cross-namespace consumers of a clustered Provider. Low; capacity-accounting bypass on shared hosts.
  - **Before:** a consumer could set `force-delete` on its VM while its delete was held (`ProviderUnavailable`, `HostUnreachable`, `DiskCheckFailed`, `DiskInUse`, `OwnDomainOnAnotherHost`) or failing, or while its Provider was refused (`ConsumerNotAllowed`, `ProviderRefMismatch`), and the finalizer was released without a provider Delete. The domain kept running on the shared hosts outside the committed-capacity accounting. `orphan-on-delete` was already gated for that case (review M4).
  - **Now:** for a bound VM (or one whose own domain was found on another host) in another namespace than its clustered Provider, force-delete is honoured only when the Provider carries `infra.virtrigaud.io/allow-consumer-orphan-on-delete: "true"`. Otherwise the annotation is ignored and the delete is retried as if it were not set. New condition `ForceDeleteRefused=True` with reason `ForceDeleteNotAllowed`, a constant message, and one `Warning` event when it is set. It is removed when the annotation goes or the Provider allows it. Metric reason `force-delete-not-allowed`.
  - `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/provider_types.go`: GoDoc only. `ProviderAllowConsumerOrphanOnDeleteAnnotation` now also covers force-delete. No schema change.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_status_messages.go` (new), `virtualmachine_controller.go`, `virtualmachine_reconfigure_result.go`, `virtualmachine_clustered.go`: raw resolver and provider transport errors no longer reach VirtualMachine status. Low; information disclosure (ADR-0007 A6 threat 5).
  - **Before:** on the non-delete path, a `getProviderInstance` failure copied the resolver error into `Ready`. That error can name the TLS Secret's namespace/name, the provider Service's ClusterIP:port and the runtime phase. The describe, power, reconfigure, task-check and create failure conditions copied gRPC transport text, which names the dial target. A consumer of a clustered Provider in another namespace could read all of it.
  - **Now:**
    - A resolver failure sets the constant `providerResolveFailedMessage`.
    - A transport failure sets the constant `providerNotReachedDetail`. Transport failures are gRPC `Unavailable`, `DeadlineExceeded` and `Canceled`, a context deadline or cancellation, and provider errors typed Unavailable or Timeout. Marked provider answers such as `HOST_UNAVAILABLE`, `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED`, `VM_SOURCE_RUNNING` and `IN_PROGRESS` are still shown.
    - Other provider answers are shown through `sanitizeProviderDetail`: URL userinfo stripped, one line, at most 256 bytes.
    - The cause goes to the manager log only.
  - **Audit:** the delete path already used constant messages. VMClone's equivalent is handled separately.

### Fixed
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_create_record.go`, `virtualmachine_create_marker.go` (new), `virtualmachine_controller.go` (`createVMOn`, `reconcileVM`, `handleDeletion`, `removeFinalizer`, `vmUpdateNeedsReconcile`), `internal/k8s/conditions.go`, `cmd/manager/main.go` (`APIReader` wiring): a single-host Create can no longer lose `status.id` and then orphan the VM on delete. Medium.
  - **Cause:** after a provider Create, the status write that carried the new id was a plain `Status().Update`, and its error was swallowed. A Conflict lost the id. The usual trigger is the VM being edited, or its deletion requested, during a long Create. After that:
    - the next reconcile sent a second Create;
    - deleting the VM released the finalizer without a provider Delete, so the hypervisor VM was left running.

    Clustered VMs were safe because `pendingHost` is recorded before Create.
  - **Fix: a durable create marker.**
    - Before a single-host Create, the VM records `Provisioning=True` with reason `CreateRequested` (`k8s.ReasonCreateRequested`, constant message, observedGeneration) and `status.boundProvider`. The marker is written over the object as read live, with `Status().Update` and that read's resourceVersion (optimistic lock), and confirmed before the RPC. A failed write sends nothing, a Conflict included.
    - It is not a JSON Patch test of `/status/id`. The API server fails such a test when `/status` is absent, and a new VirtualMachine has no status, so the first marker write would fail forever (re-review CRITICAL, reproduced in envtest).
    - Each marker write is one attempt, identified by its `lastTransitionTime` (RFC 3339, strictly increasing).
    - Right before the Create, the VM is re-read live through the uncached `APIReader` (review M1). There is no Create when the VM is gone or replaced, when it records an id, or when it shows a marker the cached copy did not.
    - The Create's outcome replaces the marker once the id is recorded. The marker is kept when the outcome is unknown: a transport failure, or an error the provider did not classify as a refusal.
    - These replace it:
      - Conflict, InvalidSpec, NotFound, NotSupported, Unauthorized and QuotaExceeded;
      - an answer carrying the new ErrorInfo reason `CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED` (`contracts.CreateNotPerformedReason`, `IsCreateNotPerformed`): the provider made nothing, so the Create is safe to retry or to treat as refused;
      - a non-retryable FailedPrecondition or PermissionDenied (Q, below).
    - `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`, `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` and `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED` keep the marker: the outcome is unknown. A provider also sends them for an operation that may still complete on its host, for example libvirt's "outcome unknown" and "the same copy is still running".
    - For Proxmox: InvalidSpec, NotFound, PermissionDenied, AlreadyExists, and `CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED` are definite. A plain Unavailable keeps the marker.
    - Any failure answering a re-send keeps the marker (review M1, re-review H1): it is the answer to the re-send only, and says nothing about the earlier attempt. This covers a marker re-sent to vSphere, libvirt or Proxmox, and a re-create of a vanished VM. vSphere answers Conflict for its own VM while the clone is still running, and an InvalidSpec, PermissionDenied or CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED re-send does not undo what the first attempt made.
    - Re-sends are backed off from the marker's last attempt (re-review L1): 15 s, then about as long as the failures have lasted, up to 5 min. Waiting writes nothing.
    - No Create is sent when the live object is being deleted, or has a newer generation than the request was built from (re-review L2).
    - A failure before the provider call (spec validation, building the request) is recorded on Ready only while the marker is present (review M2).
    - A marker without an id:
      - vSphere, libvirt and Proxmox are sent the Create again; they re-bind the VM stamped with the VM's UID. Proxmox stamps since #380 (P).
      - Every other type (the mock provider) waits with `Ready=False/CreateOutcomeUnknown`, a constant message and one `Warning` event, re-checked every minute. An operator resolves it by recording `status.id` (status patch) or annotating `virtrigaud.io/create-outcome=not-created@<attempt id>` (review M3).
      - The annotation names one attempt. Any other value is ignored and removed, and the annotation is removed before every new attempt. When it authorizes a create or a release, a `CreateOutcomeConfirmed` Warning event records it.
      - A re-send or a confirmed create goes ahead only while the live object still carries the attempt (and the confirmation) it was decided on (review L2).
    - Delete of a marker VM without an id is never released silently:
      - libvirt is asked (ListVMs owner stamps) for the VM stamped with the VM's UID, and that VM is deleted by id.
      - Without such a VM, the finalizer is released only on positive confirmation (review HIGH): once no Create can still be running (10 min), every domain name the Create could have used is described and must answer a definite NotFound. Those names are `<namespace>.<name>` (hash-shortened beyond 200 bytes) and the bare legacy name. The release records a Normal `CreateConfirmedAbsent` event. A lossy ListVMs alone proves nothing.
      - The single-host libvirt provider now answers a Describe of an absent domain with NotFound (re-review M1, below), so this confirmation can fire.
      - Proxmox is also looked up by owner stamp, and a stamped VM is deleted by id. A VMID cannot be confirmed absent by name, so with none listed the delete is held (P).
      - Any listed VM that reports `owner_stamp_state` makes the lookup ambiguous, and the delete is held (P).
      - Otherwise, and on vSphere, the delete is held with `CreateOutcomeUnknown` (blocked-VM backoff). Force-delete releases with `VMLeftOnHypervisor`, orphan-on-delete detaches, and a matching `not-created@<attempt id>` releases (re-checked live, audited).
    - A marker VM whose `spec.providerRef` no longer names its recorded Provider is refused (`ProviderRefMismatch`).
  - **The id record:**
    - It is a status JSON Patch with tests on `/metadata/uid` and `/status/id` and no resourceVersion precondition, retried on transient API and transport errors (`isRetriableRecordError`, reused from VMClone). Each attempt is bounded by 5 s (review L3).
    - Every failure is resolved with a live read (review M1, L2). The same id stored counts as success. Another id stored is not overwritten: a `VMRecordNotSaved` event names the VM this Create made. The record is dropped only when the VM is gone or has another UID.
  - **In-memory record (`unsavedCreates`), kept:** it holds the id, which the marker cannot. While the manager runs, the next reconcile writes the record without a Create on every provider type, including Proxmox, which would otherwise need an operator. A delete meanwhile deletes the VM by id, vSphere included. It is forgotten whenever a reconcile reads an id or re-creates a vanished VM (review L1).
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go` (`vmUpdateNeedsReconcile`): a VirtualMachine being deleted is no longer reconciled on every update, including its own status writes.
  - It is now reconciled when its deletion is requested, and then only when its generation, annotations or finalizers change. Force-delete and orphan-on-delete still take effect at once. Labels are not read by the delete path.
  - Every delete-path hold already returns an explicit `RequeueAfter`. None relies on an immediate requeue.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_power_observed.go` (`powerStateSatisfied`), `virtualmachine_controller.go`: an `OffGraceful` VM no longer loops. Medium.
  - **Cause:** providers report a powered-off VM as `Off` (vSphere, libvirt, Proxmox, mock), which never equalled `OffGraceful`. Every reconcile therefore sent `SHUTDOWN_GRACEFUL`. On vSphere that fell back to PowerOff, failed with `InvalidPowerState`, and set `Ready=False/ProviderError` every few seconds. This feeds the circuit breaker, and it starts at creation now that vSphere Create no longer powers on.
  - **Fix:** observed `Off` now satisfies `OffGraceful`. The Suspended/Unknown rules (R1, H4, L3) are unchanged.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_provider_deleting.go` (new), `virtualmachine_controller.go` (`reconcileVM`), `internal/k8s/conditions.go`: a VirtualMachine is no longer created through a Provider that is being deleted. Low.
  - **Cause:** a VM created on a Provider with a `deletionTimestamp` would hold that Provider in use (ADR-0010) indefinitely. A VM is now created only through a Provider that is not being deleted.
  - **Fix:** the hold applies, before any provider call, to:
    - an unbound VM;
    - a bound single-host VM whose hypervisor VM is gone and would be re-created.

    The VM gets `Ready=False` and `Provisioning=False` with reason `ProviderDeleting`, one `Warning` event, and is re-checked every minute (metric reason `provider-deleting`). The constant message tells the owner to point `spec.providerRef` at another Provider or delete the VM (review M2). Nothing is scheduled on a clustered Provider either.
  - The hold never writes the create marker, so the held VM does not keep the Provider in use. A VM that already carries the marker keeps it, with only `Ready` set.
  - **Unchanged:** a VM the provider already created (an unsaved create record, a clustered create in flight) and every created VM are managed as before.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_create_backoff.go` (new), `virtualmachine_controller.go`, `virtualmachine_clustered.go` (`handleClusteredCreateError`): a Create answered with a retryable `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED` or `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` is retried with a backoff. Low.
  - **Cause:** it was retried every 5 s, forever, outside the circuit breaker (which ignores both by design). Each retry cost a disk scan or a full create attempt.
  - **Fix:**
    - The retry uses the blocked-VM backoff (15 s doubling to 5 min), counted from the start of the hold (review L1). Ready is removed and set anew on the transition, so an older `Ready=False` does not shorten it.
    - The message is constant, and there is one `Warning` event on the transition. `Ready` is not rewritten per retry, although each retry rewrites the create marker before its Create.
    - Metric reason `provider-create-backoff`.
  - A `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED` or `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` Create keeps the create marker; its outcome is unknown.
  - Other retry intervals are unchanged.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go` (single-host `Describe`), `server.go` (`Describe`), `staging.go` (`virshNoDomain`): a single-host Describe of an absent domain is now `NotFound`, `codes.NotFound` on the wire (re-review M1).
  - It is recognised only by the existing `virshNoDomainMarkers` on the virsh error's stderr. Every other failure keeps its retryable error and the historical `codes.Unknown`.
  - Without this, the delete-time positive confirmation could never fire: the provider answered an absent domain with a retryable "failed to get domain info".
  - The VirtualMachine controller still treats a failed Describe as before, so a missing single-host libvirt VM is not re-created.
- `internal/providers/contracts/libvirt_domain_names.go` (new): the libvirt domain-name rule shared by the provider and the manager (re-review L5). The controller's copy had drifted: its legacy name did not exclude names virsh reads as a domain ID or UUID.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_create_marker.go` (`createRebindsOwnedVM`): Proxmox re-binding is decided by provider type, because GetCapabilities reports no owner-stamp capability. Roll the Proxmox provider before or with this manager.
- `internal/providers/contracts/errors.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/client.go` (`mapGRPCError`): new ErrorInfo reason `CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED`. The provider made nothing, and the Create is safe to retry or to treat as refused. The transport marks the mapped error with `ErrCreateNotPerformed` whatever the code. The Proxmox branch emits it for its "nothing remains" cases.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_create_backoff.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/client.go` (`mapGRPCError`, `untypedRPCError`), `internal/k8s/conditions.go`: a Create refused with a non-retryable FailedPrecondition or PermissionDenied is held with a backoff (Q). Low.
  - **Cause:** the refusal went through `providerFailureOutcome` and was retried every 5 s forever, with its outcome treated as unknown. An example is the vSphere "imported disk not found … run the VMMigration again".
  - **Fix:**
    - The refusal counts as nothing made: the marker is replaced, and `Ready` and `Provisioning` say `CreateRefused` with a constant message. This relies on the providers answering FailedPrecondition only before creating anything; the vSphere one does. The assumption is commented in the code.
    - One `Warning` event on the transition carries the provider's sanitized answer.
    - It is re-checked on the blocked-VM backoff.
    - The transport keeps the gRPC status in the chain of an answer it does not categorize (text unchanged), so the controller can read its code. This also makes a `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` on `codes.Unknown` visible.
  - `VM_IS_IMAGE_ARTIFACT` (the vSphere Delete/Power refusal of #377) is not held specifically yet: it takes the generic failed-delete path with the finalizer kept. A dedicated hold is a follow-up.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go` (`handleRejectedCreate`): a rejected Create's provider message is sanitized (`sanitizeProviderDetail`: URL userinfo removed, one line, at most 256 bytes) (review L4).

### Tests
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_create_record_test.go`: covers
  - an edit, and a deletion request, during Create;
  - persistent and transient record failures: no second Create, and the delete reaches the provider;
  - a replaced VM, and an Invalid answer for the same VM (L2);
  - a newer id that is not overwritten (M1);
  - bounded attempts (L3);
  - forgetting the in-memory record (L1);
  - the patch shape.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_create_marker_test.go`: covers
  - the marker stored before the Create;
  - a failed marker write means no Create;
  - unknown outcome keeps the marker, while a refusal replaces it;
  - no blind re-Create on Proxmox or mock, with resolution by `not-created@<attempt id>`;
  - a lingering annotation from an older attempt, or a malformed one, is ignored and removed;
  - the audit event on create and on delete;
  - the live check of the decision (L2), and attempt ids that increase;
  - a pre-request failure keeps the marker (M2);
  - a Conflict on a re-send keeps it (M1);
  - only `CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED` (and the refusals) replace the marker on a first Create; `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`, `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` and `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED` keep it;
  - every failure of a re-send keeps it, including Conflict, InvalidSpec, PermissionDenied and `CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED` (H1);
  - re-sends are backed off from the last attempt, and nothing is written while waiting (L1);
  - no Create for a live VM that is being deleted or has a newer spec (L2);
  - the confirmation's audit event is recorded only after the marker write (L3);
  - a logged annotation value is truncated (L4);
  - re-Create on vSphere and libvirt;
  - a stale cache (marker, or id) never creates;
  - delete: owner-stamp lookup on libvirt; release only when every domain name answers a definite not-found (HIGH), held when the domain exists, the answer is untyped or the provider is unreachable, or the marker is recent; hold on vSphere and Proxmox; force-delete and a matching confirmation release;
  - the libvirt domain naming, now `contracts.LibvirtCreateDomainNames`, with a drift guard against the provider's rule (L5);
  - Proxmox: re-send, deletion of a stamped VM by id, and a hold when none is listed; an unreliable stamp is ambiguous for libvirt and Proxmox (P);
  - ProviderDeleting never writes the marker and keeps an existing one;
  - a changed `providerRef` is refused.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_create_marker_envtest_test.go`: envtest against a real API server. Covers
  - a fresh VM with no stored status is created exactly once and its id recorded (fails with the earlier marker patch);
  - a marker write that loses a resourceVersion race sends no Create;
  - the post-Create record lands on an object whose status was never written.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_create_backoff_test.go`: covers
  - a non-retryable FailedPrecondition and PermissionDenied: CreateRefused, the marker replaced, one event with the answer, and the backoff (Q);
  - the backoff grows from 15 s;
  - the first retry of a hold is 15 s even after an older `Ready=False` (L1);
  - `Ready` is not rewritten and there is no second event;
  - recovery to Ready;
  - other retryable errors keep 5 s.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/describe_notfound_test.go`: absent domain is NotFound (provider and wire), a connection failure is unchanged, the marker matcher. `routing_test.go`: the single-host wire-form test now expects `codes.NotFound` for an absent domain.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/domain_naming_contracts_test.go`: the drift guard. `internal/providers/contracts/libvirt_domain_names_test.go`: the rule.
- `internal/transport/grpc/client_untyped_test.go`: an uncategorized answer keeps its text, code and details (Q). `CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED` marks the mapped error whatever its code; another domain's reason does not.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_rejected_create_message_test.go`: the sanitized rejected-create message (L4).
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_force_delete_consumer_test.go`: covers
  - a refused force-delete of a clustered consumer whose Provider is unavailable: constant condition, one event, no rewrite on retry, and deletion once the provider answers;
  - a refused force-delete after a failed Delete;
  - the allowed cases: same namespace, Provider permission, single-host.
