- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_delete_update_filter_test.go`: status, label and managed-fields updates of a deleting VM pass no reconcile, and send no provider call. Annotation and finalizer changes pass. Force-delete still releases.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_status_messages_test.go`: covers
  - resolver and transport errors kept out of `Ready`, with no rewrite when the error text changes;
  - the transport classification table.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_power_offgraceful_test.go`: `OffGraceful` with observed `Off` sends no Power call and becomes Ready, for vSphere, libvirt and Proxmox Provider types. Also covers the power decision table, including R1, H4 and L3.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_provider_deleting_test.go`: on a deleting Provider,
  - no single-host create, and no clustered placement, with a constant hold and no rewrite on retry;
  - no re-create of a vanished VM;
  - a created VM is still managed;
  - an unsaved create record is still written.

### Docs
- `docs/vm-provider-binding.md`, `docs/cross-namespace-references.md`, `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md`: the force-delete permission for clustered consumers, and the delete reconcile filter.
- `docs/vm-provider-binding.md`: the create marker and the `CreateOutcomeUnknown` runbook.
- `docs/upgrading.md`: breaking-table rows for the force-delete gate and the create marker, plus behavior-change entries for the status messages, the delete reconcile filter, OffGraceful, ProviderDeleting and the create backoff.
- `docs/release-notes/next.md`: the same changes.

### Why
These are the v0.4.0-rc1 review findings on the VirtualMachine controller:
- a lost single-host Create record could orphan a hypervisor VM;
- force-delete let a tenant leave a domain running outside a shared clustered Provider's accounting;
- resolver and transport errors leaked Provider infrastructure details to consumers;
- deleting VMs re-ran their holds on their own status writes, the class of self-triggered loop just fixed for VMClone and VMSnapshot;
- `OffGraceful` drove a permanent per-VM RPC and error loop;
- a VM created on a deleting Provider would keep that Provider's in-use hold (ADR-0010) waiting;
- a Create failing on its host retried every 5 s forever.

The security review of the branch (M1, M2, L1–L4) is folded in. So is the durable create marker that the Provider in-use finalizer counts: an unbound VM holds its Provider only with `status.id`, `placement.pendingHost` or this marker.

### Impact
- [x] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-12 08:41] - Proxmox: owner stamp on Create/Clone, re-bind of a re-sent Create (in-flight safe), owner-checked Delete, CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED and classified Create/Clone errors
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Added
- `internal/providers/proxmox/vm_ownership.go`: Proxmox VMs carry an owner stamp, as vSphere and libvirt VMs already do.
  - **Format:** one strict description (Notes) line, `virtrigaud.owner v1 uid=… namespace=… name=… phase=creating|ready sum=<16 hex>`.
  - **Where it is written:** in the same PVE call that makes the VM (`POST …/qemu` or `…/clone`). `Clone` writes it only when `target_vm` carries a UID.
  - **Phases:** `phase=ready` once every step has succeeded, then read back.
  - **Why the description and not a tag:** both the create and clone endpoints accept it, it needs no charset encoding, and it isn't subject to `user-tag-access`/`registered-tags`.
  - **Tamper evidence:** any non-canonical line that mentions the marker, a repeated stamp, or a checksum mismatch makes the stamp `unreadable`. Two owners make it `multiple`.
  - **Reserved input:** an owner identity outside `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*` is `InvalidSpec`.
  - **Clones:** keep the source's notes but never its stamp. An unstamped clone request always carries an explicit description when the source has one (PVE ignores an empty one and copies the source's).
  - **8 KiB limit:** notes that leave no room for the stamp are truncated and marked, with a warning, instead of dropped.
  - **Keyed sum deferred:** an HMAC keyed with the provider credential was considered and deferred. Credential rotation would invalidate every stamp, so it needs key versioning first. The docs tell operators to restrict `VM.Config.Options` / `VM.Audit`.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go` (`Create`, `Clone`): re-bind. With an owner, the provider searches the whole cluster (`/cluster/resources?type=vm`) and reads the stamp of every QEMU guest with the requested name.
  - **One `ready` match:** returned unchanged (`node:vmid` off the default node).
  - **A `creating` match:** finished and marked ready. An interrupted imported-disk create is removed and rebuilt from its stage only when SSH is configured and the stage still exists.
  - **A locked match:** left alone (outcome unknown).
  - **Ambiguity:** an unreadable or multiple same-named stamp, a template carrying the UID, two matches, or a namespace/name mismatch fails closed with `AlreadyExists`.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/inflight.go`: a re-sent `Create`/`Clone` never starts a second VM while PVE is still making the first. During a clone or create, the VM's config is temporary (`lock: clone|create`, no name, no description) and invisible to the owner lookup.
  - **Per-owner lock:** one `Create`/`Clone` per owner UID at a time, rollback included.
  - **In-flight record:** each create/clone task started for an owner (node, VMID, UPID; the VMID alone after a lost answer) is answered outcome-unknown until it is seen to end.
  - **After a restart:** an unnamed guest locked for clone/create, with an unrecorded clone/create task of this provider's PVE user running on its node (or unlistable tasks), holds the lookup. Another user's GUI clone does not.
- `internal/providers/contracts/create_not_performed.go`: `CreateNotPerformedReason` (`CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED`), `ErrCreateNotPerformed`, `MarkCreateNotPerformed` and `IsCreateNotPerformed`: the provider made nothing; the call is safe to retry and to treat as refused.
- `internal/transport/grpc/client.go` (`mapGRPCError`): marks any answer that carries `CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED` in `provider.virtrigaud.io`, whatever its code.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/pveapi/client.go`:
  - new calls: `ListClusterVMs`, `VMIDFree` (`/cluster/nextid?vmid=`), `ListActiveTasks`, `Identity`;
  - `APIError` for non-200 create/clone answers;
  - `WaitForTask` wraps `ErrTaskFailed`.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/pvefake/server.go`: PVE-faithful behaviour:
  - descriptions on create, clone and config get/put; temporary clone/create configs; clone task ids (the source VMID) and task users;
  - per-node VMs, with HTTP 500 "Configuration file … does not exist" for a missing VM; the clone `target` node; down nodes (HTTP 595);
  - `/cluster/resources` (with hidden VMIDs), `/cluster/nextid?vmid=`, active task listing;
  - injectable faults (after-apply, raw body, hook), failing and manual tasks, test helpers;
  - two modes to test both possible PVE behaviours: `SetErrorsInStatusLine` (error message in the reason phrase, `{"data":null}` body) and `SetEmptyResourceNames` (nameless guests listed with an empty name instead of `VM <vmid>`);
  - `SetNodes` (unordered `/nodes`).
- `internal/providers/proxmox/*_test.go`, `internal/providers/contracts/create_not_performed_test.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/client_create_not_performed_test.go`, `internal/resilience/retry_test.go`: tests for every rule and error class above, in both error and name forms.

### Changed
- `internal/providers/proxmox/create_errors.go`, `server.go`, `s3import.go`: `Create`/`Clone` failures are classified for the VM controller.
  - **`InvalidSpec`:** request errors and PVE's JSON 400 (its error text quoted, cut to 512 bytes).
  - **`NotFound`:** `Clone` source gone.
  - **`PermissionDenied`:** PVE's JSON 401/403.
  - **`AlreadyExists`:** a re-bind refusal.
  - **`Unavailable` + `CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED`** when nothing was made. Two scopes:
    - **provider-wide**, the reason alone, counted by the circuit breaker: client, node discovery, `/cluster/nextid`, the cluster list, SSH data plane not configured;
    - **one VM's**, plus `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` so the breaker ignores it: the template, source or same-named stamp read; a 5xx "already exists" for a VMID that another VM has certainly taken; a failed later step whose VM was verifiably this request's (stamp, unlocked, stopped, not marked ready by another call) and was destroyed, with its VMID then free cluster-wide.
  - **`Unavailable` without it:** outcome unknown. A transport error or other 5xx, any other or non-PVE 4xx, an unfollowed task, an unremovable VM, an SSH command that may still run (exit 255, cut off), the in-flight holds.
  - **Wire messages:** carry the category only. The PVE detail goes to the provider log.
  - **Before:** any clone-call error was `InvalidSpec`, a VMID collision was a non-retryable `AlreadyExists`, and a failed `/cluster/nextid` silently used a time-derived VMID.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/pveapi/client.go`, `server.go`: real PVE's HTTP 500 "Configuration file … does not exist" is mapped to `ErrVMNotFound`, like 404.
  - **Gone:** a VM is treated as gone only when its VMID is absent from `/cluster/resources` and free per `/cluster/nextid?vmid=`. A VM that moved to another node gives the same answer.
  - **Affects:** `Describe` (`Exists=false`), `Delete` (success), the create rollback, the owner lookup, `ListVMs` and the `Clone` source.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go` (`ListVMs`): lists from `/cluster/resources?type=vm` within the node selector.
  - Each VM reports `owner_uid` / `owner_stamp_state`.
  - A VM whose config can't be read (e.g. on a down node, listed with status `unknown`) is reported `unreadable`, not skipped.
  - Only a failed cluster list fails the call.
  - `ListNodes`' cache expires after a minute, and the node list is sorted, so `FindNode`'s default node no longer depends on `/nodes` order.
- Hardening against PVE behaviour that couldn't be verified without a lab; the code is correct for either form:
  - `internal/providers/proxmox/pveapi/client.go`: PVE's error message is read from the HTTP status line's reason phrase as well as the body (`pveErrorText`, body read through a `LimitReader`). It feeds `vmMissingAnswer`, `VMIDFree` and `APIError` (new `Reason` and `Text()`), and the "already exists" and InvalidSpec texts in `classifySubmitError`.
  - `internal/providers/proxmox/vm_ownership.go`: the restart guard treats a guest listed as `VM <vmid>` (pvestatd's default for a config without a name) like one with an empty name, and confirms from its config. A nameless guest on a down node (status `unknown`) no longer holds every Create.
- Imported-disk rebuild, in-flight records, "already exists" check, retries:
  - `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`, `create_errors.go`, `ssh.go`: a re-sent Create rebuilds an interrupted imported-disk VM only when `pgrep -f` over SSH shows no `qm importdisk <vmid>` still running. A match, or a check that can't run, is outcome-unknown.
  - `internal/providers/proxmox/inflight.go`: in-flight records expire after 2 × the task timeout (`recordedAt`); the owner lookup and the restart guard then decide.
  - `internal/providers/proxmox/create_errors.go`: `vmidTakenByAnother` reads the stamp wherever the VM lives (`vmConfigAnywhere`). The 512-byte wire detail is cut at a rune boundary.
  - `internal/resilience/retry.go`: `IsRetryable` uses `errors.As`, so a marked or wrapped `ProviderError` keeps its retryability.
- `docs/vm-ownership.md`, `docs/upgrading.md`:
  - give each Proxmox Provider its own PVE API token;
  - the delete name rule is exact and applies only to owner-carrying deletes. The adoption controller's `sanitizeVMName` isn't reachable from a provider, so a sanitized adopted name doesn't match.

### Security
- `internal/providers/proxmox/vm_ownership.go`, `server.go` (`Delete`): when `DeleteRequest.owner` carries a UID, Delete never stops or destroys any of these; it answers `NotFound`:
  - a VM stamped with another owner (a reused VMID);
  - a template;
  - an unstamped VM whose PVE name isn't the owner's name (a reused VMID, or an adopted VM with another name).

  An unreadable or multiple stamp holds the delete (`FailedPrecondition`). Without an owner the delete is unchanged except for the cluster-wide gone check. Today the manager sends the owner on clustered deletes only.

### Why
Proxmox picks a new VMID on every Create and doesn't keep names unique. A Create re-sent after an unknown outcome made a duplicate VM (also while PVE was still cloning the first one), a VM couldn't be found by its VirtualMachine, adoption could take a VM managed through another Provider object, any clone-call failure was reported as an invalid spec, and a VM on another node was reported gone. With owner stamps, in-flight tracking and the `CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED` contract, the VM controller can treat Proxmox like vSphere and libvirt.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

  - injectable faults (after-apply, raw body, hook), failing and manual tasks, test helpers;
  - two modes to test both possible PVE behaviours: `ErrorsInStatusLine` (error message in the reason phrase, `{"data":null}` body) and `SetEmptyResourceNames` (nameless guests listed with an empty name instead of `VM <vmid>`);
  - `SetNodes` (unordered `/nodes`).
- `internal/providers/proxmox/*_test.go`, `internal/providers/contracts/create_not_performed_test.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/client_create_not_performed_test.go`, `internal/resilience/retry_test.go`: tests for every rule and error class above, in both error and name forms.

### Changed
- `internal/providers/proxmox/create_errors.go`, `server.go`, `s3import.go`: `Create`/`Clone` failures are classified for the VM controller.
  - **`InvalidSpec`:** request errors and PVE's JSON 400 (its error text quoted, cut to 512 bytes).
  - **`NotFound`:** `Clone` source gone.
  - **`PermissionDenied`:** PVE's JSON 401/403.
  - **`AlreadyExists`:** a re-bind refusal.
  - **`Unavailable` + `CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED`** when nothing was made. Two scopes:
    - **provider-wide**, the reason alone, counted by the circuit breaker: client, node discovery, `/cluster/nextid`, the cluster list, SSH data plane not configured;
    - **one VM's**, plus `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` so the breaker ignores it: the template, source or same-named stamp read; a 5xx "already exists" for a VMID that another VM has certainly taken; a failed later step whose VM was verifiably this request's (stamp, unlocked, stopped, not marked ready by another call) and was destroyed, with its VMID then free cluster-wide.
  - **`Unavailable` without it:** outcome unknown. A transport error or other 5xx, any other or non-PVE 4xx, an unfollowed task, an unremovable VM, an SSH command that may still run (exit 255, cut off), the in-flight holds.
  - **Wire messages:** carry the category only. The PVE detail goes to the provider log.
  - **Before:** any clone-call error was `InvalidSpec`, a VMID collision was a non-retryable `AlreadyExists`, and a failed `/cluster/nextid` silently used a time-derived VMID.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/pveapi/client.go`, `server.go`: real PVE's HTTP 500 "Configuration file … does not exist" is mapped to `ErrVMNotFound`, like 404.
  - **Gone:** a VM is treated as gone only when its VMID is absent from `/cluster/resources` and free per `/cluster/nextid?vmid=`. A VM that moved to another node gives the same answer.
  - **Affects:** `Describe` (`Exists=false`), `Delete` (success), the create rollback, the owner lookup, `ListVMs` and the `Clone` source.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go` (`ListVMs`): lists from `/cluster/resources?type=vm` within the node selector.
  - Each VM reports `owner_uid` / `owner_stamp_state`.
  - A VM whose config can't be read (e.g. on a down node, listed with status `unknown`) is reported `unreadable`, not skipped.
  - Only a failed cluster list fails the call.
  - The vCPU count is converted with `countToInt32` (clamped, never wrapped; gosec G115).
  - `ListNodes`' cache expires after a minute, and the node list is sorted, so `FindNode`'s default node no longer depends on `/nodes` order.
- Hardening against PVE behaviour that couldn't be verified without a lab; the code is correct for either form:
  - `internal/providers/proxmox/pveapi/client.go`: PVE's error message is read from the HTTP status line's reason phrase as well as the body (`pveErrorText`, body read through a `LimitReader`). It feeds `vmMissingAnswer`, `VMIDFree` and `APIError` (new `Reason` and `Text()`), and the "already exists" and InvalidSpec texts in `classifySubmitError`.
  - `internal/providers/proxmox/vm_ownership.go`: the restart guard treats a guest listed as `VM <vmid>` (pvestatd's default for a config without a name) like one with an empty name, and confirms from its config. A nameless guest on a down node (status `unknown`) no longer holds every Create.
- Imported-disk rebuild, in-flight records, "already exists" check, retries:
  - `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`, `create_errors.go`, `ssh.go`: a re-sent Create rebuilds an interrupted imported-disk VM only when `pgrep -f` over SSH shows no `qm importdisk <vmid>` still running. A match, or a check that can't run, is outcome-unknown.
  - `internal/providers/proxmox/inflight.go`: in-flight records expire after 2 × the task timeout (`recordedAt`); the owner lookup and the restart guard then decide.
  - `internal/providers/proxmox/create_errors.go`: `vmidTakenByAnother` reads the stamp wherever the VM lives (`vmConfigAnywhere`). The 512-byte wire detail is cut at a rune boundary.
  - `internal/resilience/retry.go`: `IsRetryable` uses `errors.As`, so a marked or wrapped `ProviderError` keeps its retryability.
- `docs/vm-ownership.md`, `docs/upgrading.md`:
  - give each Proxmox Provider its own PVE API token;
  - the delete name rule is exact and applies only to owner-carrying deletes. The adoption controller's `sanitizeVMName` isn't reachable from a provider, so a sanitized adopted name doesn't match.

### Security
- `internal/providers/proxmox/vm_ownership.go`, `server.go` (`Delete`): when `DeleteRequest.owner` carries a UID, Delete never stops or destroys any of these; it answers `NotFound`:
  - a VM stamped with another owner (a reused VMID);
  - a template;
  - an unstamped VM whose PVE name isn't the owner's name (a reused VMID, or an adopted VM with another name).

  An unreadable or multiple stamp holds the delete (`FailedPrecondition`). Without an owner the delete is unchanged except for the cluster-wide gone check. Today the manager sends the owner on clustered deletes only.

### Why
Proxmox picks a new VMID on every Create and doesn't keep names unique. A Create re-sent after an unknown outcome made a duplicate VM (also while PVE was still cloning the first one), a VM couldn't be found by its VirtualMachine, adoption could take a VM managed through another Provider object, any clone-call failure was reported as an invalid spec, and a VM on another node was reported gone. With owner stamps, in-flight tracking and the `CREATE_NOT_PERFORMED` contract, the VM controller can treat Proxmox like vSphere and libvirt.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-12 08:38] - vSphere Create leaves new VMs powered off; imported disks confined to the VM's own namespaced migration disk; post-create steps completed or failed, never skipped
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Security
- `internal/providers/vsphere/disk_guard.go`, `disk_scan.go`, `landing_lock.go` (new), `server.go` (`Create`, `parseCreateRequest`, `Delete`, `ImportDisk`), `nfs.go`, `s3import.go`: the vSphere provider attached any datastore path in `ImageJson.Path` (from the tenant-writable `VirtualMachine.spec.importedDisk.path`) to a new VM as a persistent disk, in place, ignoring `contracts.VMImage.ImportedDisk`. A tenant could name another VM's disk (`[ds] other-vm/other-vm.vmdk`) and read and write it whenever its VM was off, grow it, and delete it with its own VM (`Destroy_Task`). The migration import also landed every disk at `[<ds>] <vm>-migrated`, named after the target VM's name only, and deleted (NFS, S3) or overwrote (pvc) that folder, so a same-named VM in another namespace could reach, overwrite or delete another tenant's landed disk. Now:
  - **Landing names carry the namespace.** ImportDisk (NFS, S3, pvc) lands at `[<ds>] <namespace>_<vm>-migrated/<namespace>_<vm>-migrated.vmdk`, derived from `ImportDiskRequest.target_vm` (which the manager already sends), as libvirt does. The separator is `_`, which no Kubernetes namespace or name can contain, so the name is injective and no VirtualMachine (vSphere names a VM and its home directory after the bare name) can squat a landing folder — e.g. a VM named `ns-a.web-migrated` in another namespace. A landing name longer than vCenter's 80-character entity limit (the import's transient VM carries it) is bounded deterministically: the start of `<namespace>_<vm>`, `__`, 16 hex digits of SHA-256(`<namespace>/<vm>`), `-migrated`. The bare `target_name` no longer decides the location (it must match the VM when set); a request without `target_vm` is refused.
  - **Create attaches a disk in place only when ALL hold** (mirroring `internal/providers/libvirt/imagepath.go`): `ImportedDisk` is set (the manager verified the path as the landing disk of a `VMMigration` in the VM's own namespace that targets this VM); the request names the VM's namespace (`CreateRequest.owner`; refused without one) and the path is exactly that VM's namespaced landing path; and no VM or template with files on the disk's datastore uses the disk. A disk landed under the pre-v0.4.0 bare name is refused with a constant message telling the user to run the migration again; a verified landing path whose disk does not exist is a `FailedPrecondition` ("landing disk not found", constant), not a retryable scan failure.
  - **The in-use check** matches by path (case-insensitively) and by disk UUID (`QueryVirtualDiskUuid` against every backing UUID in each parent chain), so the same disk reached through an NFS export under two datastore names, a vSAN/vVols namespace directory or a `[] /vmfs/volumes/...` backing is still found. It reads the VMs and templates `Datastore.vm` lists for the disk's datastore and for any datastore that is the same storage (same `summary.url` or NFS export). It fails closed (`Unavailable` + `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED`, retried, outside the circuit breaker) when the scan fails, when a VM there has no readable configuration or a disk identifiable by neither path nor UUID, or when the provider's vCenter account lacks `System.Read` on the root folder or the datastore (vCenter hides VMs the account may not see). Concurrent checks share one scan, reused for 2 s and invalidated by the provider's own attaches and imports. That `Datastore.vm` lists every VM with any file on the datastore (a VM homed elsewhere included) is vCenter's documented behaviour; vcsim records only creation-time datastores, so it is emulated in the tests and needs a lab check.
  - **No races between checks and actions.** Work on one landing folder (an in-place attach, an import and its cleanup) is serialised per provider process by a keyed lock, and a failed import re-checks its folder right before deleting it.
  - **Delete** detaches (keeping the file) every disk outside the VM's home directory before `Destroy_Task` (which deletes every attached disk wherever it is), unless it is the VM's own landing disk (namespaced, or the pre-v0.4.0 bare name) or in a same-named directory on another datastore, and no other VM uses it. Ownership compares exact case. With snapshots referencing such a disk the delete is refused (`FailedPrecondition` + `VM_DISK_IN_USE` → `DeleteBlocked`). VMs with only their own disks are deleted as before, without a scan; a VM whose configuration cannot be read is still deleted with `Destroy_Task` alone (logged).
  - Refusals and failures carry constant messages: never the path, another VM's name, or vCenter fault text (logged provider-side). `InvalidArgument` for a path that is not the VM's own verified landing disk; `FailedPrecondition` + `VM_DISK_IN_USE` for a disk another VM uses; `Unavailable` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` when a delete-time disk step fails.
  - A path beside a template without `ImportedDisk` (a `VMImage` with a vSphere template and another provider's `path`) is ignored and the template is cloned.
  - Other tenant-reachable datastore paths were checked: template clones resolve only real templates (`lookupTemplate`); OVA/OVF prepares are confined by ADR-0009; Clone takes the source VM id the manager resolved in the requester's namespace; additional disks are created new in the VM's own directory; Create attaches no ISO/CD-ROM.
  - Not closed here: the keyed lock is per provider process (run one replica per vSphere Provider); a permission that removes access below the root folder ("No access" on one VM folder) is not visible to the privilege check; the provider's shared govmomi `Finder` is not safe for concurrent RPCs (pre-existing).

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go` (`createVirtualMachine`): Create no longer powers on every VM it creates.
  - **Before:** after the template clone it called `PowerOn` unconditionally, whatever the VirtualMachine's `spec.powerState`. A VM created with `powerState: Off` booted until the VirtualMachine controller hard-powered it off.
  - **Now:** the VM is left powered off, as the libvirt and Proxmox providers do. The controller's next reconcile Describes it, sees `Off`, and calls `Power(ON)` only when `spec.powerState` is `On` or empty. `CreateRequest` has no power field; the proto is unchanged.
  - Cloud-init (`guestinfo.userdata`/`metadata`) and `guestinfo.network.*` are written into the config spec at create time, so the guest reads them on its first boot whenever the controller performs it. The provider uses no vSphere customization spec.
  - Unchanged: the `Clone` RPC (VMClone) already cloned with `PowerOn: false`; a create that binds the requester's existing VM does not change its power state; image prepare (OVA/OVF import) produces templates and never powers anything on. `SnapshotRevert` still restores a memory snapshot's running state (as libvirt and Proxmox do; the RPC carries no desired power state), and the VM controller then converges to `spec.powerState`.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go` (`createVirtualMachine`, imported-disk path): the VM reference returned by `CreateVM_Task` was redeclared with `:=` inside the branch, shadowing the outer one. Every post-create step then addressed an empty reference, which vCenter cannot resolve: the VMClass disk growth (`resizeVMDisk`) and the additional-disk attach failed with a logged warning and were skipped. A VM created from an imported (migrated) disk now gets both. The growth is grow-only: a migrated disk smaller than the VMClass `diskDefaults.size` (default `40Gi`) is grown to it, consuming datastore capacity (all at once for a thick disk), and a larger one is left alone. A GPT guest sees its backup header no longer at the end of the disk; `growpart` repairs it.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/post_create.go` (new), `server.go` (`Create`, `createVirtualMachine`, `attachAdditionalDisk`): a failed disk grow or additional-disk attach was only logged and Create returned success; a Create retried after the manager's deadline bound the existing VM without redoing skipped steps. The steps are now idempotent (grow-only; each additional disk recorded in the VM's ExtraConfig by the reconfigure that adds it, `virtrigaud.disk.additional.<N>`) and run on the bind path too; a failure returns `Unavailable` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` (retried, outside the circuit breaker), the VM is kept, and the next Create completes it. VMs created before the `virtrigaud.create.poststeps` marker are bound as they are. Records a clone inherits from its template are cleared. An additional-disk file an earlier attempt created without attaching (`FileAlreadyExists`) is attached on retry once no other VM is shown to use it.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go` (`attachAdditionalDisk`): an additional disk was created at `[<placement datastore>] <vm>/<vm>_N.vmdk`; on the imported-disk path the VM's home is on the imported disk's datastore, and `<vm>/` may not exist or may belong to another VM. It is now created in the VM's own home directory (from `config.files.vmPathName`) as `<vm>-additional-<N>.vmdk`, a name that never collides with a template's `<vm>_N.vmdk` disks.

### Added
- `internal/providers/vsphere/create_power_test.go`: vcsim tests. A template-clone create and an imported-disk create leave the VM `poweredOff` (Describe reports `Off`), with cloud-init already set, and a later `Power(ON)` starts it. A binding retry keeps the VM's power state either way. `Clone` leaves the clone off and the running source on. An imported-disk create grows a smaller disk to the VMClass size, never shrinks a larger one, and attaches additional disks; an additional disk lands in the VM's home directory on the imported disk's datastore.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/disk_guard_test.go`: vcsim tests. A foreign path is refused with or without `ImportedDisk`; the VM's own path without `ImportedDisk`, without an owner namespace, or under the pre-v0.4.0 bare name is refused; a verified own landing disk is attached; team-b's same-named VM can neither attach team-a's landing nor share its landing name, and a VM named like team-a's landing folder does not squat it; landing names over 80 characters are bounded; a missing landing disk is a `FailedPrecondition`; the scan of a disk's datastore finds a VM homed on another datastore; a disk used by another VM, a template, or under a linked-clone delta is refused; the check runs under the landing lock; a failed scan, an unreadable VM on the datastore, or a missing `System.Read` fails closed without leaking vCenter text, while an unreadable VM elsewhere does not block. Disk identity by UUID across datastore aliases and host paths (unit). Delete keeps another VM's disk (with vCenter's delete-every-attached-disk semantics emulated), deletes its own landing disk, keeps an own-named disk another VM uses, keeps a case-variant directory's disk, refuses with snapshots, and returns a constant retryable error on a detach fault. The import landing check and the failed-import cleanup (never deletes a folder in use); the keyed lock and the scan cache.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/post_create_test.go`: vcsim tests. A failed additional-disk attach or disk grow fails the Create (retryable, no vCenter text); the retried Create binds and completes it without duplicating disks; a leftover additional-disk file (`FileAlreadyExists`) is attached on retry; a pre-marker VM is left alone; inherited disk records are cleared.

### Changed
- `docs/upgrading.md`, `docs/release-notes/next.md`, `examples/vmmigration-nfs.yaml`: removed the caveat that a vSphere migration target with `powerOn: false` boots briefly; documented the new create behavior, the grow-only disk growth of migrated VMs, the imported-disk confinement and namespaced landing names (breaking-change row, in-flight migrations), and the `System.Read` requirement.

### Why
`VMMigration.spec.target.powerOn: false` and `VMClone powerOn: false` now set `spec.powerState: Off` on the VM they produce (#371). vSphere Create must never boot a VM whose spec says Off: a copy coming up beside a running source would carry the source's IP address and hostname. A security review found the vSphere provider attached any tenant-supplied datastore path in place, that its migration landing names did not separate namespaces, and that post-create failures were silently swallowed.

### Impact
- [x] Breaking change (vSphere `spec.importedDisk.path` other than the VM's own verified namespaced landing disk is refused; vSphere migrations landed before the upgrade but not yet created must be run again; the vCenter account needs `System.Read` on the root folder)
- [x] Requires cluster rollout (vSphere provider image)
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-12 07:47] - Migration source snapshots: tracked, polled, cleaned up; VMSnapshots bound to their VM and Provider; provider NotFound only for provably missing snapshots; outcome-safe single-host clone retries; no resolver or task text in status
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Fixed
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`, `vmmigration_snapshot_cleanup.go` (new): a `VMMigration` no longer leaves the source snapshot it created untracked on the live source VM.
  - **Deletion:** a failed `SnapshotDelete` or an unresolvable source Provider used to be added to `cleanupErrors`, and the finalizer was released anyway. On libvirt the leftover snapshot metadata later blocks deleting the source VM.
    - The source-snapshot step now runs first. While the snapshot may still exist and a retry can still delete it, the finalizer is kept.
    - The hold shows `SnapshotCleanup=False/SnapshotCleanupPending` with a constant message, and one Warning event when it begins. The cause goes to the manager log only.
    - A repeated hold writes nothing. Retries use the blocked-VM backoff (15 s doubling to 5 min), and the reconcile triggered by the hold's own status write sends no delete.
  - **A provider NotFound** (the snapshot is gone) is a success.
  - **A snapshot nothing can address any more** — its source VM, or its Provider in the migration's own namespace, is gone — is never reported deleted, and its `snapshotID` is kept.
    - Outside deletion the cleanup stays pending.
    - A deletion is released with a `SnapshotLeftOnHypervisor` Warning naming the snapshot.
  - A missing cross-namespace Provider is a `ConsumerNotAllowed` hold.
  - **Escape hatch:** `virtrigaud.io/force-delete: "true"` releases the VMMigration with a `SnapshotLeftOnHypervisor` Warning.
  - **Terminal failure:** `cleanupSnapshotOnTerminalFailure` was unreachable, because the terminal-Failed short-circuit returned first. A migration that failed for good (`migrationTerminallyFailed`) now goes to `handleTerminalFailure`, which deletes the snapshot or holds as above.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_snapshot_task.go` (new): the export no longer starts before the source snapshot task finishes.
  - **Before:** a task-backed `SnapshotCreate` was assumed complete on the next reconcile, and its task reference stayed set for the export.
  - **Polling:** the task is polled through `TaskStatus`, and the migration moves to Exporting only on success, with `status.taskRef` cleared first.
  - **Task failure, unknown task or timeout:** the snapshot is marked `Snapshotting=False/SnapshotFailed`, its id is kept for cleanup, and the migration fails, then retries per its policy.
  - **Bounded wait:** the task is waited for at most `spec.options.timeout`, or 2 h when unset, counted from the create.
  - **Retry naming:** a retry's snapshot name hint and request token carry the attempt (`-r<n>`), so they never collide with a snapshot an earlier attempt left behind (`cleanupPolicy: Never`). The name is cut, deterministically, to fit Proxmox's 40-character snapshot names.
  - **Task error text:** a failed snapshot, export or import task records a constant in the status; the task's text goes to the manager log only.
  - **Reuse:** a snapshot is reused, e.g. by a retry, only once it is confirmed complete. An unconfirmed one is removed and taken again.
  - **Stale reads:** the `SnapshotCreate` is never sent from a stale read (`confirmMigrationSnapshotNotTaken`, a live re-read).
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`: retry timing and status writes.
  - The first retry of a failed migration waits `retryDelay`. Retry n waits `retryDelay × backoffMultiplier^(n-1)` after the failure it retries, capped at 30 min.
  - `transitionToFailed` and the phase writes requeue after 2 s, never at once.
  - `updateStatus` retries conflicts with `retry.RetryOnConflict` on a live re-read, instead of `time.Sleep`.
- `internal/controller/vmsnapshot_controller.go`: VMSnapshot deletion and retention.
  - **Provider cannot be reached:** a deleting VMSnapshot is held with `Ready`/`Deleting=False/ProviderUnavailable`, a constant message and the blocked-VM backoff. `force-delete` releases it with a `SnapshotLeftOnHypervisor` Warning.
  - **Own-namespace Provider gone:** the VMSnapshot is released with a `SnapshotLeftOnHypervisor` Warning, the same rule as the VirtualMachine and VMMigration controllers.
  - **Retention:** a Ready snapshot's retention now applies once its VM is gone or has no provider id. `maxAge` expires it; `deleteOnVMDelete` fires when the VM is gone or being deleted (never while the VM is detached with `orphan-on-delete`), and while the VM still exists the snapshot is deleted through the provider.
  - **VM gone:** a deleting VMSnapshot with a recorded snapshot whose VM is gone is released with a `SnapshotLeftOnHypervisor` Warning, never a Normal "no provider snapshot to delete".
  - **Bound to its VM and Provider (API, additive):** `VMSnapshotStatus.vmUID` and `VMSnapshotStatus.boundProvider` are recorded when the create is issued.
    - A VM re-created under the same name, or a VM that now goes through another Provider, never gets this snapshot's `SnapshotDelete`. On libvirt and Proxmox a snapshot id is a name, so that call could delete another VMSnapshot's snapshot.
    - Such a VMSnapshot is released with a `SnapshotLeftOnHypervisor` Warning, and for retention its VM counts as gone.
    - A legacy snapshot (no `vmUID`) is bound on first reconcile only when that is provable across the two clocks. The VM must predate the VMSnapshot object (API-server timestamps), or predate the manager-written `status.creationTime` by more than a 30 s skew margin. Anything later, the ambiguous band included, is another VM.
    - The manager's readiness check requires these two fields in the installed VMSnapshot CRD, like the other additive security fields. The manager now also gets `vmsnapshots.infra.virtrigaud.io` (RBAC).
  - **Missing VM:** recorded as `Ready=False/VMNotFound` with a constant message, written only on change.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go` (snapshot functions only), `snapshot_notfound.go` (new), `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`, `pveapi/client.go`, `pvefake/server.go`: a snapshot that is not there is now answered `codes.NotFound`, so the manager treats the delete as an idempotent success. Before, a VMMigration or VMSnapshot delete held forever.
  - **vSphere:** no snapshot tree or a snapshot not in it is NotFound, also for `SnapshotRevert`. After any `ManagedObjectNotFound` (which can name the Task, e.g. after a vpxd restart) the VM is re-read: NotFound only if the VM itself is gone or the snapshot left its tree, otherwise Unavailable. `isNotFound` compares a reference's type and value only, not `serverGuid`.
  - **Proxmox:** the VM's ACTUAL node is resolved from `/cluster/resources` before the snapshot is listed or deleted (the provider used its first node, so after an HA move PVE's "Configuration file ... does not exist" was taken for "snapshot gone").
    - NotFound only when the VM is absent cluster-wide, the snapshot is not listed on its node, or PVE answers "snapshot '<name>' does not exist".
    - "Absent cluster-wide" is confirmed with the permission-independent `GET /cluster/nextid?vmid=<id>`, because `/cluster/resources` hides VMs the token may not audit. A VMID in use but not listed is Unavailable, and a likely ACL problem is logged.
    - A bare 404 or any other failure is Unavailable (retried); `DeleteSnapshot` no longer treats a 404 as success.
    - PVE error messages are matched in `pveErrorText(resp)`, which reads the HTTP status line's reason phrase (where real PVE puts them, with a body of `{"data":null}`) and the body. A text that matches nothing stays retryable, never NotFound.
    - pvefake is node-aware, and can answer errors in the status line.
- `internal/controller/vmclone_controller.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/request_sent.go` (new), `client.go`, `internal/providers/contracts/not_performed.go` (new), `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`, `clone.go`: a single-host clone that fails transiently is held (`Pending`, `CloneRetrying`, a constant message, one Warning event, the blocked-VM backoff), not failed for good. It is retried only when nothing was done (`contracts.IsNothingDone`).
  - **The request never reached the provider.** This is proven, failing closed: the client's stats handler reported the RPC's Begin and no OutHeader followed (no connection was made), or the circuit breaker fast-failed (a typed error). Such a failure is marked `ErrRequestNotSent`. With no Begin at all (no stats handler), the outcome is unknown. `NewClient` and the tests share one call-options builder.
  - **The provider answered that it did nothing.** That is Unavailable with `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`, `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` or `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED`.
  - **Outcome unknown fails the clone.** This covers a transport failure after the request was sent (the provider pod killed mid-RPC), a DeadlineExceeded after sending, and a provider Timeout. A single-host Clone carries no request token: a Proxmox retry takes a new VMID and would leave a second VM.
  - **libvirt single host:** retryable failures before the define are now answered Unavailable + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`, where they used to be terminal `codes.Unknown`. A `domstate` failure on an unreachable host is no longer "source VM not found", and a pool read failure is retryable. A define whose outcome is unknown (`errDefineOutcomeUnknown`) stays terminal.
- `internal/controller/hold_watch_envtest_test.go`, `consumergrant_envtest_test.go`, `virtualmachine_placement_capacity_envtest_test.go`, `crossnamespace_envtest_test.go`: fixed a flaky held-clone spec (`:181` saw 2 Clone calls).
  - **Cause:** each spec's manager reconciled objects that other specs left in their namespaces, and resolved them to the spec's counting provider.
  - **Fix:** the spies and resolvers are now scoped to their spec's namespace. Before the fix, 3 of 10 seeded runs failed; after it, 20 of 20 pass.

### Security
- `internal/controller/rpc_failure_detail.go` (new), `vmclone_controller.go`, `vmclone_clustered.go`, `vmclone_source_power.go`, `vmsnapshot_controller.go`, `vmmigration_controller.go`: raw resolver and transport errors no longer reach consumer-readable status and events. Low; information disclosure (ADR-0007 A6, threat 5).
  - **What leaked:** the resolver's error can name the provider's TLS Secret, its Service ClusterIP:port and its runtime phase. It went into `VMClone` status, the `VMSnapshot` create retry and `VMMigration` failure messages.
  - **Now:** a constant `providerResolveFailedDetail` replaces it, with the cause in the manager log. Provider RPC errors go through `rpcFailureDetail`, which renders a gRPC transport failure as a constant and passes any other answer through `sanitizeProviderDetail`.
  - **Wait conditions:** clustered clone waits and GetCapabilities waits keep a constant condition message. The provider's answer goes into a Warning event on the transition.

### Changed
- `docs/upgrading.md`, `docs/release-notes/next.md`, `examples/vmmigration-basic.yaml`: document held VMMigration and VMSnapshot deletes, force-delete, status text, single-host clone retries, snapshot task polling, retry timing and retention.
- `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md`: VirtRigaud never deletes a migration's `nfs` or `s3` staging object, each one a full unencrypted copy of the tenant's disk. Operators must clean them up until a provider RPC exists (tracked separately).

### Why
A deleted or failed migration could leave an untracked snapshot on the live source VM, export a disk whose snapshot was still being taken, or hold a deletion forever. A single-host clone could be duplicated by a retry whose outcome was unknown. Resolver errors in tenant-readable status disclosed infrastructure details to cross-namespace consumers.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-12 07:35] - Adoption never takes templates, image artifacts, VMs another VirtualMachine owns, or VMs stamped outside this cluster; vSphere per-VM operations refuse templates
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note.** Before upgrading, run the two checks in `docs/upgrading.md`: a `VirtualMachine` (adopted or not) whose `status.id` is a vSphere template, and an adopted `VirtualMachine` duplicating one under another Provider object for the same vCenter. Detach each match with `virtrigaud.io/orphan-on-delete: "true"` before deleting it; a plain delete before the upgrade destroys the template or the other VirtualMachine's VM. **Behaviour change:** adoption no longer adopts a VM whose owner stamp names no `VirtualMachine` in this cluster; set `virtrigaud.io/adopt-stamped-vms: "true"` on a single-host Provider to adopt such VMs on purpose.

### Security
- `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go` (`ListVMs`), `list_adoptable.go`: the VMAdoption discovery feed no longer offers shared image state. High; integrity and availability of shared images; affects v0.3.11 and `main` (v0.3.11 has no stamped prepared images, but any template could be adopted).
  - **Before:** `ListVMs` listed every object `VirtualMachineList("*")` found, templates included. With `virtrigaud.io/adopt-vms` set, adoption turned prepared images (ADR-0009 Slice 3) and any other template into a tenant-owned `VirtualMachine`. Deleting it destroyed the template for every consumer; a resize changed it.
  - **Now:** `ListVMs` reads `config.template` and `config.extraConfig` in the same property call. It leaves out:
    - every template, stamped or not;
    - every object carrying a `virtrigaud.image.*` key with a non-empty value, valid or not, template or not (an import in flight, or a failed import left behind);
    - every VM whose owner stamp cannot be read (repeated key in any case, or non-string value);
    - every VM whose configuration cannot be read.
  - **Owner stamp:** `ListVMs` now reports a VM's owner UID in `provider_raw["owner_uid"]` (`contracts.VMInfoOwnerUIDKey`), as the libvirt provider does. The adoption controller already skips a VM whose UID names a live `VirtualMachine`. Before, vSphere reported none, so adoption through one Provider object could take a VM owned by a `VirtualMachine` under another Provider object for the same vCenter, or a VM whose create had not yet recorded `status.id` (the controller's name fallback never matches a vSphere MOID).
  - `ListVMs` has no other caller: the owner-filtered listing is used only for clustered providers, and vSphere does not advertise it. The proto is unchanged.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/vm_artifact_guard.go`, `server.go` (`Delete`, `Power`, `Reconfigure`, `HardwareUpgrade`, `SnapshotCreate`, `SnapshotDelete`, `SnapshotRevert`): per-VM operations refuse templates and image artifacts. Medium; a `VirtualMachine` adopted from a template before this fix (or an unstamped template an operator converted to a VM and back) could still destroy or change it.
  - **Now:** each reads `config.template` and `config.extraConfig` first (`Reconfigure` in its existing property read) and refuses a template or an object with a `virtrigaud.image.*` key (`carriesImageStampKey`, the listing's test) before changing anything: `FailedPrecondition` + `google.rpc.ErrorInfo{Reason: VM_IS_IMAGE_ARTIFACT}` (`contracts.VMIsImageArtifactReason`) and a constant message naming no object or stamp value. An object whose configuration cannot be read is refused with a plain `FailedPrecondition` (fail closed). A full `Clone` is not guarded: cloning from a template never changes it. A linked `Clone` of a source without a snapshot creates a `clone-base-*` snapshot on the source, which changes it; that step now calls `refuseImageArtifact` first (Low).
  - **Create and Clone shed every image key** (`image_artifact.go`: `isImageStampKey`, `clearedImageStampExtraConfig(source)`, `imageStampClearing`; one-line call sites in `server.go`). Medium. Detection matched any `virtrigaud.image.*` key, but `Create` and `Clone` cleared only the seven keys VirtRigaud writes. A template carrying an unknown image key (a newer release's after a rollback, an admin tool's) made every VM created or cloned from it inherit the key, and every per-VM operation on that VM, its delete included, was then refused. `Create` and `Clone` now read the source's `config.extraConfig` and clear every key in the namespace, in the source's spelling, with the one predicate detection uses. A failed read fails the create or clone before anything is made.
  - **Manager:** `internal/transport/grpc/client.go` maps the refusal to a non-retryable `Conflict` marked `contracts.ErrVMIsImageArtifact` (`contracts.IsVMIsImageArtifact`). `FailedPrecondition` never counts toward the circuit breaker. A refused `Delete` takes the existing failed-delete path: the finalizer is kept and the delete retried every 15 s. A dedicated `DeleteBlocked` hold needs a change to `virtualmachine_controller.go`, which is out of scope for this branch (follow-up).
- `internal/providers/vsphere/ova_import.go`, `image_artifact.go` (`legacyImportMarker`): a legacy (identity-less) OVA import was unstamped, so between `ImportVApp` and `MarkAsTemplate` it was a plain VM that `ListVMs` could offer for adoption. Low. Its import spec now carries one image-stamp key, `virtrigaud.image.preparedat` (the import start time). `ListVMs` excludes it and the per-VM guards refuse it from the moment it exists. The key is in `imageStampKeys`, so `Create` and `Clone` clear it on every VM made from the template. Alone it is not a valid image stamp, and a legacy name never reaches the identity path.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go` (`classifyStamps`, `domainStampReport`, `setStampReport`), `shadow.go` (`nativeListVMInfo`), `domain_identity.go` (`domainOwnerUIDs` removed): single-host libvirt adoption failed open on unreadable owner stamps. Low. The single-host `ListVMs` (virsh and go-libvirt) reported only the readable UIDs: a stamp that could not be parsed, repeated an attribute or recorded no UID looked unstamped, and adoption took the domain. Both drivers now classify stamps exactly as a clustered listing does (`classifyStamps`, extracted from `clusteredStampReport`) and report `provider_raw["owner_stamp_state"]` = `unreadable` or `multiple`. The list shadow comparison (`vmListFields`) does not compare either stamp key, so the ADR-0008 D5 soak meters nothing new.
- `internal/controller/vmadoption_controller.go` (`unmanagedProviderVMs`, `AdoptStampedVMsAnnotation`): **behaviour change.** Adoption treated "owner UID not in this cluster" as "deleted". Medium; a second VirtRigaud installation, or a restore, sharing the vCenter or host had its live VMs adopted here. An owner stamp only means something in the cluster that wrote it, so single-host adoption now leaves a VM stamped only with UIDs of no `VirtualMachine` in this cluster alone. It logs the VM and counts it in the Provider's adoption status message, unless the Provider is annotated `virtrigaud.io/adopt-stamped-vms: "true"`. Clustered adoption already never adopted a stamped VM (previous incarnation) and ignores the annotation. This includes re-adopting a VM detached with `orphan-on-delete`, which keeps the deleted `VirtualMachine`'s stamp: that now needs the opt-in. Single-host adoption also skips any VM carrying `owner_stamp_state`; both flows now treat it as set when present, whatever its value (even empty), as they treat the artifact key (`ownerStampUnreliable`).
- `internal/controller/vmadoption_controller.go` (`adoptVM`, `adoptedVMObject`): single-host adoption copied the listing's `provider_raw` verbatim into the adopted `VirtualMachine`'s `status.provider`, including a stale or, with the opt-in, another installation's `owner_uid`. Low. It now records `adoptedProviderRaw`, as the clustered flow does: no `owner_uid`, `owner_stamp_state` or `artifact`.
- `internal/providers/contracts/adoption.go` (`VMInfoArtifactKey`, `ArtifactTemplate`, `ArtifactImage`), `internal/controller/vmadoption_controller.go` (`isArtifact`), `vmadoption_clustered.go` (`skipArtifact`, `adoptedProviderRaw`): defence in depth. Providers do not list templates or image artifacts; one that does must set `provider_raw["artifact"]` (`template` or `image`). Single-host and clustered adoption skip any VM carrying the key, whatever its value, and never copy it into status. A clustered pending binding is never completed onto such a VM. The vSphere (`listExclusionFor`) and Proxmox (`template == 1`) providers keep excluding these objects instead of returning them tagged, because a manager older than the key would adopt a tagged template. `VMInfoOwnerStampStateKey`'s contract now covers single-host providers. The SDK module does not re-export these contracts.

### Fixed
- `internal/controller/vmadoption_controller.go`: single-host adoption checked its 5-minute discovery interval only after calling `ListVMs`, so every Provider update (status writes included) listed every VM of the hypervisor. The check now runs first and requeues for the rest of the interval.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go` (`ListVMs`), `list_adoptable.go` (`listCancelledError`): once its context is cancelled or past its deadline, `ListVMs` stops reading VMs and answers `Canceled`/`DeadlineExceeded`, instead of a warning per remaining VM and a partial listing.

### Added
- `internal/providers/vsphere/list_adoptable_test.go`: a vcsim listing over gRPC through the manager's transport client. An unstamped template, a stamped prepared template, a stamped import in flight, a VM with an invalid image-stamp key and a VM with an ambiguous owner stamp are all absent. An ordinary VM is listed without an owner, and a VirtRigaud-created VM is listed with its owner UID. Plus a table test of `listExclusionFor`, and `TestListVMs_StopsWhenCancelled`.
- `internal/providers/vsphere/vm_artifact_guard_test.go`: over gRPC, `Delete`, `Power`, `Reconfigure` and `SnapshotCreate` of a template and of an image import in flight, and `SnapshotDelete`/`SnapshotRevert` of the import, all come back as a non-retryable `Conflict` marked `VM_IS_IMAGE_ARTIFACT`, with the object unchanged. `HardwareUpgrade` returns the wire refusal, and an ordinary VM is still resized and deleted. Plus a table test of `imageArtifactRefusal`. `TestCreateAndClone_ShedEveryImageStampKey`: VMs created from a stamped identity template and from a template with unknown image keys (in two spellings), and a clone of a VM with unknown image keys, carry no image key and are deleted over gRPC. `TestClearedImageStampExtraConfig_FromSource` and `TestLinkedClone_NeverSnapshotsAnImageArtifact` (a template is refused and left without a snapshot; an ordinary source is still snapshotted and linked-cloned).
- `internal/providers/vsphere/ova_import_test.go` (`TestImagePrepare_LegacyOVAImport_MarkedInFlight`): the legacy import spec carries the marker, the marker alone is not a valid stamp, and a VM created from the template inherits no image key.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/domain_identity_test.go` (`TestDomainStampReport`): unstamped, one owner, the same owner twice, malformed XML, repeated attribute, empty UID, no UID, an owner plus an empty UID, two owners, one UID under two names. `domain_naming_create_test.go`: the virsh/native parity test adds an unreadable stamp, a stamp without a UID and a two-owner stamp. Both drivers emit the same `owner_uid` and `owner_stamp_state`, and the shadow comparison ignores both keys. `testdata/single_host_listvms.golden.json`: the hand-edited two-owner domain now carries `owner_stamp_state: multiple`; the command sequence is unchanged.
- `internal/controller/vmadoption_owner_test.go`: `TestUnmanagedProviderVMs` covers unreadable, multiple, unknown and empty stamp states, artifact values (`template`, `image`, empty, unknown), and stale stamps with and without the opt-in. `TestSingleHostAdoption_RecentDiscoveryDoesNotList` covers the interval check and the foreign-stamp status count; `TestSingleHostAdoption_StatusCarriesNoStampKeys` the stripped `status.provider`. `vmadoption_clustered_test.go`: `TestClusteredAdoption_ArtifactIsNotAdopted` (including a pending binding), `TestClusteredAdoption_StampedVMsOptInDoesNotApply` and `TestAdoptedProviderRaw_StripsStampAndArtifactKeys`.

### Changed
- `docs/vm-ownership.md`: what vSphere adoption is offered, the artifact key, owner stamps scoped to one cluster with the `adopt-stamped-vms` opt-in, and per-VM refusals.
- `docs/upgrading.md`: the pre-upgrade checks now compare every `status.id` (not only adopted ones), strip govc's `VirtualMachine:` prefix, and find adopted duplicates of a VM under another Provider object. New rows for the per-VM refusals, the owner-stamp scope and the stamp-state/artifact skips.
- `docs/libvirt-domain-ownership.md`, `docs/release-notes/next.md`, `examples/vm-adoption-example.yaml`: the same behaviour.
- `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`: comment only; why `ListVMs` keeps skipping templates.

### Why
A tenant adopting a shared prepared image could destroy or alter it for every VM cloned from it. Adoption must offer only ordinary VMs that no live `VirtualMachine` owns, and must not mistake another installation's VMs for orphans. Per-VM operations must never act on image state, whatever the listing offered before.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout (manager, vSphere and libvirt provider images)
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-10-11 21:27] - Deleting a Provider that is still in use waits, with its runtime kept, instead of orphaning its VMs (ADR-0010); every /tmp emptyDir gets a sizeLimit; vSphere provider runtimes run one replica with Recreate
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note.**
> - **Behavior change:** a `Provider` now carries the finalizer `provider.infra.virtrigaud.io/in-use`, added to every existing `Provider` when the manager is rolled. Deleting a `Provider` while any `VirtualMachine` (in its namespace, or a consumer namespace that is bound to it or allowed to use it), `VMSnapshot`, in-flight `VMClone` or `VMMigration` still needs it leaves it `Terminating`, with its runtime running, until they are gone (`DeleteBlocked=True/ProviderInUse`). Delete VMs before their `Provider` or namespace.
> - **Namespace deletion:** Kubernetes deletes the provider runtime's pods with the namespace. A VM whose delete misses the pod's termination window is held (`ProviderUnavailable`), not orphaned; the `Provider` shows `DeleteBlocked=True/ProviderInUseRuntimeNotKept` and the namespace stays `Terminating` until an administrator acts.
> - **Escape hatch:** `virtrigaud.io/force-delete: "true"` on the `Provider` releases it at once, with a `Warning` event `ProviderForceDeleted`; the hypervisor VMs left are unmanaged. The webhook warns (never refuses) when it is set on a `Provider` that is not being deleted.
> - **Rollback / uninstall:** an older manager, or no manager, never removes the finalizer; delete VMs and Providers first, or remove it by hand (`docs/upgrading.md`).
> - **vSphere providers run one replica with `Recreate`:** `spec.runtime.replicas` above 1 is ignored for a vSphere `Provider`, and **the vSphere provider is briefly down during every rollout**, including the manager upgrade.
> - **`/tmp` size limits:** every pod's writable `/tmp` emptyDir now has a `sizeLimit`: vSphere providers `512Gi`, libvirt/Proxmox/other providers `1Gi`, the manager `128Mi`. A pod that writes past it is evicted. vSphere stages OVA downloads and about twice a migrated disk in `/tmp`, so migrating a vSphere disk larger than about 256 GiB needs a larger limit: the Provider annotation `infra.virtrigaud.io/tmp-size-limit`, or `manager.providerTmpSizeLimit` (`--provider-tmp-size-limit`). An administrator can cap the annotation with `manager.providerTmpSizeLimitMax` (`--provider-tmp-size-limit-max`). A limit bounds the pod's `/tmp` but does not reserve node storage: size it to your nodes. The manager upgrade rolls every manager-run provider pod once.

### Fixed
- `internal/controller/provider_controller.go`, `internal/controller/provider_inuse.go`: deleting a `Provider` no longer orphans the hypervisor VMs of the VMs that use it.
  - **Cause:** the `Provider` had no finalizer, and its deletion only removed its runtime. Each of its VMs then took the "Provider not found in the VM's own namespace" delete path, which releases the VM finalizer without a provider `Delete`: the hypervisor VM kept running, unmanaged. Deleting the namespace did the same to most of its VMs. VMs in other namespaces were held forever.
  - **Hold:** while anything needs it, a `Provider` being deleted keeps its runtime reconciled (phase `Running`, so the resolver keeps serving it) and shows `DeleteBlocked=True/ProviderInUse`. The message counts the objects per kind and per namespace (at most 10 namespaces, never an object name). One `Warning` event `ProviderDeleteBlocked` is recorded when the hold begins or its reason changes. A repeated hold writes nothing: no capability fetch, no `lastHealthCheck` refresh, no status write unless something changed.
  - **What holds it:**
    - a `VirtualMachine` whose placement Provider it is (`status.boundProvider`, else `spec.providerRef`), until its `VirtualMachine` finalizer is gone, and only if:
      - it is bound, or may have something on the hypervisor (`status.id`, `status.placement.pendingHost`, or a `Provisioning` condition with reason `CreateRequested`, the new `k8s.ReasonCreateRequested` marker written before a single-host Create). A VM never created (e.g. held before its Create because its `Provider` is being deleted) holds nothing, so the two deletions cannot wait on each other;
      - it is in the `Provider`'s namespace, bound through it, or in a namespace its `spec.consumerNamespaceSelector` allows now (security review M1);
    - a `VMSnapshot` of such a VM with its finalizer;
    - an in-flight `VMClone` of such a VM;
    - a `VMMigration` in flight or being deleted, out of such a VM, or into this `Provider` from its namespace or an allowed one.
  - **Release:** once nothing holds it, the runtime is removed and the finalizer released. Watches on `VirtualMachine`, `VMSnapshot`, `VMClone` and `VMMigration` re-drive only a `Provider` being deleted, and only for a create, a delete, or an update that changes what the object holds. A 2-minute backstop covers a missed event.
  - **Lookups:** through the existing `virtrigaud.io/placement-provider` VM index and a new `virtrigaud.io/provider-in-use` index on `VMSnapshot`, `VMClone` and `VMMigration`. Nothing lists every object.
  - **Runtime not kept:** when the `Provider`'s namespace is being deleted, or it was deleted with foreground cascading deletion, the controller does not touch the runtime. It leaves `status.runtime` as it was and reports `DeleteBlocked=True/ProviderInUseRuntimeNotKept`.
  - **Escape hatch:** `virtrigaud.io/force-delete: "true"` releases the `Provider` at once and records a `Warning` event `ProviderForceDeleted` with the counts. It works even when the in-use check cannot run: the event then says so, and a plain delete is retried instead.
  - **Visibility:** readers of a `Provider`'s status and events see the names of the consumer namespaces holding it (at most 10, never an object name), and only namespaces bound to it or allowed to use it.
  - **Namespace-scoped RBAC:** a manager that may not read Namespaces treats the runtime as keepable instead of failing every reconcile, and logs that once per namespace (security review L5).
  - **Unchanged:** a `Provider` being deleted without the finalizer (deleted before the upgrade) only has its runtime removed, as before. The VM delete path's "Provider not found in the VM's own namespace" release is kept.
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/provider_webhook.go`: `virtrigaud.io/force-delete: "true"` on a `Provider` that is not being deleted gets an admission warning (security review L3). An update that leaves `spec` unchanged is always admitted. Before, a `Provider` predating the topology×type rule and breaking it could never take or lose a finalizer, so it could never be deleted. The `spec.type` / `spec.topology` immutability checks are unchanged.

### Security
- `internal/controller/provider_controller.go`, `cmd/manager/main.go`, `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/provider_tmp.go`, `charts/virtrigaud/templates/*-deployment.yaml`, `charts/virtrigaud/values.yaml`: every writable `/tmp` emptyDir now has a `sizeLimit`. Before, all were unbounded, so a provider (the component most exposed to hypervisor- and URL-controlled input) could fill its node's ephemeral storage. Low; hardening. A limit bounds the pod's `/tmp` (the pod is evicted past it); it does not reserve node storage, so a node with less free ephemeral storage than the limit can still fill up first. The chart README and values say so (security review M3); ephemeral-storage requests are not added (a 512Gi request would make vSphere pods unschedulable).
  - **Sized from what each component stages:**
    - **vSphere:** stages whole OVA downloads (capped by `VIRTRIGAUD_VSPHERE_IMAGE_MAX_DOWNLOAD_GIB`, default 256 GiB) and, for an S3/PVC import or a converted/multi-extent export, about twice the disk in `/tmp`. Default `512Gi`.
    - **libvirt and Proxmox:** stream disk data over SSH; their `/tmp` holds only KB of SSH material. Default `1Gi`.
    - **Manager:** writes nothing there. Default `128Mi`.
  - **Manager-run provider pods:** per-type default. The manager flag `--provider-tmp-size-limit` (chart `manager.providerTmpSizeLimit`) sets one value for every type. The Provider annotation `infra.virtrigaud.io/tmp-size-limit` (a positive quantity or `none`) overrides both. The Provider webhook refuses an invalid annotation value, but only when it is set or changed, so it never blocks a finalizer update. The manager refuses an invalid flag at startup. The memory-backed libvirt SSH-key tmpfs keeps its 4Mi.
  - **Administrator ceiling** (security review L1): `--provider-tmp-size-limit-max` (chart `manager.providerTmpSizeLimitMax`; empty = none). With it set, an annotation above it, or `none`, is clamped to it with one `TmpSizeLimitClamped` Warning event on the Provider per annotation value, and the flag and per-type defaults are capped at it. The manager refuses `none` or an invalid value as a ceiling.
  - **Chart:**
    - `manager.tmpSizeLimit` and `providers.<name>.tmpSizeLimit` (a quantity, or empty or `none` for no limit);
    - helpers (`virtrigaud.tmpSizeLimitValue`, `virtrigaud.tmpEmptyDir`) that fail the render on an invalid value (security review L4: `none` used to render an invalid `sizeLimit: "none"`) and stay nil-safe, so `--reuse-values` from an older chart still renders a valid emptyDir;
    - `hack/verify-tmp-sizelimit-render.sh` (`make verify-tmp-sizelimit-render`, wired into CI next to the NetworkPolicy render check) asserts the defaults, the overrides, the ceiling flag, empty and `none` values, invalid values failing the render, and `--reuse-values` from v0.3.11.
  - **Upgrade:** the new pod template rolls every manager-run provider pod once. A clustered libvirt provider (`Recreate`) is briefly down.

### Added
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/provider_types.go`: `ProviderInUseFinalizer`, `ProviderTmpSizeLimitAnnotation`, `ProviderTmpSizeLimitNone` (Go constants; no CRD schema change). `provider_tmp.go`: `ParseProviderTmpSizeLimit`.
- `internal/k8s/conditions.go`: `ReasonCreateRequested` (the pre-Create marker the VirtualMachine controller writes; this branch only reads it).
- `internal/controller/provider_tmp.go`: the `/tmp` limit resolution, `ParseProviderTmpSizeLimitMax`, the `TmpSizeLimitClamped` event.
- `internal/controller/provider_tmp_test.go`, `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/provider_webhook_test.go`: per-type defaults, precedence (annotation > flag > default), `none`, invalid values ignored, the SSH-key tmpfs untouched, the ceiling (clamp, `none`, capped defaults, one event), webhook validation of the annotation, and the force-delete warning.
- `docs/adr/0010-provider-in-use-finalizer.md`: ADR-0010 (Accepted, maintainer decision 2026-10-01), with alternatives (validating webhook, docs only, runtime outside the tenant namespace, timeout) and the namespace-deletion limit. Indexed in `docs/adr/README.md`.
- `internal/controller/provider_inuse_test.go`, `internal/controller/provider_inuse_envtest_test.go`:
  - unit tests: what holds a Provider, case by case; only bound or allowed namespaces hold it (unallowed VM, snapshot and migration do not); an unbound VM holds only with an id, a pending host or the CreateRequested marker; a forbidden Namespace read still holds, logged once; hold and release; a repeated hold writes nothing; the cross-namespace consumer; force-delete; namespace deletion and foreground cascade; the legacy path; message bounds; watches and predicate;
  - envtest specs, in a real manager: upgrade adds the finalizer; hold with the runtime kept, released through the watch; the cross-namespace consumer; simulated namespace-deletion ordering; force-delete with its event.
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/provider_webhook_test.go`: a metadata-only update of a legacy invalid Provider is admitted; a spec change on it is still refused.

### Changed
- `internal/controller/provider_controller.go` (`providerRunsSingleReplica`), `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/provider_types.go` (`spec.runtime.replicas` doc; CRD description regenerated), `charts/virtrigaud/templates/provider-vsphere-deployment.yaml`: a vSphere `Provider`'s runtime now always runs one replica with the `Recreate` strategy, like a clustered `Provider`.
  - **Why:** the vSphere provider serializes migration landing work with a per-process lock. With `spec.runtime.replicas` > 1 (allowed up to 10), or with the old and new pods overlapping during a `RollingUpdate`, two processes could race on the same landing folder.
  - **Behaviour:** a larger `spec.runtime.replicas` is ignored and logged, as on the clustered path; it is not refused at admission. The chart's opt-in vSphere Deployment renders `replicas: 1` with `strategy: Recreate`, and `providers.vsphere.replicaCount` > 1 fails the render (checked in `hack/verify-tmp-sizelimit-render.sh`).
  - **Cost:** the vSphere provider is briefly down on every rollout.
  - **Tests:** `provider_clustered_deployment_test.go`.
- `internal/controller/provider_controller.go`: the runtime part of the reconcile is split out (`reconcileRuntimeStatus`, `writeProviderStatus`) so a live and a held Provider share it. Added RBAC markers (`vmsnapshots`/`vmclones`/`vmmigrations` and `namespaces`: get/list/watch). The manager already had these verbs and `providers/finalizers: update`, so the generated role does not change.
- `internal/controller/provider_controller_test.go`: the envtest spec asserts the finalizer and drops it on cleanup.
- `docs/upgrading.md` (breaking-change row, `/tmp` limits row, vSphere single-replica row, rollback caveat), `docs/vm-provider-binding.md` (new "Deleting a Provider" section), `docs/release-notes/next.md`, `charts/virtrigaud/README.md` ("/tmp size limits", the new values, uninstall order).

### Why
A `Provider` deleted while in use, directly or with its namespace, left every hypervisor VM it managed running with nothing tracking it, an audit finding in regulated environments. The maintainer chose an in-use finalizer (Option A) over an admission webhook or documentation only. Unbounded `/tmp` emptyDirs let one pod exhaust a node's ephemeral storage; the limits are sized so that no supported import breaks at the defaults.

### Impact
- [x] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Security

Clears the Go standard-library advisories fixed in go1.26.9 that `govulncheck` traced in `net/http`, `crypto/tls`, `net/textproto` and `html/template` (GO-2026-6599, 6600, 6605, 6607, 6608 among them).
