- `internal/providers/contracts`: `VMInfo.HostID`/`OwnerNamespace`/`OwnerName`, `VMList{VMs, UnreachableHostIDs}`, `TransferOwnerRequest`, the optional `OwnerTransferrer` interface, `Capabilities.SupportsRoutedAdoption`, `VMInfoUUIDKey`, `VMInfoOwnerStampStateKey`.
- `sdk/provider/client`: `ListVMsResponse` (keeps `unreachable_host_ids`) and `TransferOwner`; `sdk/provider/capabilities`: `CapabilityRoutedAdoption`.
- Tests: `listvms_singlehost_test.go` + golden (9 single-host scenarios through the gRPC Server); `routed_list_test.go` (3 hosts with 1 unreachable, same name on two hosts, failing, hung and over-cap hosts, per-host deadline, concurrency bound, caller-deadline budget, rotation, caller gone, breaker untouched over a real gRPC hop, per-host shadow on the same lease, stamps of both definitions, capabilities); `routed_transfer_owner_test.go` (unstamped and stale domains stamped — then routed `Describe` and `Power` pass the owner check —, live, two, unreadable and persistent-only stamps refused, replaced domain, invalid identities, id-like names, idempotent retry, a stamp that did not take, routed error classes, per-host lock); `vmadoption_clustered_test.go` (adopts by (host, id) and records the binding and size, never takes a live VM's domain or a previous incarnation, cross-host duplicates, shared endpoints, single-host-managed names, unreliable stamps, unreachable host is unknown not empty, lost binding completed, binding survives a concurrent writer / deferred for a VM going away, consumer grant, refused transfer removes the created VM, foreign host, capability gate, uncached liveness proof); provider Deployment replicas/strategy; transport (incl. a > 4 MiB answer) and SDK mapping tests.

### Changed
- `internal/providers/contracts/provider.go`: `Provider.ListVMs` returns `VMList` (the compiler finds every consumer; the adoption controller is the only one).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`, `server.go`: `ListVMs` dispatches on topology; the listing core (`listVMsOn`) is shared, unchanged for single-host (its clustered options are off). The clustered provider advertises `supports_routed_adoption`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/shadow.go`: the list shadow compares on (host id, VM id) (`listJoinKey`) and runs on the virsh list's own connection; for single-host (no host id, nil connection) the join and connection are as before.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/sshclient.go`: a command run over the persistent SSH client keeps at most 64 MiB of stdout; a larger stdout fails the command (as a command failure, not a transport one) instead of being parsed truncated. stderr never fails a command: its first 64 KiB and last 960 KiB are kept and the middle is dropped and marked, so wget's progress dots on a large image download (about 156 KB per 100 MiB, which an earlier revision of this branch turned into a failed download above ~670 MB) stay a success. Bulk data is streamed elsewhere and unaffected.
- `internal/transport/grpc/client.go`: maps `host_id`, the owner fields, `unreachable_host_ids`, `supports_routed_adoption` and `TransferOwner`; accepts a `ListVMs` answer of up to 64 MiB.
- `internal/controller/vmadoption_controller.go`, `cmd/manager/main.go`: the clustered refusal is replaced by the clustered adoption flow; `RemoteResolver` is the `ProviderResolver` interface; the manager wires an uncached `APIReader`; the adopted VM object is built by one helper shared with single-host (unchanged spec); RBAC marker `hosts: get;list;watch` (already granted to the manager).
- Docs: `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md` (listing and adoption), ADR-0007 (status, A5 status line, slice 4 amendment, A6 *Slice 4 coordination*), `docs/upgrading.md`, `docs/release-notes/next.md`, `docs/libvirt-domain-ownership.md`, `docs/vm-provider-binding.md`, `docs/cross-namespace-references.md`, `docs/libvirt-shadow-reads.md`, `examples/vm-adoption-example.yaml`.

### Security
- Adoption never takes over a domain stamped with the UID of a VirtualMachine that still exists (any namespace, any Provider object), and until A6.4 takes no stamped domain at all: a previous incarnation (orphaned or restored) is left for the A6 runbook. `TransferOwner` enforces the stamp check on the host; before any transfer that names a replaceable owner the manager proves it gone with an uncached read.
- A clustered VM is identified by (host id, VM id), never by name alone (ADR-0007 D1). Brownfield duplicates across hosts are not adopted, and nothing new is adopted while a host is unknown, so a stale copy's delete cannot remove a running VM's shared disk. Residual gaps: disk paths are compared as raw strings, and only file-backed disks are listed. Follow-up: a clustered `Delete`'s in-use scan should fan out across hosts, as A6.1's R3 does for `Create`.
- The check-and-set holds within one provider process: one replica with `Recreate` is enforced for clustered Providers, and adoption refuses a Host endpoint another Host object or a single-host Provider names (fail closed when they cannot be listed; aliases of one host under two names are not recognized).
- The consumer grant is checked before a domain is handed to an existing adopted VirtualMachine; a host id that is not a `Host` of the Provider, or one being deleted, is never adopted from.
- Tenant- and admin-facing messages name hosts by `Host` name only, never an SSH endpoint or path; `TransferOwner` refusals never name the other owner; an adopted VM's status does not carry the previous owner's UID.

### Why
Slices 1–3 routed every per-VM call to the VM's host under an owner check, but a clustered provider could not list its VMs and adoption was refused, because an adopted VM needs its host binding and — with every routed call owner-checked — its domain's owner stamp. Slice 4 implements A3 (a host that cannot be listed is unknown, not empty) and adoption keyed on (host id, VM id), within A6's fail-closed restore policy.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout (manager and clustered libvirt provider; no CRD change; single-host providers are unaffected apart from the SSH output bound)
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-09-28 12:05] - ADR-0007 A6: backup and restore of clustered VMs (Accepted)
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

### Added
- `docs/adr/0007-clustered-orchestrator-provider.md`: A6 is accepted. It replaces the open question on backup and restore of clustered VMs.
  - **The problem.** A restore re-creates a VirtualMachine with a new UID and, by default, no status. Before A6, a restored clustered VM was re-scheduled as new. The host holding its domain refused the create, because the owner stamp names the old UID. The slice 2 rule then excluded that host, and another host created a second domain. On a pool shared across hosts, that create overwrote the original's disk, because the disk-target guard scanned only the create host's domains.
  - **Decided for v0.4.0 (option (c)).** A restored clustered VM fails closed and waits (`RestorePending`), and an administrator re-attaches it with a manual re-stamp runbook. Four guards ship:
    - R1: a restore marker, `infra.virtrigaud.io/placement-uid`, clustered only, which can only hold a VM;
    - R2: a previous incarnation (`VM_PREVIOUS_INCARNATION`) pins the VM to its host instead of excluding the host;
    - R3: a cluster-wide guard against disk overwrites;
    - R4: a pre-schedule uniqueness check over slice 4's cross-host `ListVMs`, not strict when a host is unreachable.
  - **Decided rule.** At most one domain per `<namespace>.<name>` per clustered Provider. After `orphan-on-delete`, re-creating the same name waits until an administrator re-attaches or removes the old domain.
  - **Slices.** A6.1 (R3, R2) and A6.2 (R1, R4) land after slice 4 and before slice 5; A6.3 is the docs. Slice 5 runs six restore checks. After v0.4.0, A6.4 automates the re-attach through an admin-created `VMRestoreBinding`.
  - **Slice 4 coordination.** Adoption on a clustered Provider re-stamps the adopted domain's owner through a compare-and-swap step, and A6.4 reuses that step.
  - **Recorded separately.** The Proxmox restore duplicate is tracked with the parked Proxmox work. Single-host Providers are unchanged.

### Changed
- `docs/adr/0007-clustered-orchestrator-provider.md`: the status paragraph, the A5 rollout table (A6.1–A6.4 around slice 5) and the follow-ups list now include A6.

### Why
Restoring a clustered VM from a backup created a second domain instead of recovering the VM, and could destroy the VM's disk on shared storage. The fail-closed guards and the runbook had to be settled before slice 5 validates the first real clustered VM.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [x] Documentation only


## [2026-09-28 09:27] - ADR-0007 Addendum A slice 3: clustered libvirt routes snapshots, Clone, GetDiskInfo, ExportDisk and task references to the VM's host
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note.** Only `Provider.spec.topology: cluster` (experimental) changes. A clustered libvirt provider now snapshots, clones and exports VMs on their bound host, owner-checked, and advertises exactly that. A clustered `VMClone` creates its target VirtualMachine **before** cloning and lands only on the source VM's host: if that `Host` is gone, cordoned, being deleted, not `Ready` or excluded for the target, the clone waits with `Ready=False` (`SourceHostGone` / `SourceHostCordoned` / `SourceHostNotReady` / `SourceHostExcluded`) and never uses another host. A `VMMigration` from a clustered VM must use the `s3` or `nfs` backend (`pvc` is refused at validation). Single-host providers are unchanged by this slice: their command sequences, responses and errors are pinned by golden files (`single_host_snapshot_clone_disk.golden.json`, `single_host_power_reconfigure.golden.json`), which origin/main reproduces byte for byte, so this slice does not affect the ADR-0008 D5 soak window (the single-host changes #357 and #358 made are theirs; the snapshot/clone golden was regenerated for #358). Roll the manager and the clustered libvirt provider together: an older clustered provider refuses these RPCs as `Unimplemented` (and does not report `supportsRoutedClone`, so the manager fails a clustered clone before creating anything), and an older manager sends no owner, which this provider refuses (`NotFound`). **Security review changes:** a clustered provider serves **full clones only** (linked is refused and not advertised); the VMClone linked-clone gate now **fails closed** for every provider (no capabilities → refused, a failed query → waits); a **libvirt linked clone into another namespace is refused** (`LinkedCloneCrossNamespace`) — vSphere linked clones are unaffected; **clustered hosts need `flock` (util-linux) and `timeout` (coreutils)** for clone and export copies, and VirtRigaud keeps its locks in `/tmp/virtrigaud-locks` (mode `0700`, the SSH user's; a directory another user created first must be removed); a clustered clone writes its disk and UEFI varstore exactly as a single-host clone does since #358 (private directory + `mv -T`, `0640`, `chown -h`, `dd` with `O_NOFOLLOW`/`O_EXCL` for the varstore; never `chmod 777`), and routed snapshots refuse while another VM depends on the disk (`VM_DISK_IN_USE`), as single-host ones do; pool directories should be writable only by root and the SSH user, or sticky (a `WARN` names them); routed errors now carry only the operation and host id (causes are in the provider log); **`Provider.spec.type` is now immutable**; a clustered clone accepts single-disk sources only; a clustered clone must fit in its source host's free capacity (else it waits `Unschedulable`) and is made at the size it was admitted at; a clustered clone that fails for good deletes the target VM it created (only that object, once); a clustered `VMSnapshot` whose name matches a leftover snapshot on the VM fails (`AlreadyExists`) instead of adopting it — delete the leftover or rename; alert on `virtrigaud_provider_host_guard_refusals_total`. Upgrade CRDs with the manager (new VMClone `status.targetUID`).

### Added
- `proto/provider/v1/provider.proto`: additive `owner` on `SnapshotCreateRequest` (6), `SnapshotDeleteRequest` (4), `SnapshotRevertRequest` (4), `ExportDiskRequest` (12) and `GetDiskInfoRequest` (5); `CloneRequest.target_host_id` (9, the landing host) and `CloneRequest.source_owner` (10); the `TaskStatusRequest` comment documents host-encoded task references. vSphere, Proxmox and mock ignore the new fields.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_tasks.go`: host-encoded task references, `host-task/v1/<host id>/<host-local reference>` (the host id is a DNS-1123 `Host` name, so it never contains the `/` that ends it). A clustered `TaskStatus` refuses a reference that is not host-encoded or is malformed (`InvalidArgument`) or that names a host outside its own registry (`NotFound`), and dials nothing for it; a known host is leased and an unreachable one is `HOST_UNAVAILABLE`. Single-host references and `TaskStatus` are unchanged.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routing.go`: `withOwnedDomain` (lease the bound host, owner-check the domain, address it by UUID) for every slice 3 call; a routed `Conflict` maps to `AlreadyExists`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_clustered.go`: the clustered `Clone`. It requires `target_host_id == source_host_id` (`InvalidArgument` otherwise; no cross-host clone, no provider-chosen host), owner-checks the source before reading its definition or disk, requires the target VirtualMachine's identity with its uid and stamps the clone with it (`stampOwnerMetadata`, `domain_identity.go`), refuses a domain of the clone's name that the target does not own (`AlreadyExists`, nothing copied), reports one the target owns as done (idempotent retry), and copies the source's cloud-init seed ISO into a per-clone seed directory.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_export.go`: the clustered `ExportDisk`: `s3` and `nfs` only (the pod-side `pvc` export is refused, as on Proxmox), request refusals before any host is leased, then owner check, an ssh transport check that names the host id and never its endpoint, and the shared s3 / nfs core on the owned domain's own disk.
- `internal/controller/vmclone_clustered.go`: the clustered VMClone flow — landing-host check (gone / not this Provider's / being deleted / cordoned / not Ready → wait, 2 min re-check), target VM created first, target `pendingHost` recorded with a checked `Status().Update` before the Clone RPC, name conflict → host excluded for the target and pending host cleared (A2 amendment) then wait, host-scoped or transient failure → retry on the same host, other failure → Failed with the pending host kept for the finalizer's owner-checked cleanup.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_budget.go`: time budgets and host-command guards for the long routed calls (`Clone`, `SnapshotCreate`, `ExportDisk`) — see Security.
- `proto/provider/v1/provider.proto`: additive `GetCapabilitiesResponse.supports_routed_clone` (field 20: field 19 is #357's `supports_honest_reconfigure`; the branch had used 19 before the rebase and never shipped it), mapped by `contracts.Capabilities` and the transport; the clustered libvirt provider advertises it; the VMClone controller checks it before creating a clustered clone's target VM (`gateRoutedClone`).
- Tests: `snapshot_clone_disk_singlehost_test.go` + golden (51 single-host scenarios through the gRPC Server; captured on unmodified origin/main — 392d79a, then df4ec4f for #358 — and reproduced byte for byte by this branch; the fakes never create or move files outside the test's directories); routed snapshot, clone, disk-info, export and task-reference tests (owner mismatch / unstamped / no owner / unreadable stamp → `NotFound` with no mutating or reading command; forged task references to unknown or attacker-chosen hosts → refused with nothing dialed; bad snapshot ids; cross-host and uid-less clones; target name taken by a foreign domain vs by the target's own earlier clone; seed isolation; `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` / `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` classification; the placeholder is never reached); controller tests for the clustered VMClone (pending host recorded before the RPC, source host gone / foreign / deleting / cordoned / NotReady / Unknown / excluded never falls back, name conflict, retry on the same host, a target pending elsewhere, a source with only a pending host), clustered VMSnapshot (host + owner sent; only-pending-host VM refused) and VMMigration (clustered source: s3/nfs pass, pvc refused); transport round trip of every new field (and none for single-host).

### Changed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`: `SnapshotCreate` / `SnapshotDelete` / `SnapshotRevert` are routed and owner-checked on a clustered provider (a snapshot id this provider could not have created is `InvalidArgument`); `GetDiskInfo` is routed and owner-checked; `Clone` and `ExportDisk` dispatch to their clustered paths; task references returned by any routed call are host-encoded. The single-host cores are shared unchanged (`snapshotCreateOn`, `diskInfoOn`, `exportFlattenToS3`, `exportConvertToNFS`, clone helpers taking the host's connection).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go` (`clusteredCapabilities`): a clustered provider advertises snapshots, memory snapshots, disk export (backends `s3`/`nfs`, relay, `qcow2`, no compression) and routed clones (`supports_routed_clone`); linked clones, disk import and image import stay hidden (D7). Single-host capabilities are unchanged.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`: clustered `GetDiskInfo` reads the disks from the owner-checked domain's own definition (no volume-name lookup) and accepts an explicit disk path only when it is one of that domain's disks; `IsTaskComplete` / `TaskStatus` route host-encoded references; the pod-side `ExportDisk` is `NotSupported` on a clustered provider.
- `internal/transport/grpc/client.go`: sends the owner on routed snapshot, export and disk-info requests, and `source_owner` + `target_host_id` on a routed clone; nothing new for a single-host VM.
- `internal/controller/vmclone_controller.go`: `bindTargetVM` no longer replaces the target's whole `status.placement` (it dropped `pendingHost` / `excludedHosts`): it writes host, pool, time and reason, promotes a pending host that names the landing host, keeps anything else, and sets `Placed=True/Bound`.
- `internal/controller/vmmigration_controller.go`: a `pvc` migration from a clustered source is refused at validation, even if an older clustered provider reported no export backends.
- Docs: `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md` (routing table, task-reference format, clone / snapshot / migration-source flows, capabilities), `docs/libvirt-domain-ownership.md` (clustered clones stamped with their target and given their own seed; single-host clones still share the source's seed), ADR-0007 (status, A5 status line, slice 3 amendment), `docs/release-notes/next.md`.

### Security
Changes from the security review of this slice:
- `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_clustered.go`, `server.go`: **no linked clones on a clustered provider (v0.4.0).** A linked clone's overlay reads its source's disk for its whole life; `Clone` with `linked=true` is `InvalidArgument` before any host is touched, and `supports_linked_clones` is not advertised.
- `internal/controller/vmclone_controller.go`: the linked-clone gate **fails closed** (a provider that does not report capabilities is refused; a failed capability query waits instead of proceeding) and runs only before a clone is issued; a **libvirt linked clone into another namespace is refused** (`LinkedCloneCrossNamespace`) — a #340 grant covers a copy, not ongoing access to the source's disk. vSphere linked clones and libvirt full clones are unaffected.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_budget.go`, `clone_clustered.go`, `routed_export.go`, `s3export.go`, `nfs.go`, `server.go`: **a routed call running past the manager's deadline tripped the Provider breaker (DeadlineExceeded), and its retry could start a second `qemu-img convert` on the same target.** Now (a) `Clone`, `SnapshotCreate` and `ExportDisk` run under a budget ending 15 s before the caller's deadline and an overrun is `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` (out of the breaker); (b) the clone copy and the export's qemu-img run as `flock -n -E 75 <lock> timeout --kill-after=10s <budget>s qemu-img ...` through the argv-safe transport, so they are stopped on the host, and a host without `flock`/`timeout` fails with a clear message instead of copying unguarded; (c) the lock makes a retry while an earlier copy runs a retryable "in progress" (`codes.Unavailable` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`) instead of a second copy; the VMClone controller retries it on the same host (`CloneRetrying`). No transport change.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routed_budget.go`: **the locks are separate files in a VirtRigaud-owned lock directory**, `clone-<domain>.lock` / `export-<domain>.lock` in `<staging>/virtrigaud-locks` (mode `0700`, the SSH user's), never the disk file: on an NFS-backed pool `flock` is emulated as a whole-file POSIX lock that conflicts with qemu's image locks, and an export no longer needs write access to the source disk's directory. Every guarded command runs through a fixed `sh -c` guard script (values are positional parameters) that refuses a lock directory that is a symbolic link or not the SSH user's, and a lock or target file that is a symbolic link (`FailedPrecondition`, `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`, nothing copied). Lock names derive only from a domain name this provider makes. A pool (or export staging) directory that a non-root account other than the SSH user can write, without the sticky bit, is warned about once per host connection (#358's `warnIfDiskDirUnsafe`; never refused). Every guard refusal increments `virtrigaud_provider_host_guard_refusals_total{provider_type, reason}` (`internal/obs/metrics/host_guard.go`; reasons `lock_dir_unsafe`, `lock_symlink`, `target_symlink`, `unknown`) and is logged as `ERROR ALERT`. The predictable lock directory is an accepted fail-closed risk; a per-Host configurable staging directory outside `/tmp` is a follow-up.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_clustered.go`, `s3export.go`: **a failed or stopped copy no longer leaves a partial copy of the tenant's disk on the host.** A clustered clone's copy is written in a private directory next to the disk's name (#358's `diskWriteDir`) that is removed whatever happens, so a copy that fails or is stopped never reaches the name; a complete copy whose clone then fails before its domain is defined (or whose rename's answer was lost) is removed under the clone's lock (`flock -w`, so a copy `timeout` just stopped can exit first), and only after the host-wide in-use check finds no domain using it; a lock another attempt still holds, a refused path, a missing tool, an unknown define outcome, a domain using the file, or a failed in-use check leave it. The s3 export's flattened copy (#358's `flattenForExport`, shared by both paths) is created by `mktemp` (exclusive, `0600`) and its removal registered before the flatten. Routed cleanups run under `context.WithoutCancel` bounded by `routedCleanupTimeout`, so the answer still reaches the manager before its deadline. An nfs export writes no host file (a partial object at the migration's own NFS destination is overwritten by the next attempt).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_clustered.go`, `server.go`, `routing.go` (rebase onto #358): **the routed paths keep #358's disk-safety checklist** (`disk_dependents.go`). The routed `SnapshotCreate` / `SnapshotDelete` / `SnapshotRevert` share the single-host cores, which run `refuseIfDiskHasDependents` on the leased host with the owner-checked handle; the routed `Delete` keeps `planDomainDeletion`. The clustered `Clone` refuses linked clones before any host is touched, builds the definition and checks the varstore path (`ensureNVRAMTargetFree`) before any write, copies the disk with `qemu-img convert` under umask `0137` into the private directory — composed with the guard as `flock … timeout … sh -c <umask> … qemu-img convert`, the lock still on its own file — renames it with `mv -f -T` and finalizes it with `finalizeClonedDisk` (`chown -h`, no `chmod`), and copies the varstore with `copyClonedNVRAM` (`dd` `O_NOFOLLOW`/`O_EXCL`, `0600`). Routed wire errors: `VM_DISK_IN_USE` (FailedPrecondition, the manager's Conflict) and `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED` (Unavailable, retried, not counted by the breaker) each with `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`; a guard that could not reach the host is `HOST_UNAVAILABLE`; any other routed failure `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`. The routed wire keeps its sanitized messages; a failure the provider describes for the requester without host output (#357's honest Reconfigure, e.g. "could not grow the VM's disk to 20 GiB") keeps that description after the operation and host (`requesterFacingMessage`). Tests: `routed_disk_safety_test.go` (routed snapshots refused while a linked clone's overlay depends on the disk, and retried when the check cannot run; the clustered clone's write order, modes, `mv -T`, `chown -h`, varstore `dd`, no `chmod`/`cp -f`; symlinked disk or varstore targets refused before any write), `TestRequesterFacingMessage`, and the VMSnapshot controller's handling of both #358 answers on a routed create.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`, `internal/controller/vmsnapshot_controller.go`: **a routed `SnapshotCreate` over its budget is "outcome unknown, retry", not "stopped"** — closing the virsh session does not stop libvirtd's snapshot job, which may still complete (a memory snapshot writing guest RAM). It is answered `Unavailable` + `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`, as is a retry refused by the domain's job lock while that job runs; the routed create is **idempotent per request, not per name**: new additive `SnapshotCreateRequest.request_token` (7) carries the VMSnapshot's uid (a migration's uid for its snapshot), the provider records it at the end of the snapshot's description, and an existing snapshot of the requested name is returned only when it records the same token — any other (a same-named leftover of an earlier VMSnapshot, force-deleted or with a dropped finalizer) is `AlreadyExists` and fails the VMSnapshot with a clear message, never adopted or replaced; other providers ignore the field; and the VMSnapshot controller retries a routed create with a retryable answer (30 s) instead of failing it, so a late snapshot is found and tracked. Single-host snapshot failures are unchanged.
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/provider_types.go`, `provider_webhook.go`: **`Provider.spec.type` is immutable** (CEL `self == oldSelf`, as `spec.topology` since #337, plus the validating webhook): the cross-namespace linked-clone refusal is decided from it, and re-typing a Provider would bypass it.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_clustered.go`: `stripBackingStores` removes only `/domain/devices/disk/backingStore` (no XML namespace), never another tool's `<metadata>`; a clustered clone refuses (`InvalidArgument`) a source with more than one writable medium (`device` disk, lun or floppy, any type; only read-only CD-ROMs are exempt) or a disk with an external data file (`<source><dataStore>`) before copying anything — only the primary disk is re-pointed at the clone's copy, so any other would be shared by source and clone.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routing.go`: **routed wire errors are sanitized.** `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` sent the dial error (including the SSH address) and `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` the raw virsh / qemu-img stderr with host paths into tenant-readable conditions; only the operation and host id cross the wire now, and the cause is logged by the provider. Codes and ErrorInfo reasons are unchanged.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_clustered.go`: the clustered clone is defined from the source's persistent definition (`dumpxml --inactive`) with the source disk's `<backingStore>` chain removed (the clone's disk is a standalone copy).
- Docs: a clone (and so a cross-namespace clone) carries the source's cloud-init user-data and its provisioning secrets (`cross-namespace-targets.md`, `libvirt-domain-ownership.md`); a clustered `nfs` export needs host→NFS egress and relies on AUTH_SYS trust (`clustered-provider-inventory.md`); `upgrading.md` lists the linked-clone changes.

### Added (clustered clone capacity and cleanup)
- `internal/controller/vmclone_capacity.go` (new), `vmclone_clustered.go`, `cmd/manager/main.go`: **a clustered clone is admitted against its source host's committed capacity** before its target's pending host is recorded and before the Clone RPC, under the per-Provider assume lock and cache the VMClone controller now shares with the VirtualMachine controller (so a concurrent create and clone never overbook). It counts at `admittedFootprint` of its pending record — the class named by `spec.target.classRef`, else the source's own size — raised to the balloon ceiling it is provisioned with (memory hot-add from that class, or for a clone of the source's size from the source's recorded `memoryCeilingMiB`, the class's setting only when unrecorded). An admitted clone is assumed until its pending host is visible; the pending host records `pendingResources` and `memoryCeilingMiB` (#356); a refused write drops the assumption. **The size is frozen once admitted:** the Clone RPC's class override is built from the recorded admission (vCPU, memory, memory hot-add; vCPU hot-add from the class), never from the VMClass re-read at RPC time, so a class edited after admission cannot change what is created; a retry of an admitted clone reuses the recorded admission; a class that cannot be read makes the clone wait with a condition instead of being sent without an override. A clone that does not fit is not sent: its target gets `Placed=False/Unschedulable` naming only the clone's size and host, the VMClone stays `Pending` with a backoff of up to 2 minutes, and no other host is tried; a missing pool or an unknown size fails closed. `committedPlacements` became the reader-based `committedPlacementsFrom`, and `placedWithAssumptions` gained a reader-based `placedWithAssumptionsFrom`, for this.
- `internal/controller/vmclone_controller.go`: the clustered bind records the target's `status.currentResources` at the size the Clone RPC sent (the admitted size) and keeps its `status.placement.memoryCeilingMiB` (for a clone of the source's size, the source's ceiling), and clears `pendingResources`, so a clone counts at its admitted size, never at its class floor or a hot-add flag its tenant controls (scheduler review N5).
- `internal/controller/vmclone_clustered.go`, `vmclone_controller.go`: **a clustered clone that fails for good (terminal `Failed`) removes the target VirtualMachine it created** (event `TargetRemoved`); its finalizer runs the owner-checked Delete on the pending host. Only the object the clone created is deleted: new additive VMClone `status.targetUID` records its uid when the clone creates it (the copyable clone-uid annotation is never enough), and a VM under the target name with another uid is never cloned onto, bound or removed. It must also be unbound, not refused by the clone (`TargetConflict`), on a clustered Provider, and in a namespace that still grants the clone; the delete carries uid and resourceVersion preconditions. The decision is made **once** and recorded as the `TargetCleanup` condition (`True/TargetRemoved` or `False/TargetKept` with why). Retrying, `Pending` and blocked-host states never delete. Single-host clones are unchanged. An older VMClone CRD prunes `targetUID`; removal then never runs (fail-safe).
- Tests: `vmclone_capacity_test.go` (fits → sent with its pending size, bound at the cloned size with the source's ceiling; no fit → `Unschedulable`, no RPC, no other host, no committed figures; hot-add clones at their ceiling, recorded or from the class; target class sizing; unknown size waits; an admitted pending clone is not re-checked; a concurrent create and clone on a nearly full host never overbook, either order, with a lagging cache); `vmclone_frozen_size_test.go` (the RPC carries the admitted size; a class edited after admission is frozen out, and the bind records the size sent; an unreadable class waits); `vmclone_target_uid_test.go` (the created target's uid is recorded; a re-created VM with a copied annotation is never deleted; the decision is made once; a replaced target is never cloned onto); `routed_snapshot_token_test.go` (adopted only with the same token; a leftover of another request, no token, or a request without one is `AlreadyExists`; the token is recorded; an invalid token is `InvalidArgument`); `routed_cleanup_test.go` (a disk a domain uses, or whose use cannot be checked, is never removed); `vmclone_failed_target_test.go` (terminal failure removes the target; retryable / host-unavailable / name-conflict keep it; never a VM the clone did not create, another clone's, a bound one, a single-host one, one bound between check and delete, or one in a namespace that revoked the grant).

### Fixed
- Clustered clones no longer share the source's cloud-init seed ISO, so deleting a clone can no longer delete the source's seed (and vice versa). The single-host clone keeps the old behaviour for now (tracked; changing it would restart the D5 soak window).

### Why
Slices 1 and 2 routed `Describe`, `Delete`, `Power` and `Reconfigure`; everything else a clustered VM needs after create was refused. Slice 3 routes the snapshot family, `Clone`, `GetDiskInfo` and `ExportDisk` to the VM's bound host under the same owner check, so a VirtualMachine can never snapshot, clone, read or export another tenant's domain on a shared host, and it applies A2 to clones (pending host first, clone stamped with its target) so a lost answer or a deleted target never leaks a domain.

### Impact
- [x] Breaking change (linked clones: the gate fails closed, and a libvirt linked clone into another namespace is refused; `Provider.spec.type` is immutable; see `docs/upgrading.md`)
- [x] Requires cluster rollout (CRDs, manager and clustered libvirt provider; clustered hosts need `flock` and `timeout`; single-host providers are unaffected)
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-09-28 07:30] - libvirt: deleting a running linked clone deleted its source VM's disk; linked-clone dependency guard; linked clones disabled; VM files created with their final mode; VMSnapshot deletes retried
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note.** libvirt `LinkedClone` is refused in this release (`LinkedCloneUnsupported`): use `FullClone`. A libvirt source VM whose disk a linked clone still uses (in any namespace) can no longer be deleted, reverted or snapshotted until the clone is gone: delete the clones first, and keep the source powered off (starting it sets a `LinkedClonesDependOnDisk` warning). Every VM disk is now created `0640` and `chown -h`'ed to `libvirt-qemu:kvm` (never `chmod`'ed as root): the provider's SSH user must be `root`, in `kvm`, or allowed passwordless `sudo qemu-img info -U` (sudoers: `virtrigaud ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/qemu-img info -U *`, never `qemu-img *`), or the disk checks fail (retryably) and Delete/snapshot operations do not proceed; existing disks keep their mode. Keep pool directories writable only by root and the SSH user (a `WARN` is logged otherwise); a root SSH user is not supported on a pool directory other accounts can write. A symbolic link at a VM disk's name is refused (`Conflict`). Remove `.virtrigaud-export-*`/`.virtrigaud-import-*` leftovers of earlier releases by hand. A `VMSnapshot` whose provider delete fails, or cannot be sent while its VM exists, now keeps its finalizer and is retried; `force-delete` removes it anyway. See `docs/libvirt-clones.md` and `docs/upgrading.md`.

### Security
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`, `domain_disks.go` (new): **pre-existing data-loss bug (released, single-host; also reached by the clustered Delete): deleting a running linked clone ran `sudo rm` on its SOURCE VM's disk.** `domainDiskPaths` scanned `virsh dumpxml` line by line and returned every `<source file=…>`, including the `<backingStore>` libvirt lists for a running disk — for a linked clone, the source's disk. The definition is now read with `encoding/xml` (`parseDomainDisks`) and only top-level `<disk type='file' device='disk'>` sources count (`diskFiles`); backing stores, block-job mirrors, cdrom/floppy media and seeds never do. `domainDiskPaths` (clone source, disk info) uses the same list.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`: Delete reads the definition once (`planDomainDeletion`); a definition it cannot read or parse now fails the delete with a retryable error and leaves the domain intact (it used to undefine the domain and strand its disks). It removes only: the domain's own top-level disk files that are, as named, **regular files — never a symbolic link, nor its target** (`hostDiskKind`, a fixed `sh` test with the path as `$1`, re-checked by `deleteDiskFile` right before `sudo rm -f --`) — directly inside the default pool directory or an allowed image directory (canonicalized on the host); the members of their backing chains that are its **own external-snapshot chain** (`ownChainFiles` / `ownChainMembers`: walking down from the top, the overlays its snapshots added — `<domain>-disk.<snapshot name>` — down to and including the disk it was created with, `<domain>-disk.qcow2` or a blank `<domain>-disk`; nothing below that disk, even a file named like `<domain>-disk.<x>…`; same rules, used by no other domain — never a base image, another VM's disk, or a pre-snapshot disk a linked clone reads); and its own cloud-init seed directory, found structurally (`cloudInitSeedDir`) and kept while another domain references it. Anything else is left in place and logged. Before destroy/undefine it refuses, leaving the domain intact, while another domain uses one of those files as a disk or backing file anywhere in its chain.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`: the single-host orphan cleanup of a VM whose domain is gone only removes `<resolved default-pool dir>/<id>-disk.qcow2`, and only when it exists and no domain uses it (it used to try `/var/lib/libvirt/images/<id>-disk.qcow2`, `<id>.qcow2` and `<id>-disk`).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/disk_dependents.go` (new), `imagepath.go`: dependency guard. `domainRefsOnHost` splits `diskSourcesInUse`'s host scan per domain (every disk chain read once), `diskDependents` counts the OTHER domains using a file, and `refuseIfDiskHasDependents` (any host runner, domain name or UUID) refuses with `diskDependentsError`: gRPC `FailedPrecondition` + `ErrorInfo` `VM_DISK_IN_USE`, naming only the requester's domain and the number of dependents. A running domain whose definition lists every disk's `<backingStore>` has its chain taken from the definition, no image opened (`liveDomainDoc`, `liveChainListed`); a shut-off domain's chain is walked one image at a time (`walkBackingChain`: `sudo -n qemu-img info -U [-f <format its parent names>] --output=json -- <file>`, `qemuImgInfoOnHost`, falling back to the SSH user when sudo itself refuses — not permitted, password required, not installed) — **never `--backing-chain`, which had qemu-img open, as root, whatever backing name each header holds**. A backing file is followed only when its full-backing-filename is an absolute local path to a regular file (`backingKindScript`, fixed `sh -c` test, path as `$1`); a protocol (`nbd:`, `http:`…), `json:` or relative backing, a device, FIFO or directory, an odd format name and a chain deeper than 32 images fail the check closed; a missing file ends the chain. Every image, the disk itself included, must be a regular file before qemu-img opens it (`checkChainFileKind`). A qcow2 external data file is recorded as a reference, never opened by the walk; one not named by an absolute local path fails the check closed. Every sudo'ed call starts `qemu-img info -U` (the adopt-in-place size read gains `-U`), so sudo can be limited to exactly that. Delete only scans when it has files to remove; no cache. The file carries a call-site checklist of every operation that must hold the guard (for the ADR-0007 Slice 3 rebase).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/disk_dependents.go`, `routing.go`, `internal/providers/contracts/errors.go`, `internal/transport/grpc/client.go`: **a guard that cannot run no longer opens the circuit breaker.** One domain whose disk the SSH user cannot read (`0600 libvirt-qemu`, an inactive pool, root-squashed NFS) failed every Delete/Snapshot* on the host, and the single-host wire form (`Unknown`) counted toward the Provider-wide breaker on every 15-second finalizer retry. `guardCheckFailed` now returns `diskCheckFailedError`: retryable, and gRPC `Unavailable` + `ErrorInfo` `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED` (new `contracts.VMDiskCheckFailedReason`; plus `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` when routed), which `isInfraFailure` never counts — but only when the host answered: a host that cannot be reached during the check (`isHostTransportFailure`: the SSH connection or libvirtd failed) returns `guardHostUnreachableError`, a host failure like any other (`HOST_UNAVAILABLE` when routed; a plain, counted `Unavailable` on single-host). `hostCheckFailed` keeps its cause for `errors.As`/`Is` only (`hiddenCauseError`, message unchanged), so a connection lost in the middle of the host scan is still recognized (a routed image confinement that loses its host is `HOST_UNAVAILABLE` too, was `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`). Details stay in the provider log.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`, `provider_virsh.go`: SnapshotCreate (every kind), SnapshotRevert and SnapshotDelete run the guard before the snapshot command: a revert rewrites, an external snapshot delete commits into, and an internal/memory snapshot writes into the file a linked clone reads; a disk-only snapshot would hide the dependency behind a new overlay.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/clone.go`, `server.go`: **libvirt linked clones are disabled.** A linked clone reads its source VM's live, unfrozen disk, so powering the source on while a linked clone of it exists corrupts the clone — a hazard no delete/snapshot guard can catch. `Clone` refuses `Linked=true` with an sdk `InvalidSpec` (gRPC `InvalidArgument`, never counted toward the circuit breaker) before any host command runs ("linked clones are disabled on libvirt in this release: the source disk is not frozen, so the source's writes would corrupt the clone; use FullClone"), and single-host `GetCapabilities` reports `SupportsLinkedClones=false`, so the manager's `gateLinkedClone` fails the `VMClone` with `LinkedCloneUnsupported` before calling `Clone` (`internal/controller/vmclone_controller.go`: the message now names `spec.options.type: FullClone`). Full clones and vSphere linked clones are unchanged; existing libvirt linked clones keep working and stay protected by the guards above. Follow-up: re-enable once the base is frozen at clone time (an external snapshot of the source, or cloning only from an immutable template image).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/disk_mode.go` (new), `clone.go`, `storage.go`, `s3import.go`, `nfs.go`, `conn.go`, `virsh.go`: **no world-writable VM disks, and no root `chown`/`chmod` that follows a swapped-in symlink.** Between creating a VM file and `sudo chown`/`sudo chmod <path>`, anyone able to write the directory could replace it with a symlink and have root chown/chmod the target (e.g. `/etc/shadow`). Every VM disk now gets its final mode when it is **created**: `qemu-img`/`cat` run under `umask 0137` (`withUmask`, a fixed `sh -c 'umask "$1" && shift && exec "$@"'`; `writeVMDiskArgv`) in `createFullCopy`, `createLinkedOverlay`, `DownloadCloudImage`, `convertImageToVolume`, the s3/nfs import converts and the local import copy, and a blank disk is made with `vol-create` (definition on stdin, `runVirshStdin`) carrying `<permissions><mode>0640`. `qemu-img` creates files `0644` at most, so the mode is `0640` (`vmDiskMode`: owner rw, group r — nothing writes a VM disk through the group), not the earlier `0660`/`777`. Ownership goes to the qemu user with `sudo chown -h libvirt-qemu:kvm -- <path>` (`chownToQemu`); every separate `chmod` is gone, and an imported disk adopted in place is only chowned. `warnIfDiskDirUnsafe` logs a `WARN` (never refuses), once per directory and provider process, when a non-root account other than the SSH user can write a directory VM files are created in and it is not sticky. Disks created by an earlier release keep their mode. Follow-up: `0600 libvirt-qemu` with every read through `sudo -n`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/staging.go`, `disk_mode.go`, `clone.go`, `storage.go`, `s3import.go`, `nfs.go`, `conn.go`: **a disk is never written through a symbolic link at its name.** `ensureDiskTargetFree` checked `[ -e ]`, which follows links: a dangling link planted at the target looked free (qemu-img/cat then created its target) and a link to an unused file looked like a stale leftover to overwrite — with a root SSH user, e.g. `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys`. It now refuses a link at the target, dangling or not (`Conflict`; `targetKindScript`, shared with the varstore check). And every disk is written inside a private directory next to its final name (`diskWriteDir`: `mktemp -d`, unpredictable `.virtrigaud-write-*`, `0700`, the SSH user's) and renamed onto the name with `mv -f -T` — rename(2) replaces a link planted there after the check, never follows it — the directory being removed whatever happens: `createFullCopy`, `createLinkedOverlay`, `DownloadCloudImage`, `convertImageToVolume` (convert and resize in the directory), the s3 import (staged object and converted disk, checked there; the predictable pool-dir staging name is gone), the nfs import and the local import copy. A private directory, not a mktemp file: mktemp creates `0600` and qemu-img keeps an existing file's mode. A blank disk is created by libvirt (`vol-create`, which refuses an existing name).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/s3export.go`: **the s3 export's flattened copy is private and always removed.** It was flattened into a predictably named, SSH-umask (typically world-readable) temp next to the source whose removal was armed only after the flatten succeeded, so a failed or interrupted export left a multi-GB copy of the VM's disk behind. `flattenForExport` creates it with mktemp (exclusive, unpredictable, `0600`, the flatten under umask `0177`), arms its removal before the flatten runs, and removes it detached from the request's cancellation with a bound (`removeHostPath`).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/clone.go`: Clone builds the target definition before writing any file and refuses (`Conflict`) a UEFI varstore target that is a symlink or used by any domain (`ensureNVRAMTargetFree`). The varstore copy (`copyClonedNVRAM`) removes a stale unused target (`sudo rm -f --`) and creates it with `sudo dd iflag=nofollow oflag=nofollow conv=excl` (`O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`) under `umask 0177` instead of `sudo cp -f` (which followed symlinks as root) — nothing that appears at the path in between, and no other hard link to a stale file, is written through — `0600` from the start, then `chown -h`.
- `internal/controller/vmsnapshot_controller.go`: **a `VMSnapshot` whose provider `SnapshotDelete` fails keeps its finalizer.** Any failure other than "already gone" used to release it, leaving the snapshot (the guest's RAM, for a memory snapshot) on the hypervisor untracked — and the VM's later undefine failing on its metadata — with a Normal event claiming success. Now: a `VM_DISK_IN_USE` refusal sets `Ready=False`/`Deleting=False` reason `DeleteBlocked`, a `Warning` event when new, and re-checks every minute; any other failure sets reason `ProviderError`, a `Warning` `SnapshotDeleteFailed`, and retries after 15 s doubling to 5 min; only `NotFound` or `virtrigaud.io/force-delete: "true"` releases it, the latter with a `Warning` `SnapshotLeftOnHypervisor` naming the snapshot, VM and Provider (and a manager log line). The Normal `SnapshotDeleted` event is recorded only when the snapshot was deleted, already gone or never existed, and says which. A delete that cannot be sent at all while the VM still exists (`vmRefFor` failed: an ungranted or revoked cross-namespace Provider, a clustered VM with no confirmed host binding, a `providerRef` that no longer names the bound Provider) keeps it too (`retainForUnaddressableSnapshotDelete`: reason `ConsumerNotAllowed`/`Unbound`/`ProviderRefMismatch`/`PlacementTopologyMismatch`, same backoff) — it used to be released. Only a VM that no longer exists or `force-delete` releases it then. Follow-up (not in this change): record the intended snapshot name before the create RPC, after ADR-0007 Slice 3 lands its `request_token`.

### Added
- `internal/providers/contracts/errors.go`: `VMDiskInUseReason` (`VM_DISK_IN_USE`), `VMDiskCheckFailedReason` (`VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED`), `ErrVMDiskInUse` and `IsVMDiskInUse`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routing.go`: a routed (clustered) refusal is `FailedPrecondition` with `VM_DISK_IN_USE` and `VM_OPERATION_FAILED`, a routed check failure `Unavailable` with `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED` and `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` — per-VM failures, never counted toward the Provider circuit breaker.
- `internal/transport/grpc/client.go`: `mapGRPCError` maps `FailedPrecondition` + `VM_DISK_IN_USE` (only) to a `Conflict` wrapping `contracts.ErrVMDiskInUse`; `isInfraFailure` excludes `VM_DISK_CHECK_FAILED`.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`, `internal/k8s/conditions.go`: a Delete refused with `VM_DISK_IN_USE` (`contracts.IsVMDiskInUse` — any other `Conflict` is an ordinary failed delete, 15-second retry) keeps the finalizer, sets `Ready=False` with the new reason `DeleteBlocked` (how many domains depend on the disk, and the way out), records a `Warning` event and re-checks every minute; `force-delete` still wins.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/linked_clone_warning.go` (new), `provider_virsh.go`, `internal/providers/contracts/provider.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`, `internal/k8s/conditions.go`: **power-on warning for the source of an existing linked clone** (never a refusal). After a successful On or Reboot the provider counts the domains depending on the started domain's disks (bounded to 30 s; it never fails the power operation), keeps the count by the domain's UUID (dropped when the domain is deleted; a VM re-created under the same name never inherits it), and Describe reports it in `ProviderRaw["linked_clone_dependents"]`; the VM controller sets the new `LinkedClonesDependOnDisk=True` condition (`Ready` unchanged) with a `Warning` event when it becomes true, removes it on a zero count, and keeps it when no count is reported (provider restart). The message says a linked clone in another namespace holds the source's delete until removed or the source is detached with `orphan-on-delete`.
- Tests: structural parsing of the review's live linked-clone XML; the per-domain scan and dependency count (running and shut-off clones, shared disks, symlinks, fail-closed); a foreign `0600` disk read through `sudo -n` and failing closed without it; a running clone's chain from its XML with its image unreadable; the sudo fallback table; the check-failed wire form and breaker on both paths; single-host and clustered Delete of a source (refused, nothing touched), of its clone (overlay only) and of the source afterwards; an unreadable definition (domain intact); symlinked disks (neither link nor target removed, a path swapped for a symlink after the plan kept); the VM's own snapshot chain removed and a base or a clone-read pre-snapshot disk kept; orphan cleanup (removed, kept as a surviving clone's backing file, absent); snapshot create/revert/delete refused on the source and allowed on the clone and after it is gone; the manager mapping (`IsVMDiskInUse` only for `VM_DISK_IN_USE`) and breaker; `DeleteBlocked` on the VM and the `VMSnapshot`, and a failed `VMSnapshot` delete keeping its finalizer with backoff, `force-delete` and already-gone; the power-on warning (provider and controller); a linked `Clone` refused with no host command run, capabilities without linked clones, `LinkedCloneUnsupported`, full clones unchanged; Create, adopted, blank and cloned disks created `0640` and only `chown -h`'ed; real commands with a sudo shim that swaps in a symlink right before the privileged chown/chmod (the old chown+chmod follow it; the clone disk and varstore paths leave the victim untouched); real `qemu-img`, `cat` and `dd` create `0640`/`0600`; the pool-directory check table and its once-per-directory cache; the varstore copy run with the real commands (a hard-linked stale target leaves the other link untouched, a symlink target is refused); an SSH failure or libvirtd down during the check is a host failure on both paths, a connection lost mid-scan too; the one-image-at-a-time chain walk (a symlinked link, named formats; `nbd`, `http`, `json:`, `file:`, relative, FIFO, device, directory and odd-format backings refused without `qemu-img` seeing the name; a FIFO or device as the disk itself refused; a local data file recorded and not opened, an `nbd:` one failing the check; a loop cut at the limit; a missing file ends the chain; a `json:` backing fails the guard closed); dangling and live links at a clone's disk path refusing the clone before anything is written; real `qemu-img` + `mv` replacing a link planted at the final name without writing its target (the private directory `0700`, next to the name, removed); the s3 export's staging file made by real `mktemp` (`0600`, one per export), removed even after cancellation and by a failed flatten; the own-chain membership table and a look-alike VM's disk kept; the dependents count by UUID and dropped on delete; a `VMSnapshot` whose VM cannot be addressed keeping its finalizer (ungranted Provider, `providerRef` mismatch), released by `force-delete` or a VM that is gone. Test fixtures answer `qemu-img info` per image and refuse `--backing-chain`. The routing/ops fixtures and the clustered fixture now use a scratch pool under the package directory (TestMain), and no test process opens or stats `/var/lib/libvirt` (verified with `strace`).

### Changed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/clone.go`: `createLinkedOverlay`, `createFullCopy`, `finalizeClonedDisk` and `copyClonedNVRAM` are free functions over the host's `*VirshProvider`, so the protections carry over to the ADR-0007 Slice 3 routed clone core. No behavior change.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/routing_test.go`, `power_reconfigure_routing_test.go`: the pinned single-host and clustered Delete call sequences include the guard's reads (`pool-dumpxml default`, `list --all --uuid`) before destroy/undefine, one `dumpxml` instead of two, and `rm -f --`; a replaced domain's clustered Delete stops at the checked UUID's `dumpxml`; the clustered Power sequence gains the read-only `dumpxml` + `list --all --uuid` after the start.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/testdata/single_host_power_reconfigure.golden.json`: **regenerated** (own commit). `power-on`, `power-on-define-fails`, `power-reboot` and `power-reboot-stop-fails` end with the read-only dependents count (`dumpxml vrcallseq-web`, `list --all --uuid`); every other Power and every Reconfigure scenario is unchanged. This restarts the ADR-0008 D5 soak window for Power.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/clone_safety_test.go`, `domain_naming_create_test.go`, `imagepath_test.go`: the pinned clone/create host commands change — disk creation runs as `sh -c <umask script> sh 0137 qemu-img …` into `<pool>/.virtrigaud-write-<random>/<name>` followed by `mv -f -T -- <that> <pool>/<name>`, the NVRAM `dd` as `sh -c <umask script> sh 0177 sudo dd …`, ownership as `sudo chown -h libvirt-qemu:kvm -- <path>`, no `sudo chmod` at all, and a blank disk is `vol-create <pool> /dev/stdin` instead of `vol-create-as`. The Power/Reconfigure golden file is unchanged by rounds 3 and 4; no pinned sequence covers the s3 export (it needs an ssh:// transport).
- `docs/libvirt-clones.md` (new: linked clones disabled and the power-on hazard, the dependency guard and what the requester sees, what Delete removes, disk modes and pool directory permissions, the follow-ups), `docs/README.md`, `docs/upgrading.md` (breaking row for `LinkedClone`, behavior row, SSH-user privileges and the least-privilege sudoers line, the #334 row's shared-disk warning), `docs/release-notes/next.md`, `docs/image-preparation.md` (the chain walk), `docs/adr/0007-clustered-orchestrator-provider.md` (follow-up note).
- `examples/advanced/vm-reconfigure-and-snapshot.yaml`, `examples/vmclone-basic.yaml`: no longer ask libvirt for `LinkedClone`.

### Why
A security review found that deleting a running linked clone deleted its source VM's disk, and that nothing stopped an operation on the source (delete, snapshot revert/delete) from destroying a linked clone's data; it also flagged world-writable VM disks and the root `cp` of the UEFI varstore that followed symlinks. Its second round found that one unreadable disk on a host could open the Provider's circuit breaker, that `VMSnapshot`s were dropped with the snapshot left on the host, and that Delete could follow a symlink, strand disks or leave a VM's own snapshot chain behind. Its third round found that a root `chown`/`chmod` after creating a VM file followed a swapped-in symlink, that `sudo qemu-img info --backing-chain` opened arbitrary backing names as root, that an unreachable host inside the check was not treated as a host failure, and that a `VMSnapshot` whose VM could not be addressed was still dropped. Its fourth found that a symbolic link at a disk's name was followed by the write, and that the s3 export's temporary copy was world-readable and left behind on failure. Powering on a linked clone's source still corrupts the clone and cannot be guarded, so William decided to disable libvirt linked clones in v0.4.0 until the base is frozen, and to warn rather than refuse the power-on.

### Impact
- [x] Breaking change (no API change: libvirt `LinkedClone` is refused; a source VM with linked clones is refused delete/snapshot operations until its clones are deleted; a failed or unaddressable `VMSnapshot` delete keeps the object; the SSH user needs `kvm`, `root` or `sudo qemu-img info -U` to read VM disks; a chain with a non-local backing file fails the disk check)
- [x] Requires cluster rollout (manager and libvirt provider images)
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-09-28 06:47] - Security review of the honest Reconfigure result: failures counted at the larger size, disk first, backoff, honest-reconfigure capability
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note.**
>
> - **Clustered Providers: resizes are held until the provider reports `supportsHonestReconfigure`.** Roll the libvirt provider images promptly after the manager; until then resizes of clustered VMs wait (`Reconfiguring=False/ProviderLacksHonestReconfigure`). Single-host Providers are resized as before (warning logged).
> - **Upgrade the CRDs first**: readiness also requires `Provider` `status.reportedCapabilities.supportsHonestReconfigure`.
> - A failed Reconfigure is retried on a per-VM backoff (5 s doubling to 5 min) instead of every 5 s.

- `proto/provider/v1/provider.proto`: `DescribeResponse.vcpus` (field 7; the vCPUs online, 0 = not reported) and `GetCapabilitiesResponse.supports_honest_reconfigure` (field 19). Additive; bindings regenerated. `contracts.DescribeResponse.VCPUs`, `contracts.Capabilities.SupportsHonestReconfigure`, mapped by `internal/transport/grpc/client.go`. `contracts.ReconfigureResult` / `restart_required` unchanged.
- `sdk/provider/capabilities/capabilities.go`: `CapabilityHonestReconfigure` and `Builder.HonestReconfigure()`.
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/provider_types.go`: `status.reportedCapabilities.supportsHonestReconfigure` (CRD regenerated); `internal/controller/provider_controller.go` surfaces it; `internal/controller/vmcrdfeatures.go` readiness requires it.

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/reconfigure.go`: the disk is grown before any CPU/memory change, so a disk grow a tenant's VMClass forces to fail leaves no CPU/memory grow applied (review H1c). The single-host golden was regenerated in its own commit (disk-first order).
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_reconfigure_result.go`, `virtualmachine_controller.go`: a failed Reconfigure on a clustered Provider records `status.currentResources` = max(recorded, desired) per resource, as for restart-required, because it may have applied part of the change; `Reconfiguring=False/ProviderError` carries `observedGeneration` and is also set when the failure is handled as host-scoped (review H1a). Single-host is untouched (no capacity accounting; #354 rule). `syncMemoryCeiling` raises a recorded ceiling to a higher provider-reported maximum and no longer lowers it after a failure (H1b); `syncRecordedCPU` raises a clustered VM's recorded CPU to the vCPUs `Describe` reports (H1d).
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_reconfigure_result.go`, `virtualmachine_placement_capacity.go`: the failed-Reconfigure re-send is paced by a per-VM backoff, 5 s doubling to 5 min, reusing the placement backoff (`nextWithin`/`remaining`); a spec change is sent at once; success resets it (review H2).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/server.go`, `provider_virsh.go`: a single-host Reconfigure that failed on the VM carries `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` (historical code and message kept) and no longer counts toward the manager's circuit breaker; an unreachable host keeps the plain, counted error (review H2).
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_reconfigure_result.go`, `virtualmachine_controller.go`, `virtualmachine_resize_gate.go`: no resize — grow, shrink, or shrink applied while off — is sent to a clustered Provider that does not report `supportsHonestReconfigure` (review H3). libvirt advertises it; vSphere, Proxmox and mock do not yet.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`: a `Suspended` VM whose `spec.powerState` is `Off` is powered off (destroy); `Unknown` stays fully hands-off (review H4). (`OffGraceful` is held since review L3, entry above.)
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`, `shadow.go`: `Describe` reports `VCPUs` (dominfo `CPU(s)` / live `<vcpu current>`).

### Changed

Security review of the honest-Reconfigure change: a tenant could force a failure after an admitted grow (a huge VMClass disk size), revert the spec, and leave the domain at the grown size while it was counted at the old one; a failing resize was retried every 5 s and single-host failures tripped the breaker; an older provider's reply was still trusted; hands-off blocked powering off a suspended VM.

## [2026-09-27 08:55] - Fix: libvirt Reconfigure applies every change or reports it (restart required / error); "Off" means powered off
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note.**
>
> - **libvirt `Reconfigure` no longer reports success for changes it did not apply.** Each CPU/memory/disk change is applied to the running VM and its persistent definition, applied to the definition only and reported as restart-required (`Reconfiguring=True/RestartRequired`: power-cycle the VM — off, then on), or it fails (`Reconfiguring=False/ProviderError`). A memory shrink of a running VM always needs a restart, and lowers the VM's memory maximum (removing memory hot-add headroom).
> - **`status.powerState` can be `Suspended` or `Unknown`** for libvirt VMs (paused, suspended to RAM, unclassifiable; reported as `Off` before). Such a VM is neither powered on/off nor resized (`Ready=False/PowerStateUnmanaged`).
> - **Upgrade the CRDs first, then the manager, then the libvirt providers.** Readiness requires the widened `status.powerState` enum. The single-host Reconfigure golden changed: the ADR-0008 D5 soak window restarts.

### Added
- `proto/provider/v1/provider.proto`: `TaskResponse.restart_required` (field 2; set only by a `Reconfigure` that applied a change to the persistent definition only) and `DescribeResponse.max_memory_mib` (field 6; the most memory the guest can use without host action, 0 = not reported). Additive, backward-compatible; bindings regenerated (`make proto`).
- `internal/providers/contracts/provider.go`: `ReconfigureResult{TaskRef, RestartRequired}` (returned by `Provider.Reconfigure`, whose doc no longer allows a silent no-op) and `DescribeResponse.MaxMemoryMiB`; mapped by `internal/transport/grpc/client.go`.
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/virtualmachine_types.go`: `ObservedPowerState` for `status.powerState` (enum adds `Suspended`, `Unknown`; spec unchanged). CRDs regenerated.
- `internal/k8s/conditions.go`: reasons `RestartRequired` and `PowerStateUnmanaged`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/reconfigure.go`: the new Reconfigure core (see Fixed).
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_reconfigure_result.go`, `internal/controller/virtualmachine_power_observed.go`: manager handling (see Changed).
- `docs/reconfigure-results.md`: the three outcomes, libvirt semantics, the `status.currentResources` invariant, the clustered memory ceiling.

### Fixed
- `internal/providers/libvirt/reconfigure.go`, `provider_virsh.go`: the persistent definition (`dumpxml --inactive`) is read and changed first (`--config`), then the running domain (`--live`) — a live change was never persisted before and was undone at the next power cycle. A failed `setvcpus`/`setmem`/`setmaxmem` (live-refused changes excepted) or a failed offline disk resize is an error (was success, `requiresRestart` logged). The vCPU and memory maximums are raised before a grow beyond them (a stopped non-hot-add VM's grow used to fail silently). A live change the running domain refuses — vCPUs beyond its maximum or not hotpluggable, memory beyond its running balloon maximum, any memory shrink (the balloon is not trusted) — is reported as `RestartRequired`. An offline disk already large enough is not resized. A domain that is paused, `pmsuspended`, shutting down, crashed-but-active or in an unknown state is refused retryably, unchanged (review R1a). Errors name what could not be done, never the virsh command, stderr, a path or an endpoint; the cause stays in the chain (an unreachable host is still `HOST_UNAVAILABLE`; otherwise `VM_OPERATION_FAILED` on the routed path).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`, `shadow.go`: `mapLibvirtPowerState` / `mapNativeDomainState` (kept identical for the ADR-0008 shadow): `running`/`idle` → `On`; `shut off`/`in shutdown`/`crashed` → `Off`; `paused`/`pmsuspended` → `Suspended`; anything else → `Unknown` (every non-running state, even `idle`, was `Off`) (review R1b).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`: new domains on a clustered Provider get `<pm>` with suspend-to-mem and suspend-to-disk disabled; single-host domain XML is byte-identical (review R1c).
- `internal/providers/libvirt/testdata/single_host_power_reconfigure.golden.json`: regenerated deliberately in its own commit; power scenarios identical, Reconfigure scenarios changed or added as listed in that commit.

### Changed
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_controller.go`, `virtualmachine_reconfigure_result.go`: a restart-required result records `status.currentResources` = max(recorded, desired) per resource — a grow is counted at once, a shrink never lowers the counted size while the old size still runs — with `Reconfiguring=True/RestartRequired`; the provider is asked again every 2 minutes (at once after a spec change) until it answers "applied". A failed `Reconfigure` leaves `status.currentResources` untouched and is re-sent even after the spec is reverted, until one succeeds. `lastReconfigureTime` uses the reconciler clock.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_reconfigure_result.go` (`syncMemoryCeiling`): a bound clustered VM without `status.placement.memoryCeilingMiB` gets it recorded once from `Describe`'s `max_memory_mib` (review R2); a recorded ceiling is lowered, never raised, when the provider reports less — after a confirmed memory shrink (review R3) — never while a change is pending a restart or a task runs.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_power_observed.go`, `virtualmachine_controller.go`, `vmadoption_controller.go`: status records the observed power state (an unexpected value becomes `Unknown`); a `Suspended`/`Unknown` VM is neither powered nor reconfigured; adoption adopts a VM that is not powered off as `spec.powerState: On`.
- `internal/controller/vmcrdfeatures.go`: readiness requires the `Suspended`/`Unknown` values of `status.powerState`.
- `internal/providers/libvirt/provider_virsh.go`, `shadow.go`: `Describe` reports `MaxMemoryMiB` (dominfo "Max memory", rounded up).
- `internal/providers/vsphere/server.go`, `internal/providers/proxmox/server.go`, `internal/providers/mock/provider.go`: `restart_required: false` set explicitly.
- `docs/upgrading.md`, `docs/release-notes/next.md`, `docs/adr/0007-clustered-orchestrator-provider.md`, `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md`, `docs/libvirt-shadow-reads.md`, `docs/README.md`: the above; the ADR-0007 follow-up "libvirt Reconfigure must return an error for a change it did not apply" is closed.

### Why
Since #354 the manager records `status.currentResources` only after a provider-confirmed Reconfigure, and the clustered committed-capacity accounting (#355/#356) trusts it, but the libvirt provider confirmed changes it had not applied — a status showing a size the VM did not have, and an under-count of a clustered host. The scheduler security review (R1–R3) added that a paused or PM-suspended guest was reported `Off`, so a shrink deferred until power-off could be recorded while the guest still held its old size.

### Impact
- [x] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-09-25 23:50] - ADR-0007 scheduler accuracy, follow-up: live shrinks wait for power-off, memory hot-add counts at its ceiling, pending size recorded
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note (clustered providers only).**
>
> - **Shrinking a running VM** on a clustered Provider now waits until the VM is powered off. Nothing is sent while it runs; it keeps counting at its current size and gets `Reconfiguring=False/ShrinkPendingPowerOff`. Set `spec.powerState: Off`, wait for `status.currentResources` to show the new size, then set `On` again. VirtRigaud never powers a VM off by itself. A change that shrinks one resource and grows another waits as a whole.
> - **Memory hot-add VMs** count at their balloon ceiling, 4× their memory, existing VMs included. After the upgrade, check the committed gauges against each host's capacity.
> - **A pending create whose VMClass grew** after it was scheduled (larger, or memory hot-add turned on) is not retried: `Placed=False/PendingSizeGrew`, until the VMClass is restored or the VM deleted.
> - **Upgrade the CRDs first**: readiness requires `status.placement.pendingResources` and `status.placement.memoryCeilingMiB`.
>
> Single-host and thin-client Providers are unaffected.

### Added
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/virtualmachine_types.go`: `status.placement.pendingResources` (`PlacementResources`: the CPU and memory a pending clustered create was admitted at) and `status.placement.memoryCeilingMiB` (the balloon ceiling recorded at scheduling; `0` = none). CRDs regenerated.
- `internal/providers/contracts/hotplug.go`: `HotplugResourceMultiplier`, `MaxHotplugVCPUs`, `HotplugCeilingVCPUs`, `HotplugCeilingMemoryMiB` — the hot-add ceiling rule, now shared by the libvirt provider (`internal/providers/libvirt/reconfigure_online.go` delegates to it) and the scheduler.
- `internal/providers/contracts/deadlines.go`: `ReconfigureCallTimeout` (5 min), used by the gRPC client's `Reconfigure` and by the resize assumption TTL.
- `internal/scheduler/assume/assume.go`: `AssumeFor`, an assumption with its own TTL (never below the cache's); `Touch` keeps each entry's TTL.
- `internal/k8s/conditions.go`: reasons `ShrinkPendingPowerOff` and `PendingSizeGrew`.

### Changed
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_resize_gate.go`: on a clustered Provider a shrink of a running VM is deferred (`deferClusteredShrink`: no `Reconfigure`, `Reconfiguring=False/ShrinkPendingPowerOff`, retried with the unschedulable backoff) and applied once the VM is observed powered off (`applyPendingShrinkWhileOff`, run before any power change; `currentResources` recorded only after the provider applied it). A shrink is never refused on capacity. The gate compares footprints with the memory ceiling applied, so a live memory grow within the ceiling needs no check; a missing or foreign HostPool now fails closed (`PlacementError`); the refusal message is built from the VM's own sizes. An admitted resize is assumed for `ReconfigureCallTimeout` plus the status-write bound (N4).
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_placement_capacity.go`: `admittedFootprint`, `pendingFootprint` and the scheduling request count a memory hot-add VM at its ceiling (`memoryCeilingOf`: the recorded ceiling, else the VMClass flag); a pending VM counts at `pendingResources` when recorded. Both critical sections (`scheduleUnderLock`, `checkResizeUnderLock`) release the Provider's lock with `defer`, and every read under the lock is bounded by the lock wait (`lockBoundContext`).
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_clustered.go`, `virtualmachine_controller.go`: `pendingHost` is recorded with `pendingResources` and `memoryCeilingMiB`; `refuseGrownPendingCreate` stops a retry that grew (or gained a ceiling) with `PendingSizeGrew` and keeps the pending host; the bind and a conflict release clear `pendingResources`.
- `internal/controller/vmcrdfeatures.go`: readiness also requires `status.placement.pendingResources` and `status.placement.memoryCeilingMiB`.
- `docs/adr/0007-clustered-orchestrator-provider.md`, `docs/clustered-provider-inventory.md`, `docs/upgrading.md`, `docs/release-notes/next.md`, `docs/vm-provider-binding.md`: the above, the force-delete caveat, and two new follow-ups (the clustered clone bind records no `currentResources` — the Slice 3 branch adds the clone fit check; libvirt `Reconfigure` must return an error for a change it did not apply — tracked separately, affects single-host).

### Why
Security re-review of #355 (N1–N6): a live shrink only deflates the balloon, so recording it let the scheduler hand out capacity the guest could take back; a hot-add VM's balloon ceiling was not counted; a VMClass edited while a create was pending could grow the retried Create; a panic under the assume lock would have held it forever; and a resize assumption could lapse while its `Reconfigure` still ran.

### Impact
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Requires cluster rollout
- [ ] Config change only
- [ ] Documentation only

## [2026-09-25 23:03] - ADR-0007 scheduler accuracy: committed capacity, an assume cache and a resize gate for clustered placement
**Author:** @wrkode (William Rizzo)

> **Operator note (clustered providers only).** The clustered scheduler now subtracts what each host already holds: every VM bound to it, pending on it, or being deleted from it, in any namespace, at its admitted size. A pool that used to accept any number of VMs on one host now refuses the ones that do not fit. Those VMs report `Placed=False/Unschedulable` with their own request only (for example `requested 4 vCPU and 4096 MiB, which exceeds the free capacity of every candidate host`), and are retried after 30 s, 1 min, then every 2 min.
>
> - **Resizes:** a resize-up is sent only if it fits on the VM's host. Otherwise the VM keeps its size and gets `Reconfiguring=False/InsufficientHostCapacity`.
> - **Pending VMs:** `spec.classRef` and `spec.resources` of a VM whose create is pending are immutable (CRD rule; upgrade the CRDs first).
> - **Orphan-on-delete:** a consumer in another namespace can orphan-on-delete a clustered VM only if the Provider carries `infra.virtrigaud.io/allow-consumer-orphan-on-delete: "true"`.
> - **Gauges:** `virtrigaud_host_committed_cpu`/`_memory_mib` are administrator-sensitive. Restrict `/metrics` with the chart's NetworkPolicy or `--metrics-secure`.
> - **No per-tenant quota:** a shared clustered Provider has none yet.
> - **Not counted:** domains VirtRigaud does not manage. Keep room for them with an overcommit ratio below 1 or by cordoning.
>
> Single-host and thin-client Providers are unaffected.

### Added
- `internal/scheduler/assume/assume.go` (new): an in-process assume cache (kube-scheduler's *assume* step).
  - A per-Provider lock (a semaphore with a bounded wait, `LockWithin`) covers reading what is committed, `Schedule` and the assumption. It never covers an API call.
  - An assumption ends when the informer cache shows the VM's record: on the assumed host for a create, at the admitted size for a resize. It also ends when the VM is gone, on `Forget`, or after its TTL. `Touch` keeps a resize alive while its task runs, and `Assume` copies the labels.
  - Correct in process because only the elected leader runs reconcilers.
- `internal/scheduler/resize.go` (new): `CheckResize` admits a resize against the host's free capacity. It checks only the growing resources and excludes the VM's own entries. `ResizeDoesNotFitError` carries a tenant-safe message plus the arithmetic for the log.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_placement_capacity.go` (new): committed-capacity accounting.
  - `committedPlacements` lists the Provider's VirtualMachines in every namespace through a field index (`placement_index.go`). A VM being deleted counts until the VirtualMachine finalizer is gone; after that, even with a foreign finalizer, it no longer counts.
  - Another VM counts at its admitted size (`admittedFootprint`):
    - `status.currentResources` when recorded;
    - its effective size (`effectiveResources`: the VMClass with any `spec.resources` override applied) while its create is pending;
    - otherwise its VMClass size, read only if its namespace may use the class;
    - at least 1 vCPU / 128 MiB.
  - The scheduled VM itself counts at the effective size its Create sends.
  - `scheduleAndAssume` / `placedWithAssumptions`: schedule under the lock and settle the assumptions the snapshot supersedes.
  - `updatePlacementStatus`: status writes bounded to 30 s, made after the lock is released.
  - `unschedulableBackoff`: the per-VM retry backoff, 30 s doubling to 2 min.
  - `committedOnHost` gives one host's sum to the Host controller.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_resize_gate.go` (new): `admitClusteredResize` admits a clustered resize-up under the Provider's lock before `Reconfigure` is sent. The desired size is `effectiveResources` (#354), the same one `needsReconfigure` compares and the Reconfigure sends.
  - A refusal sets `Reconfiguring=False/InsufficientHostCapacity`, leaves the VM at its size and retries with the backoff.
  - An unregistered host fails closed.
  - A shrink always passes.
- `internal/controller/virtualmachine_clustered_orphan.go` (new): `orphanRefusal` holds the orphan-on-delete of a bound consumer VM of a clustered Provider in another namespace unless the Provider allows it. The VM gets `Ready=False/OrphanOnDeleteNotAllowed` and a Warning event, and the finalizer is kept.
- `api/infra.virtrigaud.io/v1beta1/virtualmachine_types.go`: a root CEL rule makes `spec.classRef` and `spec.resources` immutable while `status.placement.pendingHost` is set and `status.id` is empty (no new field). `VMCRDFeatureChecker` requires the rule for readiness.
